CONCLUSION: ColorIndexId = surfaceIndex*4; surfaceIndex = ColorIndexId/4; front value = Surfaces[surfaceIndex].FrontColor, back value = Surfaces[surfaceIndex].BackColor. Front/back is chosen by a visibility test (see TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest) against poly+4/+6. UV-GENERATION FORMULA FOUND (2026-08-11 second follow-up, CORRECTS a wrong claim this entry previously made about g_UseFlatPolyFallback/DAT_00471890): that flag does NOT choose between two texture-lookup styles -- it chooses between the REAL scanline-textured rasterizer (flag==0) and an entirely separate flat/solid 2D polygon-fill FALLBACK (flag!=0, see g_UseFlatPolyFallback's own entry) that never samples a texture at all. Only the flag==0 path reaches TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA/B. In that path, the resolved frame index indexes a 20-byte-stride per-frame descriptor table at g_ActiveBitmapArray[1] (a pointer distinct from the DBA object itself -- see g_ActiveBitmapArray's corrected entry): 4 leading int32 fields F0,F1,F2,F3 (bytes 0-15) plus a 5th field F4 at byte 16 (passed to the rasterizer as param_4, likely a pixel-data pointer/handle). The UV-corner array built for the rasterizer's 4-vertex quad is exactly [V0=(F0,F1), V1=(F2,F1), V2=(F2,F3), V3=(F0,F3)] -- confirmed via decompiled assignment sequence (_DAT_0048a190.._0048a1ac = F0,F1,F2,F1,F2,F3,F0,F3). This is a standard axis-aligned rect-corner mapping (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left in vertex order) IF F0/F1=(left,top) and F2/F3=(right,bottom) of that frame's own texture-space rect. NOT YET TRACED: the builder function that populates g_ActiveBitmapArray[1]'s descriptor table (would settle whether F0-F3 are always a trivial (0,0,width,height) per independently-cropped frame, matching Herculan's existing per-frame DynamixBitmap parsing, or genuine shared-atlas sub-rect coordinates requiring new file/mechanism support) -- a bounded follow-up if resumed, not chased this session per the project's 'don't spend unbounded time on RE before shipping' lesson. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.
entries.source: docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md 2026-08-11, settled 2026-08-11 follow-up, UV formula found 2026-08-11 second follow-up

entries.name: TSGroup_RenderPolys
entries.description: Render-setup wrapper (implicit-this via unaff_EBP, likely a __thiscall stub or inlined caller) for a TSGroup-like runtime object. Reads iVar1+0x10 (Indexes ptr, default &DAT_005d8014 if null), +0x14 (Points ptr -> DAT_005d8894, confirmed by later x6-byte-stride vertex math matching Vec3Short), +0x18 (Surfaces ptr -> DAT_005d88a2, the 'per-surface runtime record array' TSTexture4Poly_Render indexes), +0x1c (Polys ptr, walked as an array of object pointers), +0x22 (ushort, copied to DAT_005d889c, bounds-checked <1000 and used as a memset-zero byte count for a scratch buffer at DAT_005d88a6 -- matches DTSModelTransformer.cs's on-disk 'colorCount' = Surfaces.Length*4 field exactly, both in field order and in the x4 convention), +0x26 (ushort Polys.Length, loop bound). Loop body calls (*(int*)*polyPtr + 0x1c) i.e. each poly's own vtable slot +0x1c -- matches TSShapeInstance_RenderPolys's documented per-poly render dispatch. Field order (Indexes.Length, Points.Length, colorCount, Polys.Length) is an exact match for TSGroup's on-disk chunk layout as already independently implemented in DTSModelTransformer.cs's ReadTSGroup/WriteTSGroup -- strong two-source confirmation this is TSGroup's own render-time field layout, not merely 'some context object'. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSGroup_RenderPolysFromRef
entries.description: Explicit-param_1 (__cdecl) sibling of TSGroup_RenderPolys (FUN_0042349d) -- identical field reads (param_1+0x10/0x14/0x18/0x1c/0x22/0x26) into the same globals, differing only in dispatching the poly walk via FUN_0042362c(param_1,0) instead of an inline loop. Same TSShapeInstance_Render/RenderFromRef-style by-value-vs-by-ref pairing already documented for TSBitmapPart's mechanism. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: g_ActiveSurfaceRecords
entries.description: Global pointer, set from the active TSGroup-like object's own +0x18 field by TSGroup_RenderPolys/RenderPolysFromRef for the duration of one group's poly walk (save/swap/restore pattern, same shape as g_ActiveBitmapArray). Points at a flat int32[] where surface index k occupies 4 consecutive int32 slots (Front, FrontLine, Back, BackLine), matching TSSurfaceEntry's 8-short/16-byte on-disk layout and DTSModelTransformer.cs's colorCount=Surfaces.Length*4 convention. TSTexture4Poly_Render indexes it at byte offset ColorIndexId*4 (front) and ColorIndexId*4+8 (back), which only lands correctly on a single surface's Front/Back slots if ColorIndexId itself equals surfaceIndex*4 -- confirmed true by the independent file-format cross-check. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA
entries.description: One of two near-identical textured-polygon scanline rasterizer variants called by TSTexture4Poly_Render (dispatched by DAT_00471898), only reached via TSTexture4Poly_Render's g_UseFlatPolyFallback==0 path. Genuine span-based rasterizer: per-edge clipping (FUN_0045c318/c5a4/c6f8), perspective-correct-looking fixed-point interpolation of screen position + a fourth interpolant (lighting or a second UV axis, not yet disambiguated), and inner-loop draw calls (FUN_0045bd58 etc.) -- confirms real (if not yet fully decoded) UV-mapped texturing, not flat shading. UPDATE (2026-08-11 second follow-up): the CALLER's UV-corner-generation formula (what param_2 contains per vertex) is now found -- see TSTexture4Poly_Render's entry. What's still not decoded is this function's OWN internal per-pixel interpolation/sampling math (the fixed-point span-fill loop itself, and the 4th-interpolant's exact semantics) -- not needed to resolve which UV a given vertex gets, only to bit-exactly reproduce the rasterizer's own fill algorithm.
entries.source: docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md 2026-08-11, UV formula found 2026-08-11 second follow-up

entries.name: TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB
entries.description: The other of the two rasterizer variants TSTexture4Poly_Render dispatches between -- longer and does extra sub-span/mip-style step-size selection (DAT_00471980/84/88 thresholds) not present in TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA, suggesting a mipmapped/higher-quality path vs. a simpler one, but not confirmed. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: maybe_TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest
entries.description: Called by TSTexture4Poly_Render with poly+4/+6 (Normal/Center vertex-index fields) as arguments; result gates which of a front-color/back-color pair gets used. Reasoned from call-site usage, not independently disassembly-verified instruction-by-instruction the way other 'high' confidence entries in this file are -- worth confirming before relying on the exact facing-test semantics.

entries.name: g_MechTextureGroupNames
entries.description: 7-entry array of pointers to the literal strings 'light'/'medium'/'heavy'/'enemy'/'apocatex'/'razortex'/'newhercs' (the strings themselves start at 0049a437, 0x0049a37c holds an 8th unrelated pointer -- not part of this array, unresearched). Confirmed dead in DBSIM.EXE's own code (zero xrefs to the array base or any individual string, checked both via ReferenceManager and a full-binary decompiled-text scan) -- DBSIM does NOT read this table at runtime to pick a mech's DBA. The real runtime mechanism is MechType_TextureGroupIndex (see that entry) feeding g_MechTextureGroupSlots directly; this string table is very likely leftover linked-in rodata from the same shared ThreeSpace source file, present in the binary but never actually executed. Byte-verified against Herculan/docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md's already-known 7-name set from VSHELL/user domain knowledge -- exact match.

entries.name: g_MechTextureGroupSlots
entries.description: 8-byte-stride array, one slot per texture group (light/medium/heavy/enemy/apocatex/razortex/newhercs -- see g_MechTextureGroupNames, though this array is populated independently of that dead string table; the loader that fills each slot from a real .DBA wasn't traced this session). MechType_InitOne (0041a8) writes '&g_MechTextureGroupSlots + textureGroupIndex*8' directly into every mesh sub-component's TSShapeInstance+0x26 (the confirmed bound-active-DBA field from docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md's VSHELL RE) at mech-spawn time -- this is the actual, confirmed, executed mech-to-texture-atlas binding mechanism in DBSIM.EXE.

entries.name: MechType_InitOne
entries.description: Per-mech-type init, called once per valid slot (0-0x54) by Mechs_InitAllTypes. Opens the per-mech-type resource files (name built from the mech's own code string + several folder-prefix globals), reads a 0xd8-byte fixed record into the MECH_TYPE_DATA[typeIndex] struct (0x21e bytes/entry) at record offset 2, initializes hit-zone/collision/debris sub-resources, and -- the confirmed answer to 'how does DBSIM pick a mech's texture' -- for every mesh sub-component of this mech type, sets TSShapeInstance+0x26 (bound active DBA, see docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md) to '&g_MechTextureGroupSlots + typeRecord[0x96]*8'. typeRecord+0x96 is MechType_TextureGroupIndex (see that entry); the 0xd8-byte record it lives in is read directly from simvol0/dat/<MECHNAME>.DAT, byte-exact match with HercWorks.Core's already-ported (but previously unregistered) HercSimDat/HercSimDataTransformer -- offset 0x96 in the record = offset 148 in the file = HercSimDat.ModelSkinId, which the original Java port had already named correctly without knowing why.

entries.name: Mechs_InitAllTypes
entries.description: Creates the 'mechs' object pool (string xref confirmed) sized DAT_004a9d8a*0x21e (the MECH_TYPE_DATA record size), then loops mech-type slot 0..0x54 calling MechType_InitOne (004201a8) for every slot MechTypeSlot_GetIndex (0041ff00) reports as in-use (!= 0xff).

entries.name: maybe_MechTypeSlot_GetIndex
entries.description: Trivial accessor, returns (&DAT_004a9d8c)[param_1] -- a per-slot byte, 0xff sentinel meaning 'unused', otherwise the allocated dense index used by MechType_InitOne. Not independently cross-checked beyond its two callers (Mechs_InitAllTypes, MechTypeSlot_Allocate).

entries.name: maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate
entries.description: Assigns the next dense allocation index (DAT_004a9d8a, post-incremented) to slot param_1's (&DAT_004a9d8c)[param_1] entry the first time it's requested; on the very first allocation overall, also caches an object-pool handle (FUN_0040feb4(1) result) into _DAT_004a9df4. Not independently cross-checked beyond call-site usage.

entries.name: Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint
entries.description: Registers one structure's footprint in the height grid's +0xf0 scratch array, ready for Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints to level it. Sets the scratch byte to 1 for the cell the structure stands in unconditionally, then walks the cells in the position's radius-sized bounding box and, for each whose corner (cellX << cellShift, cellY << cellShift, position.z) is within radius by Math_FastMagnitude3D -- the z terms cancel, so the test is planar -- marks that cell plus the three west, south and south-west of it, covering all four quads meeting that corner. radius is the caller's SimObject_GetShapeRadius (vtable +0x10). Callers: Base_AttachToGroup (00405c3c) and DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects' own base branch, each immediately before that structure's height query. No bounds checking beyond refusing to step to a negative index.

entries.name: Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints
entries.description: THE REASON A TURRET STANDS ON A FLAT-TOPPED MOUND. A zone heightmap marks each emplacement with a single raised sample (ZONE555: one cell of 120 in a plain of 97 under each turret), which as a corner sample is the apex of a four-quad pyramid at the cell's CORNER while the structure stands near its centre. This levels it instead: walk every cell, and where the scratch byte is marked (bit 0) but not yet counted (bit 1), flood-fill the connected region with Terrain_AccumulateFootprint to get its raw-height sum and count, then write sum/count back over it with Terrain_WriteFootprintHeight. Finishes with Terrain_BuildSurface, since every normal, diagonal selector and baked shade is now stale. Called once by DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects (at 004263d9) after the whole roster is placed, which then re-queries every base's ground height. Walks both axes to 1 << widthShift, which would half-cover a taller-than-wide zone; every retail zone is square.

entries.name: Terrain_PaintFormationPad
entries.description: Stamps one base formation's material over the terrain tile a world point falls in, and marks that formation's occupied cells for the flattening pass. The only writer of cell +0xf bits [2:7] outside the two zone loaders, and the only path by which materials 2-12 reach shipped terrain -- TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap's roll is capped at 2. The tile is 1 << (0x15 - mat0[material].BlockShift) world units square, independent of CellShift, and dimension x dimension map entries span it exactly; a cell takes 1 << (CellShift - 13) entries per axis. Every cell of the tile is painted; only cells whose map byte is nonzero also get Terrain_SetCellScratch(1), which is the second input to Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints (00471190) alongside the per-object radius marks of Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint (00470dc8), and is why a base's whole pad levels as one region. Map row 0 indexes the tile's HIGH-y edge and counts down. The material write is skipped entirely when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set (the low-memory mode: -l, or under 12 MB physical), leaving the ground flat but unpainted.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Terrain_PaintFormationPad(void *grid, int *worldPoint, int materialIndex, unsigned char **mapRows, int dimension)

entries.name: Terrain_AccumulateFootprint
entries.signature: void __cdecl Terrain_AccumulateFootprint(void *grid, int cellX, int cellY)
entries.description: Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints' measuring half: an eight-way recursive flood fill over cells whose +0xf0 scratch byte has bit 0 set and bit 1 clear. Sets bit 1, then adds the cell's raw height byte to DAT_006b54f4 and increments the cell count DAT_006b54f8, which the caller divides to get the region's average height.

entries.name: Terrain_WriteFootprintHeight
entries.signature: void __cdecl Terrain_WriteFootprintHeight(void *grid, int cellX, int cellY, int height, int force)
entries.description: Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints' writing half, and the part that produces the FLAT TOP rather than a flat set of corner samples. Eight-way recursive like Terrain_AccumulateFootprint but over bit 2 of the +0xf0 scratch byte; the force argument makes a cell take the height whether or not it is part of the footprint, and it is passed 1 only for the neighbours east, north and north-east. Those three are therefore written but not recursed through, being unmarked, so a region gains one sample on each of those two sides -- which turns a single marked cell into a 2x2 block of equal samples, i.e. one flat quad centred on the structure with the four surrounding quads sloping down to the plain.

entries.name: Terrain_SetCellScratch
entries.signature: void __cdecl Terrain_SetCellScratch(void *grid, int cellX, int cellY, unsigned char value)
entries.description: Stores one byte in the height grid's +0xf0 per-cell scratch array at (cellY << widthShift) + cellX. Coordinate-addressed counterpart to HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte (00470c68), which addresses the same array by cell pointer. No bounds check.

entries.name: Terrain_GetCellScratch
entries.signature: unsigned char __cdecl Terrain_GetCellScratch(void *grid, int cellX, int cellY)
entries.description: Reads one byte of the height grid's +0xf0 per-cell scratch array at (cellY << widthShift) + cellX. Getter for Terrain_SetCellScratch. No bounds check.

entries.name: HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte
entries.signature: void __cdecl HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte(void *grid, void *cell, unsigned char value)
entries.description: Writes the HeightGrid's parallel per-cell scratch byte array at +0xf0, addressing it by cell pointer -- ((cell - grid[+0xec]) >> 4) -- where Terrain_SetCellScratch (00470cd0) addresses the same array by cell coordinates. Called once per cell by TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap with 0, zeroing the array at load; the ASCII fallback loader writes it inline instead. The array's consumers are the structure-footprint pass (Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint / Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints) and then, at runtime, Terrain_DrawCellObjects' per-cell pending-object count.

entries.name: Math_RandomNext
entries.description: The game's pseudo-random generator: an additive lagged Fibonacci generator over a 56-entry (0x38) table of shorts with two rotating byte cursors at state+0x70 and state+0x71. Each call does table[i] += table[j]; returns the new table[i] in the low 16 bits; then advances both cursors modulo 56. Callers pass the state block address (0x4d261d) and mask the result -- & 0xfff for the terrain material roll in TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap and for the explosion's ~51% per-component roll in FUN_004187d0. The 56 seed values live in the data section and have not been extracted.

entries.name: Cpp_VectorNew
entries.description: The compiler's C++ 'vector new' runtime helper (carries the 'Illegal mode in vector new' error string): optionally allocates param_2*param_3 bytes (plus a 4-byte count prefix when mode bit 0x10 is set), then invokes the element constructor param_5 once per element at param_2 stride. Worth having named because it appears in the middle of data-structure loaders -- e.g. the HeightGrid cell array allocation in TerrainZone_PopulateFromBitmap -- where it can otherwise be mistaken for domain logic.

entries.name: HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch
entries.description: Single-statement function: memsets the HeightGrid's +0xf0 per-cell scratch byte array to 0, sized (1 << grid[+0x100]) * (1 << grid[+0x104]) -- exactly one byte per cell. Called first thing in maybe_Scene_SubmitFrameObjects (0042841c), so it runs once per frame. That reset is what lets one array serve two unrelated uses: the structure-footprint pass's marked/counted/written bits at mission spawn, and from the first frame onward a per-cell pending-object count, incremented by 00470cac and consumed and re-cleared per cell by Terrain_DrawCellObjects (0046e4a0). Without it the first frame would read a flattened base's footprint marks as object counts.

entries.name: Terrain_IncrementCellObjectCount
entries.description: Increments the +0xf0 scratch byte of the cell a 16-byte cell pointer names and returns the new value -- the per-frame writer of the pending-object count Terrain_DrawCellObjects (0046e4a0) reads back and clears. Addresses by cell pointer, like HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte (00470c68), rather than by coordinates like Terrain_SetCellScratch (00470cd0). The count is only meaningful after HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch (0046e840) has reset the array for the frame.

entries.name: HeightGrid_GetCellScratchByte
entries.description: Reads the +0xf0 scratch byte for the cell a 16-byte cell pointer names -- the by-pointer counterpart of Terrain_GetCellScratch (00470cf4), and the read half of HeightGrid_SetCellScratchByte (00470c68).

entries.name: maybe_Scene_SubmitFrameObjects
entries.description: Per-frame scene assembly. Calls HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch(ActiveHeightGrid) first, then walks ~10 separate global object lists (the flat/flat2 ground shapes from maybe_Ground_LoadFlatShapes' list at 004a9711, GlobalMechList, and eight others), calling a small per-object submit helper (004282d8 / 0042837c / 004283b4) on each and caching a 2-byte result pair into each object at +0x7a / +0x1ea. Named 'maybe_' because the per-object helpers were not decoded, so 'submit for render' vs. some other per-frame pass is inferred from position and structure, not proven.

entries.name: maybe_Terrain_ComputeViewDistance
entries.description: LOCATES THE CONSUMER OF THE HeightGrid LOD FIELD (+0x10c), previously recorded as unlocated. Converts the viewer position (param_2+4/+8) to cell coordinates by >> cellShift (+0x108), then computes grid[+0x10c] << cellShift -- the LOD field scaled from cells into world units. If the viewer's cell is within LOD cells of any grid edge (tested against both 1 << grid[+0x100] and 1 << grid[+0x104]) that distance collapses to a literal 1000. Then builds a transform from the viewer's angle (+0x14) plus grid[+0x110] and emits two values into param_3. Called once per frame from 0042e700 with ActiveHeightGrid, writing into the world object at +0x72. Named 'maybe_' because the final three-call chain (00480330 / 0048c4f0 / 0048c5c4) was not decoded, so 'view/draw distance' is the reading most consistent with the arithmetic and the edge clamp, not a proven semantic for the two outputs.

entries.name: World_LoadTheater
entries.description: World/theater setup, called by DBSim_LoadScriptDat with script.dat's 20-byte header as its argument (it copies the first 5 dwords to DAT_004cfd48). Builds the base name 'world<N>' via _itoa where N = DAT_004cfd48*2 + DAT_004cfd5a, i.e. header[0]*2 + header[18] -- five theaters, two variants each. Loads dpl\world<N>.dpl (the per-theater palette, which is what the retail WORLD0.DPL..WORLD9.DPL family is), then reads wld\world<N>.wld field-by-field (descriptor layout decoded and verified byte-exact against all ten retail .WLD files), then 'shades' via 0042e760, then world<N>.rmp -- the 8-bit software renderer's colour-ramp/lighting LUT. .RMP layout, byte-verified against all 10 retail files (WORLD0-9.RMP, all exactly 98312 bytes): int32 width, int32 height, then width*height*256 raw bytes (every file: width=32, height=12, 8+32*12*256=98312). width/height are read via the same generic field-reader callback used for .wld fields; the body is read in one call into DAT_004a09b0 (FUN_004734ac(fileHandle, width*height*256, DAT_004a09b0)). Installs _DAT_004a5b18=rampTableBase and DAT_004a5b1c=DAT_004a5b20=width -- height is used locally for the allocation size and not retained in any global. TSSolidPoly_Render's ramp-offset formula ((DAT_004a5b1c-1)*shade & 0xffffff00, i.e. (width-1)*shade rounded down to a multiple of 256) confirms width=32 is the light-level-row COUNT with 256 bytes per row (one byte per dither-table output 0-255), so that path only ever reads the first 32*256=8192 bytes of the 98304-byte body; the other 11 height-slices are not consumed by it (purpose unknown, possibly a different render mode's ramp bank). Finishes with Terrain_BindTextureBank(the 4th of the descriptor's 5 trailing strings) and maybe_Ground_LoadFlatShapes.

entries.name: maybe_Ground_LoadFlatShapes
entries.description: Loads a DTS shape set and binds a matching DBA to it, choosing base name 'flat' when param_1 == 0 and 'flat2' otherwise; the same base name is used for both 'dts\<name>' and 'dba\<name>'. Stores the loaded shape list at 004a971c with its count at 004a9720, then loops over every loaded shape writing the bound-DBA pointer into each instance's +0x26 -- the SAME bound-active-DBA field confirmed for mech texturing in docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md. Called at the end of World_LoadTheater. Retail data has FLAT2.DBA (a single 64x54 frame). Named 'maybe_' because what the flat/flat2 shapes are actually drawn as (ground plane, distant filler, skirt) was not determined.

entries.name: Terrain_RayWalk
entries.description: Ray-versus-terrain traversal, the largest function in the terrain module (5129 bytes). Halves the segment delta until every component fits +/-32000, derives four Q16 slopes via 0047df5c, classifies the ground-plane delta into an octant 0-7, then walks the height grid cell by cell with a two-phase step (a minor-axis crossing stashes the major-axis exit and replays it next iteration). Each step yields an exit point and an edge code 0=W/1=E/2=N/3=S, tested by Terrain_EdgeCrossingTest and refined by Terrain_CellSurfaceIntersect. param_6 selects the body: 0 = thin ray (weapon fire, via Sim_RaycastTerrain), 1 = swept volume (movement collision, via 0046fe84/0046ff74/0046fcac). Six multiplies in the octant-2/3 arms are 32-bit truncating imul/sar rather than Math_Q16Multiply.

entries.name: Terrain_EdgeCrossingTest
entries.description: Terrain_RayWalk's per-step test: (grid, cellX, cellY, exitPoint, edgeCode) -> is the terrain along that cell edge at or above the exit point. Takes the edge's two corner heights (rawByte * grid+0x118 + grid+0x110); below both = clear, at or above both = hit, straddling = interpolate the edge height at the exit point (fraction along Y for edges 0/1, along X for 2/3). Bounds-checks only the flat corner index, so an edge in the last column reads the next row's first cell -- the same wrap Terrain_HeightQuery has.

entries.name: Terrain_CellSurfaceIntersect
entries.description: Solves exactly where a segment meets the ground inside one cell, once Terrain_EdgeCrossingTest has reported a crossing. Builds a plane from each of the cell's two face normals (cell+0x1 and cell+0x7) through a corner that triangle contains, and intersects via Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect; works in cell-local X/Y with world Z and adds the cell origin back on the way out. Result returned in the statics at DAT_006b50e0. Near triangle first, selected by cell+0xf&3 the same way Terrain_HeightQuery selects. Two quirks: selector 0's far triangle has no corner in this cell, so it shifts one cell east and uses corner (x+1,y); selector 2's far plane keeps the NEAR triangle's plane constant rather than recomputing it against the far normal.

entries.name: Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect
entries.description: (plane{nx,ny,nz,d}, segment{start[3],end[3]}, out[3]) -> bool. Denominator = dot(n, end-start), numerator = -(dot(n, start) + d); rejects a parameter outside the segment by comparing the pair with the sign of the denominator rather than dividing first, then applies it per component through a 64-bit multiply (0047de78) and divide (0047dd21).

entries.name: Terrain_BuildCellSurface
entries.description: Writes one height-grid cell's diagonal selector (cell+0xf bits [0:1]) and both face normals (cell+0x1 and cell+0x7, three shorts each) from its four corner heights. Selector 1 = coplanar quad (h00+h11 == h01+h10, both normals identical), 2 = split along the (0,0)-(1,1) diagonal, 0 = along the anti-diagonal. Normals are in raw height units -- horizontal components are corner differences, vertical is cellSize/HeightScale -- doubled, then rescaled to length 0x800 by FUN_0046c138. This is the writer of the selector bits that was open until 2026-08-24; neither zone loader touches them.

entries.name: Terrain_BuildSurface
entries.description: Runs Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade (0046c2ec) over every cell of a height grid, row by row. The last row and column have no east/north neighbour to difference against and keep a flat (0,0,0x800) normal and selector 0. Two callers: TerrainZone_LoadHeightmap's zone load, and the tail of Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints (00471190), which has just changed raw heights and so needs every normal, selector and baked shade rebuilt over them.

entries.name: Terrain_ResolveCellTexture
entries.signature: int __cdecl Terrain_ResolveCellTexture(int *materialRecord, int cellX, int cellY, int *uvOut)
entries.description: Terrain texture selection and tiling. Takes an 8-byte dat\mat0 record, the cell's X and Y, and a UV-rect output of four (u, v) pairs -- pair i belongs to vertex i of Terrain_DrawCellQuad's quad, in its corner order (cellX,cellY), (cellX,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY), so u rises with cellX and the negated v FALLS with cellY. Indexes the active terrain bitmap descriptor table (_DAT_006b4fc4, 20-byte stride -- the SAME per-frame descriptor structure the mech texture path uses, see dts-texture-binding.md) by mat0 field 0, i.e. mat0's first field IS a DBA frame index. Then branches on mat0 field 1 (BlockShift): if 0, the frame's own F0..F3 UV corners are used verbatim (texture stretched across the quad); otherwise shift = cellShift + BlockShift - 13 and the rect becomes u0 = (cellX << shift) & 0xff, v0 = (cellY << shift) & 0xff, spanning 2^shift texels, with V negated. The & 0xff wrap is a 256-texel tiling space -- which is why the terrain banks are 256x256 and must be edge-tileable. Returns descriptor field 4 (bytes 16-19) as a short: the bitmap handle handed to the polygon draw. Retail: mat0 record 0 = {frame 0, BlockShift 6}, record 1 = {frame 1, BlockShift 6}; that is shift = cellShift - 7, so 128 texels per cell at cellShift 14 and 64 at 13 -- 128 world units per texel either way.

entries.name: Terrain_BindTextureBank
entries.description: Binds the terrain texture bank. Takes a bare base name, joins it with the 'dba' folder pointer (PTR_DAT_004a0a28), loads that resource, and stores its 20-byte-stride frame descriptor table into _DAT_006b4fc4 for Terrain_ResolveCellTexture to index. Called from World_LoadTheater with the 4th of the five NUL-terminated strings at the end of the world<N>.wld descriptor -- so the terrain bank is named in DATA, not in code, which is exactly why neither DBSIM.EXE nor VSHELL.EXE contains the strings 'ice'/'bsnow'/'volcan'/'moon' despite those .DBA files shipping. Retail mapping: WORLD0/1 urban, 2/3 bsnow, 4/5 volcan, 6/7 ice, 8/9 moon.

entries.name: Raster_PerspectiveDivide
entries.description: The perspective divide, ahead of Raster_ProjectToScreen's centring: screenOut[0] = (viewPoint[0] << DAT_006c60ac) / viewPoint[1], screenOut[1] = (viewPoint[2] << DAT_006c60ac) / viewPoint[1], or both over DAT_006c60b4 with a shift of 0 (the orthographic mode). Returns screenOut. Dividing components 0 and 2 by component 1 is what fixes the view-space axis order as (across, DEPTH, up) -- the fact that says which component Terrain_DrawCellQuad's fog distance is. DAT_006c60ac is the focal shift installed from view+0x1a.

entries.name: Raster_SetupTexturedSpan
entries.description: Per-vertex setup for the textured/Gouraud span fills. In its param_6 == 2 (Gouraud) branch it computes each vertex's ramp row as shade * (DAT_004d3d38 - 1) + DAT_004a08c8 << 8 -- the same arithmetic as Raster_ShadeRampRow, depth bias included. Together with Raster_DrawPolygon's mode-1 branch this is why the Gouraud and textured paths fog by the same rule as the flat ones, even though neither renderer calls Raster_ShadeRampRow itself.

entries.name: Prefs_SetOption
entries.signature: void __cdecl Prefs_SetOption(short index, unsigned char value, char apply)
entries.description: Writes one simulator option: saves the old byte to (&DAT_004d2028)[index], stores value at (&DAT_004d1fbc)[index], and when apply is non-zero calls the option's handler at (&DAT_004d2060)[index] with the new value. The option array based at DAT_004d1fbc is what makes DAT_004d1fc3 (terrain detail) option 7. Derived from raw disassembly: three stack args at EBP+8/+0xc/+0x10, RET with no operand.

entries.name: Prefs_LoadOptions
entries.description: Loads data\prefs.cfg over the option array: memset(&DAT_004d1fbc, 0, 0x36) then a 0x36-byte read straight into it, so THE FILE IS THE ARRAY -- unparsed, an option's index is its byte offset, and a retail prefs.cfg is 54 bytes. Then walks all 0x36 options calling each one's handler from DAT_004d2060 and seeding the shadow copies at DAT_004d1ff2 (when param_1 is non-zero) and DAT_004d2028. Its argument was not derived from disassembly, so no signature is recorded.

entries.name: Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion
entries.description: Per-frame terrain visibility setup, called twice per frame from the frame function 0045fb9c with ActiveHeightGrid passed AS A PARAMETER (which is why a search for readers of the ActiveHeightGrid global missed the terrain render path entirely). WRITES the LOD field: grid[+0x10c] = (short)DAT_004a0bcc[DAT_004d1fc3], then >>= (cellShift - 14) when cellShift > 14. DAT_004a0bcc is three int16s -- 6, 10, 14 cells -- indexed by the terrain-detail option DAT_004d1fc3, so the draw radius is a player setting; the >> only ever fires on the two shift-15 zones and nothing compensates below shift 14. Passes grid[0x10c] << cellShift to 00428bc0 (which derives 5 distance bands), builds the visible cell-space region into grid+0x28 with count grid+0xc8 / pointer grid+0xcc / visible flag grid+0x11c, and installs two texture-basis vectors at grid+4 and grid+0x10.

entries.name: Terrain_DrawCellQuad
entries.signature: void __cdecl Terrain_DrawCellQuad(int cellX, int cellY, void *grid, int *vertexBlock)
entries.description: Draws one terrain cell. The caller (FUN_0046dcd8 / FUN_0046dea4) hands it a vertex block already carrying the quad's four camera-space corner positions, in the order (cellX,cellY), (cellX,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY+1), (cellX+1,cellY); this fetches the matching four cells at grid[0xec] + index*0x10 (16 bytes/cell) and adds each corner's projected raw height byte (cell[0], via 00495240 against the grid+0xd0 projection state). It re-derives the diagonal split here from the projected corners rather than reading cell[+0xf]: z0+z2 == z1+z3 emits one 4-vertex quad, < 0 splits along corner 0-2, > 0 along corner 1-3. Texture comes from Terrain_ResolveCellTexture(&mat0[cell[0xf] >> 2], cellX, cellY, uvOut), whose four UV pairs are handed to the vertices by index in all three branches -- the fact that pins the corner-to-UV mapping. Each triangle's shade byte is cell[+0xd] (near) / cell[+0xe] (far) and its backface test uses the normals at cell[+0x1] / cell[+0x7] via Terrain_FaceVisibilityTest. Fog: installs the visibility range grid[0x10c] << grid[0x108] via Raster_SetVisibilityRange, then Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance(min of the four corners' component 1) -- component 1 is the view-space DEPTH (Raster_PerspectiveDivide divides by it), so a whole cell is fogged from its NEAREST corner's depth, not per pixel and not from a radial distance. Ends by calling Terrain_DrawCellObjects for the cell.
entries.source: docs/formats/terrain-texturing.md, 'Which quad corner takes which UV'

entries.name: Terrain_BuildDrawRegionQuad
entries.description: Builds the terrain draw region as a square of radius (grid[+0x10c] << cellShift) world units centred on the viewer (DAT_006b4fc8 / DAT_006b4fcc), clamped to the grid's own extent ((1 << widthShift) - 2 << cellShift, plus origin at grid+0xf4/+0xf8), and emits it as a 4-corner quad at constant Z (grid+0xfc); writes count 0 instead when the clamped region is empty. Confirms the LOD field is literally a terrain draw radius in cells.

entries.name: maybe_Sim_RenderFrame
entries.description: The per-frame render root. Order: Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion(ActiveHeightGrid, view, 0), then FUN_004327ac(CockpitViewInstance) (per-widget paint dispatch over the weapon-slot array and the chain/link/autotrack/shield/etc. sub-widgets), then maybe_Scene_SubmitFrameObjects (the 3D world), then conditionally a second terrain setup plus maybe_Terrain_ComputeViewDistance and 0042883c, then Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate, then three more vtable paint dispatches on CockpitViewInstance sub-objects (+0x1f5, FUN_00433158's result, +0x20b). Widget paint therefore happens BEFORE the 3D scene submit each frame, not after -- though DBSIM's software-blit ordering need not constrain an OpenGL implementation that composites via alpha/depth instead. Named 'maybe_' because the individual draw dispatches were not decoded; its role as the frame root is solid (it is the sole caller of both the terrain setup and the view setup).

entries.name: maybe_Terrain_SetDistanceBands
entries.description: Given the terrain view distance in world units (grid[+0x10c] << cellShift), computes five scaled values via 0047dfa4 against a 5-entry short table at DAT_0049abb0, storing them at DAT_004cfa0c. Shape of fog band or LOD threshold setup derived from the terrain draw distance. Named 'maybe_' because the consumer of DAT_004cfa0c was not traced.

entries.name: g_UnusedTerrainTypeNames
entries.description: A 3-entry pointer table to the literal strings 'urban', 'waste', 'ruins' (at 0049ab82/0049ab88/0049ab8e); the 4th slot is not a pointer, so the table is exactly 3 long. Found via string xref while hunting terrain texture selection. DEAD DATA -- ES2FindAddressRefs on this address returns zero references anywhere in DBSIM, the third confirmed instance of this binary's dead-table pattern after g_MechTextureGroupNames and the RTTI type-name strings. Recorded so a future session does not re-derive it as a live terrain-type selector; note also that only URBAN.DBA exists in retail data (no WASTE/RUINS).

entries.name: Hud_WorldUnitsToMetres
entries.description: THE GAME'S UNIT SCALE, stated by the original itself: 'return (worldUnits / 1000) * 6', i.e. 1000 world units = 6 metres, one world unit = 6 mm, 166.667 units per metre. Three call sites, two unrelated HUD gadgets, both feeding it a raw difference of two world positions: Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator (0043c3e4, the 'WAYPOINT n: d M.' string) and the scanner MFD contact-range readout (0043ebe0/0043eecc). The integer divide quantises the displayed figure to multiples of 6 m.

entries.name: Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator
entries.description: Per-frame HUD waypoint indicator: picks the active waypoint (or the nav-target position), computes the 2D ground distance from the player mech via Math_FastMagnitude2D, converts it with Hud_WorldUnitsToMetres, and builds the on-screen string as <prefix> + itoa(waypointNumber) + ': ' + itoa(metres) + ' M.'. Also draws the direction diamond/arrow triangles.

entries.name: Hud_UpdateSpeedReadout
entries.description: Formats the HUD speed text: itoa(Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph(LocalPlayerMech)) followed by the literal ' K/H' (0049c112). The gadget it writes into is DAT_004d185c, built in Gau_RovingGunsightWidget against the width template '000 K/H'.

entries.name: Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph
entries.description: Converts a mech's current speed to the KPH figure the HUD prints: currentSpeed * typeRec[+0xc2] / typeRec[+6], where MechType_InitOne sets typeRec[+0xc2] = Math_Q10Multiply(315, maxForwardSpeed) -- so the whole thing reduces to speed * 315/1024 (0.3076). Verified against the manual's HERC specs: OUTLAW's 325 max reads exactly 100 KPH, SAMSON's 190 reads 58 against a quoted 60, COLOSSUS 180 -> 55, MAVERICK 285 -> 88 against 90. Flyers (typeRec[+0x50] != 0, i.e. the Razor) take a different branch through the map-range helper 0047de3c. The 315 looks designer-fitted to make the fastest HERC read a round 100, so this constant should NOT be used to derive the simulation's tick length.

entries.name: Math_Q10Multiply
entries.description: Q10 fixed-point multiply: (int64)a*b >> 10. Previously seen unnamed in the shield-balance code; also builds the HUD's speed-display scale factor in MechType_InitOne.

entries.name: Math_Q16Multiply
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point multiply: (int64)a*b >> 16. Used by MechType_InitOne to rescale a mech type's speed fields by a Q16 ratio built with Math_Q16Divide.

entries.name: Math_Q16Divide
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point divide: ((int64)a << 16) / b.

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude2D
entries.description: Sqrt-free 2D magnitude approximation: max(|dx|,|dy|) + min(|dx|,|dy|)/2 -- the octagonal estimate, exact on axis and up to ~11.8% high on a diagonal. The 2D counterpart of Math_FastMagnitude3D. This is the distance both HUD distance readouts display, so the original's own on-screen ranges carry that error.

entries.name: maybe_Math_MapRange
entries.description: Five-argument linear remap: maps param_1 from the range [param_2,param_3] onto [param_4,param_5] with a rounding bias term. Named 'maybe_' because it was only observed in one place (the flyer branch of Mech_GetDisplaySpeedKph).

entries.name: Time_GetCoarseTicks
entries.description: (GetTickCount() - startTick) >> 4, i.e. elapsed time in 16 ms units (62.5 Hz). The mission clock gadget (0043dcac) advances one displayed second per 0x3c=60 of these units, so the original's clock runs ~4% fast. This is the coarse UI/event timebase and is NOT the same thing as SimTickDelta, which Sim_MainTick reads from a separate per-frame timing struct.

entries.name: Vec2_Subtract
entries.description: In-place 2D vector subtract: a->x -= b->x, a->y -= b->y. Confirms the HUD's waypoint/contact distances are ground-plane distances, Z ignored.

entries.name: Vec2_Magnitude
entries.description: Thin wrapper: Math_FastMagnitude2D(v->x, v->y) via 0049298e.

entries.name: Vec2_DistanceBetween
entries.description: Copies a 2D point, subtracts another (Vec2_Subtract) and returns the approximate magnitude (Vec2_Magnitude) -- the distance primitive the HUD waypoint indicator uses.

entries.name: DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects
entries.description: DBSIM's world-spawn pass and the function that actually builds a mission's objects -- the second of two reads of data\script.dat. RE-OPENS the file from the top (path built from maybe_DatFolderPrefixPtr + the string at 0049aa3e), skips blocks 1-6, then walks blocks 7-13 again. For every slot DBSim_LoadScriptDat's first pass marked live it constructs an object and reads that object's OWN record for placement: block 7 (134B) gives mech type at +0x28, weapon fit at +0x2a, position ref at +0x3e, heading ref at +0x40; block 8 (92B) gives position +0x28, heading +0x2a, flyer type +0x2c; block 9 (52B) gives base type +0x00, position +0x02, heading +0x04. Position refs resolve into the block-1 coordinate array (DAT_004a9e90, stride 0xc); heading refs into the pre-multiplied block-2 array (DAT_004a9e94). Mechs and bases get Terrain_HeightQuery plus the type's foot offset; flyers get no query. Each base also registers its footprint with Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint before that query. It then reads block 11 into DAT_004a9e84 (stride 0x7a) via DBSim_BuildGroupRecord, remapping member refs to dense object indices, and appends the player.mec lance in place of record 0's members. With the roster down it calls Terrain_FlattenStructureFootprints (00471190) at 004263d9 and re-queries every base's ground height, the terrain having moved under them. Reading pass 1 (DBSim_LoadScriptDat) alone suggests script.dat carries no placement data; it is this pass that reads it.

entries.name: DBSim_BuildGroupRecord
entries.description: Builds one script.dat block-11 record into a 0x7a-byte in-memory group record: discriminator (record +0x28) at group+0, formation id (+0x2a) at group+2, heading value at group+10, the resolved block-1 coordinate pointer at group+0x18, the resolved row-10 action pointer at group+0x14, and an allocated array of member object pointers at group+0xc. Then attaches every populated member by discriminator -- Mech_AttachToGroup (0/mechs), FUN_00421ee8 (1/flyers), FUN_00405c3c (2/bases) -- passing each its slot index within the group.

entries.name: Mech_AttachToGroup
entries.description: Attaches a mech to its mission group: stores the group pointer at mech+0x45 and the member slot index at mech+0x49, then fills in heading and position ONLY IF still at the -0x8000 'unset' sentinel -- which is why a roster record's own position ref wins where set and the group's point is the fallback. Position comes from the group's coordinate pointer (group+0x18), or from FUN_00423b0c against the group's route when that is null. Z is Terrain_HeightQuery plus the mech type's foot offset (typeRecord+0x16), plus 5000 when typeRecord+0x50 is set. Calls mech vtable +0x78 (Mech_ApplyFormationOffset) with the position first. FUN_00421ee8 and FUN_00405c3c are the flyer and base equivalents; the flyer one deliberately does no terrain query and substitutes z=5000 when the coordinate's z is zero.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyFormationOffset
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x78. Spreads a group's members around its spawn point. No-ops for slot 0 (the leader stands on the point exactly); otherwise looks up Formation_GetSlotOffset(group's formation id at group+2, mech+0x49) and hands the offset to Formation_RotateAndAddOffset, which rotates it by the group leader's heading before adding it to the position.

entries.name: Formation_GetSlotOffset
entries.description: Returns a static 3-short {x, y, 0} formation offset: table[formationId * 0x1c + slot * 4 - 4] and the short after it. So a formation is 28 bytes = seven (x, y) short pairs, covering follower slots 1-7. OPEN: the table pointer _DAT_004a9df0 has exactly one reference in the whole binary -- this read -- and lives in uninitialised data, so nothing links it to a file. dat\MFORMS.DAT fits the shape exactly (142 content bytes = count + five 28-byte formations, formation 0 a symmetric wedge at 10000-unit steps) but is unconfirmed. Contrast the base equivalent (FUN_00405b9c/Base_LoadFormationTable, 2026-08-14), whose load site IS confirmed -- this pointer never got the same treatment.

entries.name: Formation_RotateAndAddOffset
entries.description: Rotates a formation offset into world space and adds it to a position. Takes the group leader (first entry of the group's member array at group+0xc), lazily builds its rotation matrix from its heading (leader+0xc -> leader+0x12, guarded by the stale flag at leader+0x32 that Mech_AttachToGroup clears), rotates the offset by it, and accumulates into the caller's x/y/z. Also the base-formation attach path's rotator (called from FUN_00405c04); for a heading-only object (no pitch/roll, true of every base) the matrix build (FUN_0047eaac) plus apply (FUN_0047fedc) reduces algebraically to a plain 2D rotation: worldDX = dx*cos(heading) - dy*sin(heading), worldDY = dx*sin(heading) + dy*cos(heading).

entries.name: Base_AttachToGroup
entries.description: Base/structure equivalent of Mech_AttachToGroup (00417aa8), called from DBSim_BuildGroupRecord (00423b34) for discriminator 2. Stores the group pointer at +0x45 and the member's slot index within the group's DiscriminatedRefs array at +0x49. Fills heading only if unset (-0x8000 sentinel), applying a per-slot heading nudge from a formation-indexed table when the slot is nonzero. Fills position only if unset: reads the group's own coordinate pointer (group+0x18) or falls back to its route (FUN_00423b0c), then -- only when the adjustAnchor arg (the raw block-11 record's own 0x06 BinaryFlag) is nonzero -- replaces that shared point's position within its terrain tile with the formation's own fixed fraction of it, from BFORMS.DAT record +0x14 (map dimension), +0xc and +0x10 (the fraction in 256ths). This is what puts the group on the pad Base_ApplyFormationTerrain (00405db0) paints over the same tile; the two are gated by the same flag. It then unconditionally calls the object's own vtable +0x78 (Base_ApplyFormationOffset, FUN_00405c04) with the position, then Terrain_MarkStructureFootprint (00470dc8) with that position and the object's SimObject_GetShapeRadius, then a terrain height query. Mechs have no equivalent: Mech_AttachToGroup takes no such flag and contains none of this arithmetic.
entries.signature: void __cdecl Base_AttachToGroup(void *structure, void *group, short slot, int adjustAnchor)

entries.name: Base_ApplyFormationTerrain
entries.description: Repaints the ground under one base group with its formation's own material -- what puts a retail base on a marked concrete pad instead of open terrain. Called from DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects (004253d8) immediately after DBSim_BuildGroupRecord, for discriminator-2 groups whose block-11 BinaryFlag is set, passing the group's first-attached member. Reads that object's group pointer (+0x45) -> formation id (+2) -> the BFORMS.DAT record at DAT_004a9630, and returns without doing anything when the record's material index (+8) is -1, which is exactly the six formations that carry no layout map. Otherwise hands Terrain_PaintFormationPad (00471260) the object's position (+0x26), that material index, the record's row-pointer array (+0x18) and its map dimension (+0x14). Sibling of Base_AttachToGroup (00405c3c), which snaps the group onto the tile this paints under the same flag.

entries.name: Base_ApplyFormationOffset
entries.description: Vtable +0x78 for every base subtype (confirmed identical across all five base vtables: 0x497940/0x4979d4/0x4978ac/0x497784/0x497818, each layered on the common base vtable 0x49a54c) -- the structural match for Mech_ApplyFormationOffset (00417898). No-ops when the object's group-relative slot (+0x49) is 0 (the group's first-claimed member); otherwise looks up BaseFormation_GetSlotOffset(group's formation id, slot) via FUN_00405b9c and hands the offset to Formation_RotateAndAddOffset (00411d64).

entries.name: BaseFormation_GetSlotOffset
entries.description: Base equivalent of Formation_GetSlotOffset (004205cc), but reading a variable-length, file-backed table instead of a flat one: DAT_004a9630[formationId] is a per-formation record whose +4 field is a pointer to that formation's slot-offset array (10 bytes/slot: two int32s X,Y then a trailing int16), indexed as ptr + (slot-1)*10 -- i.e. slot N uses the (N-1)-th entry, so slot 1 (the group's first follower) uses entry 0. Returns {x, y} as two int32s (z is a one-time-zeroed static, never written per-call -- bases take no Z offset). DAT_004a9630 is populated by Base_LoadResources (00405fac) from dat\BFORMS.DAT -- unlike the mech table, this load site IS confirmed.

entries.name: Base_LoadResources
entries.description: base.cpp's resource-load sequence for the base/structure subsystem: streams dat\bforms (-> DAT_004a9630, formation offsets; see BaseFormation_GetSlotOffset), dat\lc_wpns, dat\bases (-> DAT_004a9620, the BASES.DAT type table BaseTypeTable.cs also reads; this is the only reader of it -- an entry at 0043a2e0 carried a copy of this description under the name Bases_LoadTypeTable until 2026-08-18, when that address was identified as MfdStatusScreen_Ctor and renamed), dat\basecol (collision), dat\bhulks, dat\basetex and dat\vehtex (texture banks) via a shared plain-file-read helper (FUN_00472e08 open / FUN_004734ac read via a vtable+0x18 dispatch / FUN_00472e58 close -- no container header, first bytes of each file are its own content, confirmed against BASES.DAT's independently-verified byte-exact parse). BFORMS.DAT's per-formation record is fully variable-length: int32 slot count N, N*10 bytes of slot data, an int32 material index (-1 for the six formations with no layout) and two more int32s (where the group's anchor sits in its tile, in 256ths), an int32 buffer count M, then M {1 length byte + that many data bytes} buffers -- confirmed byte-exact: walking the retail file this way consumes all 3186 content bytes with 17 formations (matching the block-11 formation id field's documented 0-16 range) and nothing left over.

entries.name: MfdStatusScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's status screen, shared by mode 0 (STATUS, F1) and mode 4 (TARGET, F5) -- MfdDisplay_Ctor builds one of each. Lazily loads the `bases`, `vehicles` and `flyers` sprite banks (folder "hba"/"dba" off VideoMode_UseHiResBanks) for target silhouettes, sets the wireframe viewport to inset+(0x2d,0xd)-(0x5f,0x3a), and builds five text labels from tables at 0049bd84 (x0), 0049bd8e (y0) and 0049bd98 (font selector into {ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE, [14] RED}). CORRECTED 2026-08-18: was named Bases_LoadTypeTable. It does not read dat\BASES.DAT -- that is Base_LoadResources (0043a3xx family, see its own entry); the collision was between loading the BASES sprite bank and loading the BASES data file. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: BaseType_LoadShape
entries.description: The whole of a structure type's model selection, indexing dat\BASES.DAT's table at typeIndex * 0x3c: the field at +6 picks the library (0 -> dgs\bases via BaseType_ResolveShape with classId 0x2bc0001, else dts\bases_an via the animated-library path with 0x1e0003) and the field at +2 is the shape index within it; the field at +0x32 picks the texture bank (0 -> basetex, else vehtex, except type 0x34 which borrows RAZOR's mech bank). Cross-check: exactly eight types select the animated library and BASES_AN.DTS holds exactly eight roots, numbered as those eight reference them. CORRECTED 2026-08-14: the 0x2bc0001/0x1e0003 constants are not recordSize<<16|version -- they are ClassItem registry classIds, and 0x2bc0001 is literally BASES.DGS's own leading 4 bytes. See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: BaseType_ResolveShape
entries.description: Resolves one dgs\bases shape by index (called by BaseType_LoadShape): reopens the file, then loops calling the ClassItem peek/skip primitive (FUN_0047a1fc, then FUN_0047a2a8 to skip) until the requested index is reached, then calls ClassItem_LoadResource once for the real load. Confirms dgs\BASES.DGS/BHULKS.DGS are flat sequential ClassItem lists, not random-access. See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: BaseShape_Construct
entries.description: ClassItem registry loadFn for classId 0x02bc0001 (dgs\bases/bhulks shape records): allocates a 0x438-byte object, installs the class's vtable (0049aaa0), then calls vtable+0xc (BaseShape_ReadFromStream). See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: BaseShape_ReadFromStream
entries.description: Field reader for a dgs\bases/bhulks shape record (vtable+0xc for classId 0x02bc0001), on top of the generic ClassItem base-class chain (ClassItemTree_ReadFromStream). Its tail is the shape's COLLISION VOLUME, a coarse height field: int16 columns (+0x2a), rows (+0x2c), origin column (+0x2e), origin row (+0x30), cell shift (+0x32), a 256-entry int32 height table (+0x34, 1024 bytes, last entry addressed as the ceiling at +0x430), then rows*columns height codes (+0x434). CORRECTED 2026-08-27: this was read as '5 undecoded scalars + an opaque block' followed by 'sub-record count * sub-record size raw records' -- the same byte count, so every retail record parsed correctly while all of it was named wrongly. See docs/simulation/hit-detection.md.

entries.name: ClassItemTree_ReadFromStream
entries.description: Generic base-class reader shared by dgs\bases/bhulks shape records (one level up from BaseShape_ReadFromStream): reads two int16 counts, a parallel int16 array, and a per-entry 32-byte vector (undecoded -- consumed by a BSP-adjacent walk, FUN_00476a1c). Byte-verified as part of the full record shape -- see dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: ClassItemTree_ReadChildren
entries.description: Generic base-class reader (below ClassItemTree_ReadFromStream): reads an int16 child count then that many nested objects via ClassItem_LoadResource. For dgs\bases/bhulks shape records, every retail child is an ordinary TSObjectHeader-family DTS chunk (observed tag 0x0014000c = TSDetailPart) -- the key finding that lets DTSModelTransformer.ReadOneObject parse it directly. See dgs-hd0-notes.md.

entries.name: ClassItemTree_ReadBaseHeader
entries.description: Deepest base-class reader in the ClassItem shape-tree hierarchy: 3 int16 head fields (+4, +6, +8) + 6 raw bytes. Shared by dgs\bases/bhulks shape records. CORRECTED 2026-08-27: the third field (+8) is the shape's BOUNDING RADIUS, not an id -- SimObject_GetShapeRadius and the LOD selector FUN_004033e4 both read it as one, and it tracks BASES.DAT +0x2a within about a fifth across all 45 records.

entries.name: LoadNameList
entries.description: Loads a nam\<name>.NAM list -- a flat run of NUL-terminated ASCII names indexed by type number -- with a capacity bound as the second argument. Called with ('mechs', 0x55) into the mech name table DAT_004a9de4 that MechType_InitOne indexes, and with ('flyers', 0x22) into DAT_004a9e74. These are the tables that turn script.dat block 7's and block 8's type numbers into resource base names; MECHS.NAM ships 21 names and FLYERS.NAM 3.

entries.name: TSSolidPoly_Construct
entries.description: TSSolidPoly's real constructor, found via g_TSObjectTypeRegistry's tag=0x00140002 entry. Same Watcom multi-base-class stamping pattern as TSTexture4Poly_Construct, finishing with &PTR_FUN_0047ee38 -- the actually-used TSSolidPoly vtable at runtime. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: g_TSSolidPolyVtable
entries.description: TSSolidPoly's real, fully-constructed vtable (found via TSSolidPoly_Construct's final vtable-pointer stamp). Slot +0x1c (TSSolidPoly_Render, FUN_00422a32) is what TSGroup_RenderPolys's per-poly dispatch (*(*polyPtr)+0x1c) calls for a TSSolidPoly, mirroring TSTexture4Poly's g_TSTexture4PolyVtable +0x1c slot exactly.

entries.name: TSSolidPoly_Render
entries.description: TSSolidPoly's real vtable-slot-0x1c render method (see g_TSSolidPolyVtable). Resolves surface record via (ColorIndexId*4 + g_ActiveSurfaceRecords) -- same *4 stride as TSTexture4Poly_Render, independently reconfirming ColorIndexId=surfaceIndex*4. Runs maybe_TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest against poly+4/+6 (Normal/Center point indices, each *6 into the Vec3Short point array) to pick front (piVar3[0]/[1] = Front/FrontLine) or back (piVar3[2]/[3] = Back/BackLine) color pair -- confirms TSSurfaceEntry's 4-slot Front/FrontLine/Back/BackLine layout applies to flat polys too, not just textured ones. Skips drawing if both resolved color dwords have top byte 0x18-shift == 0x14 (looks like an uninitialized/sentinel guard, not chased further). Otherwise clips via FUN_0045e694/FUN_0045ec54 and fills via FUN_0045f364 -- the SAME flat/solid 2D fill chain TSTexture4Poly_Render's DAT_00471890!=0 fallback branch also uses, confirming that branch really is 'reuse the flat-poly fill path' as its name implies. No dithering/lighting-ramp math visible anywhere in this chain -- VSHELL (a shell/viewer app) passes FrontColor/BackColor straight through to the fill routines, unlike DBSIM's in-mission renderer.

entries.name: TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest
entries.description: DBSIM's counterpart to VSHELL's maybe_TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest -- called identically (two Vec3Short point pointers, Normal then Center) from all three flat poly renderers (TSSolidPoly_Render 00474db4, TSShadedPoly_Render 0047542c, TSTexture4Poly_Render 00474e9c) to pick front vs. back surface color. Confirmed via structural match, not independently disassembled instruction-by-instruction.

entries.name: Light_ComputeShadeForFace
entries.description: The per-face 'shade byte' (0-255, clamped) calculation feeding TSShadedPoly_Render (0047542c). TSSolidPoly_Render does NOT call it -- a solid poly carries no light term at all. NOT a simple angle calc -- a real light-accumulation loop over the active light list (DAT_006c6130, max 10 slots, count DAT_006c612c), dispatching per-entry on a type tag from FUN_0048d94b: type 0 = ambient (adds a flat intensity from FUN_0048d956 unconditionally -- never seen actually populated this session, see Light_AddDirectional/PointHelper's entries), type 1 = directional (dot-product-like test via FUN_0048d99b against the face's Normal point (param_1), only contributes when the result crosses a fixed threshold, i.e. face-vs-light-direction test), type 2 = point light (distance-attenuated: displacement from the light's position (FUN_0048d961) to the face's Center point (param_2) combined with the Normal via FUN_0048d86e, divided by distance/range fields FUN_0048d973/FUN_0048d97e). Params: param_1 = poly's Normal-index Vec3Short pointer, param_2 = poly's Center-index Vec3Short pointer (same two pointers TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest receives). Sibling functions FUN_0048bdcc/FUN_0048c060 are near-identical variants (different param shapes) used elsewhere for the same shade calc, likely per-vertex vs. per-face evaluation.

entries.name: Light_Register
entries.description: Adds a light object pointer to the active light list (DAT_006c6130, 10-slot max, dedups by pointer identity). Only 4 call sites in the whole binary: FUN_00407388/FUN_00407444 (pooled directional/point light getters, see their own entries), FUN_00407878 (re-registers a persistent light list DAT_004a9690 into the active manager), and Sim_InitMissionSession (FUN_004614fc, inlines the same directional-light-creation logic as FUN_00407388 and calls this directly).

entries.name: Light_GetOrCreateDirectional
entries.description: Pooled-object getter/constructor for a type=1 (directional) light: recycles from a small free-list at param_1+0x35c/+0x360 if available, otherwise allocates+constructs (vtable &PTR_LAB_0049f8d8, type field at +0x16 set to 1), then registers it via Light_Register (FUN_0048bd44). Not yet traced who calls this (likely weapon/effect spawn code, not chased this session -- out of scope for static mission-geometry lighting).

entries.name: Light_GetOrCreatePoint
entries.description: Same pooled-object pattern as Light_GetOrCreateDirectional (FUN_00407388) but for a type=2 (point) light (vtable &PTR_LAB_00497ac8, type field +0x16 set to 2). Likely explosion/muzzle-flash light spawning; callers not traced this session.

entries.name: Light_CreateMissionSun
entries.description: MAJOR FINDING: called exactly once per mission, unconditionally, from Sim_InitMissionSession (FUN_004614fc) right after the light-system reset (FUN_0048dbfc) and before DBSim_LoadScriptDat -- creates the ONE directional 'sun' light every mission gets. Direction is NOT read from any mission/theater file: it's built from two HARDCODED constant vectors, local_38=(0,0x1000,0) and local_40=(-6000,0,21000), combined via FUN_0047eaac (looks like a normalize/transform) then FUN_0047ffb4 (looks like it derives a direction from a target-point + up-vector pair, output stored as the light's direction field). Intensity is set via vtable+4 call with literal 0x100 (256). The created light is registered via Light_Register (FUN_0048bd44) AND pushed onto a persistent list (DAT_004a9690) via FUN_00407800, so it survives a later Light_ReregisterPersistent (FUN_00407878) call. No separate ambient (type=0) light creation was found anywhere in the binary this session -- Light_ComputeShadeForFace's type-0 branch may be genuinely unused by real missions, meaning faces angled away from the sun likely render fully unlit (shade=0), not floor-lit. FUN_0047eaac/FUN_0047ffb4/FUN_0048d99b (the actual per-face dot-product math) are NOT yet decoded -- needed for a byte-exact reimplementation, but the qualitative shape (single fixed sun direction+intensity, no mission-specific lighting data) is now solid enough to plan an engine implementation around.

entries.name: Sim_InitMissionSession
entries.description: Per-mission session setup: resets the light system (FUN_0048dbfc), creates the mission's one hardcoded sun light (Light_CreateMissionSun), then calls DBSim_LoadScriptDat and DBSim_SpawnMissionObjects. Confirms lighting setup happens once per mission load, independent of which script.dat/theater is loaded. Also picks the FOCAL SHIFT -- 9 when DAT_004d30c4 >= 0x4b1 and 8 otherwise -- and passes it as the third argument of the view constructor FUN_0048bc98, which stores it at view+0x1a. That is the whole of the field of view; see docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE; docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md for the focal shift

entries.name: BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14
entries.description: Builds a 3x3 rotation matrix (9 Q14 fixed-point shorts + 1 mode byte, 10 shorts total output) from a Vec3Short of Euler angles (param_1), using a sin/cos lookup table at DAT_004a25dc (1024-entry quarter-wave table, angle unit = 0x10000 per full circle, i.e. raw/65536*360 = degrees). Has a fast-path when the X and Y angle components are both zero (2-axis-only case, cos/sin of Z alone); otherwise builds the general 3-axis matrix via the standard trig-table-driven approach (same trig-table technique as the sim's other rotation math, see [[project_es2_terrain_format]]-adjacent RE). Called by Light_CreateMissionSun with angles (-6000, 0, 21000) -- confirms the sun's direction is computed, not stored as a literal vector.

entries.name: RotateVectorByMatrixQ14
entries.description: Matrix-vector multiply: rotates param_1 (Vec3Short) by the 3x3 Q14 matrix param_2 (as built by BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14), writing the result to param_3. Has fast-paths for the matrix's degenerate mode byte (param_2[9]) similar to the matrix builder's own fast path. Called by Light_CreateMissionSun as rotate((0,0x1000,0), sunRotationMatrix) -- i.e. the sun's direction is 'straight up' rotated by the fixed Euler angles, not an arbitrary hand-authored vector.

entries.name: DotProductVec3Short
entries.description: Literal 3-component dot product on two Vec3Short pointers: a.x*b.x+a.y*b.y+a.z*b.z, no scaling/clamping. Called (via the Light_ComputeShadeForFace accessor wrapper FUN_0048d99b) with the poly's Normal-index point and a directional light's own direction vector -- confirms the type-1 (directional) lighting term in Light_ComputeShadeForFace is a plain dot product, i.e. the poly's 'Normal' auxiliary point genuinely holds a normal-like vector (not a position), consistent with the earlier front/back visibility-test finding that Normal/Center are auxiliary vertex-index fields used for facing math, not literal mesh geometry.

entries.name: DotProductVec3Int
entries.description: Same as DotProductVec3Short but on int (not short) components -- used by Light_ComputeShadeForFace's type-2 (point light) branch after converting the light-to-face displacement into ints.

entries.name: maybe_g_BitmapAtlasCache
entries.description: CORRECTS this entry's own prior 'static compiled-in dither table' claim from earlier the same session -- that was WRONG. DBSIM.EXE's total file size is 724,512 bytes; this address sits in the DATA section's second (huge, 2,245,120-byte) chunk, which is almost certainly BSS-style zero-fill reserved space, not literal file content, ruling out a ~16MB static table outright. Traced the real populator: FUN_00469d10 (a rectangle-packing cache-insertion routine, recurses into an overflow bank via param_1[0x200]/[0x201] when a 256-wide row is full) and its wrapper FUN_00469f38 (allocates a 20-byte-stride descriptor per inserted image via Cpp_VectorNew, matching the SAME stride as TSTexture4Poly's already-solved g_ActiveBitmapArray[1] frame-descriptor table). FUN_00469f38 is called from 7 places across totally unrelated subsystems -- Base_LoadResources, maybe_Ground_LoadFlatShapes, Weapons_LoadResourceTables, Terrain_BindTextureBank, and two weapon-effect loaders (bullets.cpp/beam.cpp equivalents, FUN_0040ade0/FUN_0040b6e0) -- each packing a freshly-loaded DBA's frames into this SAME shared atlas via FUN_0045cdd8 (DBA loader). CONCLUSION: this is a generic runtime bitmap/texture atlas cache shared by the whole engine (mechs, weapons, terrain, ground shapes), not a purpose-built dither table. TSSolidPoly_Render's (colorField<<16 | pixelCoord) addressing therefore means 'sample pixel pixelCoord from cached bitmap slot colorField', not 'look up a fixed dither pattern' -- meaning the earlier assumption that colorField=FrontColor (a 0-255 palette index) is now suspect; it more plausibly indexes a specific SMALL-N cached bitmap slot (a dither/shading swatch loaded once per theater), which would also explain why the naive 16MB address range is never actually exercised. WHICH atlas slot TSSolidPoly_Render's shading swatch specifically occupies, and who inserts it, was NOT found this session -- none of the 7 known FUN_00469f38 callers is an obvious 'load lighting dither pattern' site. This is now the real open question, distinct from and more specific than 'extract the dither table's raw bytes'.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 follow-up (correction pass), docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md

entries.name: g_CurrentShapeDbaContext
entries.description: RESOLVES handoff item #6/#8. Set once per shape instance by FUN_0042fa18 (maybe_TSShapeInstance_PrepareRenderContext) as `param_1 + 0x1a`, i.e. a pointer into the per-shape render object -- the exact same offset pattern as VSHELL's TSShapeInstance+0x26 bound-DBA field, just a different struct layout. g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] (== param_1+0x1e) is the shape's currently-bound DBA's 20-byte-stride frame-descriptor table -- THE SAME g_ActiveBitmapArray[1]-equivalent table TSTexture4Poly_Render indexes for UV corners. TSTexture4Poly_Render (FUN_00474e9c) uses `g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] + FrontColor*0x14` to fetch a frame descriptor, then reads its field+0x10 (the 5th int32, F4 -- previously found to be a 'texture-data pointer/handle' in the TSTexture4Poly descriptor) as the value shifted into the shared bitmap atlas (maybe_g_BitmapAtlasCache/DAT_004d4f88) bank selector for ordered-dither pixel fill.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 second follow-up (#6 continuation)

entries.name: maybe_TSShapeInstance_PrepareRenderContext
entries.description: Per-shape-instance render setup, called once before a shape's polys are drawn. Installs g_CurrentShapeDbaContext (DAT_006c60e8 = param_1+0x1a) and the surface-record base (_DAT_006c697a = param_1+0x61) that the poly renderers read from -- i.e. this is where 'the currently bound DBA' becomes visible to the poly-render layer for this shape, DBSIM's counterpart to VSHELL's TSShapeInstance_Render save/swap/restore step. Also does per-point LOD/pop rotation math (BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 per point) unrelated to texturing. Name is a guess from structural role, not from an RTTI/registry match.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 second follow-up (#6 continuation)

entries.name: maybe_TSGouraudOrSimilarPoly_Render
entries.description: Sibling poly-render function reusing g_CurrentShapeDbaContext/_DAT_006c697a exactly like TSSolidPoly_Render (same ColorIndexId*4 surface lookup, same FrontColor-indexes-frame-descriptor-table pattern feeding FUN_00468078 as the 4th arg). Not yet matched to a specific TSPoly subtype via the RTTI registry -- flagged here only because it shares and thus corroborates the g_CurrentShapeDbaContext mechanism.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 second follow-up (#6 continuation)

entries.name: TSTexture4Poly_Render
entries.description: CORRECTS this address's long-standing 'TSSolidPoly_Render' name, which was assigned by structural resemblance to VSHELL's TSSolidPoly_Render and was wrong. DBSIM's DTS type registry (g_TSObjectTypeRegistry, 004a63c8) settles it by construction: tag 0x0014000f -> ctor 0048e210 -> final vtable 004a5f24, whose slot +0x1c is this function. FrontColor really is a frame index into g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] here, because this is the TEXTURED poly type; the flat/solid type is TSSolidPoly_Render (00474db4) and works completely differently. Also the only reader of DAT_004a5b1c: when that is zero the poly is drawn in FUN_00468078 mode 0 (plain texture copy, no light term), which is how Bullet_Draw (0040a120) makes a projectile fullbright.

entries.name: TSSolidPoly_Render
entries.description: DBSIM's real flat/solid poly renderer, from the DTS type registry (tag 0x00140002 -> ctor 0048e06c -> final vtable 004a5ef8, slot +0x1c). Short: pick the front pair (surface[0]=Front, surface[1]=FrontLine) or the back pair (surface[2]/[3]) by TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest, skip when both have 0x14 in the top byte, then fill = Raster_ShadeRampRow(0x80)[Front] and line = same table [FrontLine], and hand both to the polygon fill (FUN_0048d518, which draws the fill then re-draws an outline in the line colour when the two differ). NO texture lookup, no frame index, and NO light term -- the shade byte is the literal 0x80. The surface value is a PALETTE INDEX, not a DBA frame: all 1517 plain TSSolidPoly surfaces across every retail .DTS carry a zero flag and a value inside 0-255. Contrast TSShadedPoly_Render (0047542c), which is the lit variant and is what nearly all mech and building geometry uses.

entries.name: TSShadedPoly_Render
entries.description: The lit flat-poly renderer, from the DTS type registry (tag 0x00140003 -> ctor 0048e2d4 -> final vtable 004a6000, slot +0x1c). Same surface-pair selection as TSSolidPoly_Render, then per face: shade = Light_ComputeShadeForFace(normal, center), fill = Raster_ShadeRampRow(0x80)[ Palette_ShadeRampLookup(Front, shade) ] and likewise for the line colour. Palette_ShadeRampLookup (00430e34) is the extra step the solid variant does not have: the surface value selects one of the active palette's shade ramps rather than a palette entry. This is the type nearly every mech and building surface actually is (1227 of APOCA's 1368 polys, 2049 of BASES_AN's).

entries.name: Palette_ShadeRampLookup
entries.description: Palette_ShadeRampLookup(value, shade): idx = value & 0xff, clamped to 0 when >= ActivePaletteObject+0x0c (the ramp count); reads ActivePaletteObject+0x10 as an array of 8-byte {int16* indices, int32 length} shade ramps and returns ramp[idx].indices[ Q8Multiply(shade, length) ], stepping back one when that lands on the end. So a value here is a RAMP NUMBER, not a colour: the ramps are per-material brightness sequences of palette indices. They live in the tail of each .DPL, after the 256 colour entries, and HercWorks.Core's DynamixPaletteTransformer does not parse them yet. Sole consumer found: TSShadedPoly_Render.

entries.name: Raster_ShadeRampRow
entries.description: Raster_ShadeRampRow(shade) = ((shade * (DAT_004d3d38 - 1) + DAT_004a08c8) & 0xffffff00) + DAT_004a09b0 -- the base of one 256-byte row of the theater's world<N>.rmp, indexable directly by palette index. DAT_004d3d38 is the ramp's shade-level count (32 in every retail file) and DAT_004a08c8 a whole number of 8192-byte depth slices set from the drawn object's distance by Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance. Both flat poly renderers call it with a literal 0x80, which with 32 levels is row 15.

entries.name: Raster_SetShadeRampDimensions
entries.description: Raster_SetShadeRampDimensions(shadeLevels, depthSlices) -> DAT_004d3d38 / DAT_004d3d3c, plus a 1/n reciprocal table. Sole caller is World_LoadTheater, which passes the world<N>.rmp header's own two int32s (32 and 12 in every retail file) straight through -- which is what fixes Raster_ShadeRampRow's row arithmetic.

entries.name: Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance
entries.description: Sets DAT_004a08c8, the depth-slice byte offset Raster_ShadeRampRow adds: zero for anything inside half the visibility range (DAT_004a08c4), otherwise Q16Multiply(t, depthSlices - 1) * shadeLevels * 256. That is the original's distance fog, and it is what the world<N>.rmp's 12 height slices are for -- an earlier pass recorded them as unused. Called per drawn object (FUN_0042876c, with the object's own distance), per terrain cell (Terrain_DrawCellQuad), and with zero from maybe_TSShapeInstance_PrepareRenderContext.

entries.name: g_TSObjectTypeRegistry
entries.description: DBSIM's DTS node factory, the counterpart of VSHELL's 0047f258: 12-byte entries of {uint32 tag, constructorFnPtr, nameStringPtr} where tag is the on-disk chunk marker. Use it rather than structural resemblance to identify a TSObject subclass -- doing so corrected two poly-render assignments (see TSSolidPoly_Render 00474db4 and TSTexture4Poly_Render 00474e9c).

entries.name: TSGroup_ReadFromFile
entries.description: TSGroup's vtable +0x0c load method (group struct is 0x28 bytes, built by the type registry's tag-0x00140014 ctor 0048e7a4). Reads four int16 counts into +0x20 indexes / +0x22 points / +0x24 surfaces / +0x26 polys, allocates +0x10 / +0x14 / +0x18 / +0x1c for each, then streams them. The surface array at +0x18 is surfaceCount int32s read RAW -- no conversion of any kind -- so the value a poly renderer indexes really is the file's own {int16 colour, int16 flag} pair packed into one int32.

entries.name: Bullet_Fire
entries.description: Bullet_Fire(missileId, muzzleWorldPoint, aimEulerTriple, ownerMech) -- spawns one travelling PROJ.DAT Type-2 Bullet from the effect pool DAT_004a9746. Copies the muzzle point to obj+0x26 (the frame's translation), stores the euler triple at obj+0x0c with components 0 and 2 displaced by (spread*2 & random) - spread from the BULLETS.DAT record's +0x0a, sets obj+0x52 = ownerMech->vtable+0x38 (travel speed) + PROJ.Speed, and plays the record's +0x08 sound. Returns the object so Bullet_FirePowered can add to it.

entries.name: Bullet_FirePowered
entries.description: Bullet_Fire plus two writes: obj+0x56 = the capacitor charge the shot was fired at (which scales both damage figures Q10 in Bullet_TickUpdate; zero leaves them at face value), and for missileId 9 only (the plasma cannon) obj+0x5b = ownerMech+0x1a4, the firing machine's selected target, which is what makes that one subtype home.

entries.name: Bullet_GetTypeRecord
entries.description: return DAT_004a977c + obj[0x41] * 14 -- the BULLETS.DAT record for a bullet's subtype id. The table is indexed by the PROJ.DAT record's subtype id, exactly as BEAM.DAT is.

entries.name: Bullet_LoadResources
entries.description: bullet.cpp's init (named by the BULLET.CPP string at 00498601). Loads dat\bullets into DAT_004a977c as a count plus that many 14-byte records, dts\bullets into the shape array DAT_004a9784, and dba\bullets into DAT_004a978a, packing its frames with BitmapArray_PackToAtlas; finally binds &DAT_004a978a as every bullet shape's +0x26 bound-DBA context.

entries.name: Bullet_HomingSteer
entries.description: The plasma round's guidance, and a steer of the object's EULER ANGLES rather than of a velocity: takes the bearing from the shot to obj+0x5b's position via Math_EulerToward, moves euler[0] and euler[2] toward it through Math_RateLimitedMoveToward capped at 0x280 per 125 ms, integrates over the tick, and clears the matrix-dirty flag at obj+0x32.

entries.name: Bullet_Draw
entries.description: The Bullet class's vtable slot 0. Sets DAT_004a5b1c = 0 for the duration of the call, which is what makes a projectile's textured polys draw unlit (see TSTexture4Poly_Render), installs the object's frame as the model transform, renders the shape instance at obj+0x34, and restores DAT_004a5b1c from DAT_004a5b20.

entries.name: Math_EulerToward
entries.description: Math_EulerToward(out, from, to), d = from - to: euler[2] = Math_Atan2Guarded(dx, dy) - 0x4000, euler[1] = 0, euler[0] = Math_Atan2Guarded(FastMagnitude2D(dx, dy), dz). Math_Atan2Guarded takes (x, y), so euler[2] is the ground bearing and euler[0] is an ELEVATION above the horizon, not a polar angle from +Z. The quarter-turn subtraction is because the simulation's forward axis is model Y. Same helper and same argument order as Math_HeadingToward.

entries.name: g_TSPolyUseAltPath_maybeDead
entries.description: CLOSES handoff #7. Read-only byte: 6 read sites (TSTexture4Poly_Render x5, maybe_TSGouraudOrSimilarPoly_Render x1), ZERO write sites found anywhere in DBSIM.EXE (checked via getReferencesTo across the whole binary). Read directly from the mapped image (ES2ReadDataValue.java): value is 0, in an initialized/file-backed (not BSS) DATA block -- i.e. this is a compile-time constant baked into the shipped exe, not a runtime-toggled setting, same pattern as VSHELL's DAT_00471890 (g_UseFlatPolyFallback) in the sibling ThreeSpace codebase. Since every reader branches on `==0`/`!=0` and the byte is permanently 0, the `==0` branch (the one solved in handoff #6: local_c/g_CurrentShapeDbaContext[1] frame lookup, FUN_00468078 dispatch) is the ONLY branch that ever executes in retail DBSIM.EXE. The `!=0` branch (local_28-based lookup, FUN_0048c848/FUN_0048cfec/FUN_0048d518) is dead code in the shipped game and does not need reverse engineering for a faithful Herculan.Engine implementation.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 third follow-up (#7 closure)

entries.name: g_TSSolidPolyRasterizerVariant_maybeDead
