entries.description: Same dead-constant pattern as g_TSPolyUseAltPath_maybeDead (0049f26c): single read site (TSTexture4Poly_Render, selects FUN_00468078 vs FUN_0046865c), zero write sites anywhere in DBSIM.EXE, value read directly from the image is 0 in an initialized DATA block. FUN_00468078 is therefore confirmed as the only rasterizer dispatch target ever taken in retail for TSTexture4Poly.
entries.source: flat-shaded lighting RE, 2026-08-14 third follow-up (#7 closure)

entries.name: Mech_LoadResources
entries.description: mechsys.cpp's resource-load sequence for the mech subsystem -- the mech-side twin of Base_LoadResources (00405fac). Resets the mech-type-slot table (memset &DAT_004a9d8c, 0xff, 0x55), then streams dat\mforms (string 'mforms' at 0049a46b, joined with the shared 'dat' folder-prefix helper FUN_00492ae0): reads a 2-byte record count into DAT_004a9dec, allocates that many 28-byte vector elements (Cpp_VectorNew(..., 0x1c, count, ...) -- 7 (x,y) int16 pairs/formation, matching Formation_GetSlotOffset's stride), stores the vector pointer into _DAT_004a9df0 (previously unwritten anywhere in disassembled code -- see that symbol's updated entry), then reads count*28 bytes straight from the file into the buffer. Afterwards loads the 7 mech texture groups (g_MechTextureGroupNames/g_MechTextureGroupSlots) via FUN_0045cdd8/FUN_00469f38, unrelated to formations. This function was never auto-disassembled by prior analysis passes (it sits directly after another function's RET with no call-graph edge Ghidra had found, so nothing walked into it) -- found by raw byte-scanning for the 'mforms' string's address as a PUSH-immediate operand, then manually disassembling/decompiling from there. Registered into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table via a thunk at 00420654 (FUN_00401d64(Mech_LoadResources, 2)), confirming it is live code the game runs, not dead weight.
entries.source: docs/formats/script-dat.md 2026-08-14 (mech formation spread, resolving the MFORMS.DAT load-site gap)

entries.name: g_MechFormationTable
entries.description: The mech formation-offset table pointer Formation_GetSlotOffset (004205cc) reads. Previously documented as having no write site anywhere in DBSIM.EXE -- that was true only of the code Ghidra had disassembled; Mech_LoadResources (0041fdb0), found 2026-08-14, writes it (`_DAT_004a9df0 = extraout_EAX_00;` immediately after Cpp_VectorNew allocates count*28 bytes and before the file's formation data is read into that buffer). Sits in a tight cluster of mech-subsystem globals: DAT_004a9de4 (mech name table, LoadNameList's target) / DAT_004a9dec (formation count) / this pointer / DAT_004a9df4 (cached object-pool handle, maybe_MechTypeSlot_Allocate).

entries.name: Mech_RegisterLoader
entries.description: Thunk that registers Mech_LoadResources (0041fdb0) into DBSIM's subsystem-loader table via FUN_00401d64(Mech_LoadResources, 2), then separately allocates the 7-slot mech-texture-group vector (Cpp_VectorNew(&g_MechTextureGroupSlots, 8, 8, 1, ...)). Found by raw dword-scanning DBSIM.EXE for Mech_LoadResources' address used as a PUSH-immediate operand (68 B0 FD 41 00); like Mech_LoadResources itself, was never auto-disassembled by prior analysis (sits right after another function's RET, no call-graph edge into it).

entries.name: RegisterSubsystemLoader
entries.description: Appends (funcPtr, id) to a global registration table (DAT_004a80d0, 6-byte entries: 4-byte function pointer + 2-byte id) at the slot indexed by a global counter (DAT_00497074) that it then increments. Confirms whatever registers itself here -- e.g. Mech_LoadResources via the 00420654 thunk -- is walked and invoked by DBSIM's generic subsystem-init driver rather than being dead code.

entries.name: s_mforms_0049a46b
entries.description: String literal 'mforms', mechsys.cpp's dat\MFORMS.DAT resource name (joined with the 'dat' folder prefix by FUN_00492ae0 in Mech_LoadResources). Sits in a literal pool alongside other mechsys.cpp string constants (difficulty names, texture-bank names) immediately followed by the source-file name 'mechsys.cpp' itself -- typical MSVC layout for a translation unit's string constants. No Reference object existed to this address before Mech_LoadResources was manually disassembled, because that function itself was never auto-analyzed; found by raw byte-scanning every initialized memory block for the literal ASCII bytes.

entries.name: ResourcePath_BuildFolderName
entries.description: The shared folder\name resource-path builder: ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(name, folder) writes 'folder\\name' into a shared static buffer (&DAT_006cbcae) via FUN_00492a84(name) + strcat('\\') + strcat(folder). Confirmed by tracing its two operands against known-good results (e.g. ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(hercName, "vue") and the folder-name pointer table at CockpitDpl_ResourceFolderNames). Matches Herculan.Engine.Content.GameContent's own folder\name resolution convention exactly -- this is DBSIM's side of the same addressing scheme.

entries.name: CockpitDpl_ResourceFolderNames
entries.description: A 12-entry constant pointer table of resource folder-name strings: dpl, gl, dmg, col, edg, dba, dci, dfn, gau, hfn, hdg, hba (0x4a0a14-0x4a0a43, pointing into a shared string pool at 0x4a0a44 that separately also holds wb/rb (fopen modes) and nam/dat/bnd/dts, those last four belonging to a different, not-yet-located table). Despite the name, this table is NOT cockpit-exclusive -- gau/dpl/dba/dci/dfn/hfn/hdg/hba are all mech-subsystem resource kinds reused site-wide; named for the first confirmed use found this session (index 0, "dpl", is PTR_DAT_004a0a14, used directly by the COCKPIT.DPL/IMPACTCP.DPL load calls -- see CockpitPaletteSingleton).

entries.name: CockpitPaletteSingleton
entries.description: Pointer to the currently-loaded cockpit-family DynamixPalette object. First loaded lazily (guarded by == 0) as the literal resource 'dpl\\cockpit' (s_cockpit_0049ae69 + CockpitDpl_ResourceFolderNames[0]="dpl", via ResourcePath_BuildFolderName + ClassItem_LoadTaggedResource) -- confirms DBSIM loads COCKPIT.DPL by a plain literal name, not a derived/offset one, and the real retail file ES2/VOL/simvol0/dpl/COCKPIT.DPL exists under exactly that name. Later swapped to 'dpl\\impactcp' (IMPACTCP.DPL, also a real retail file) as a second, smaller damage/impact-flash palette, whose colors get copied into a 24-entry sub-range of the global active display palette (Palette_InstallRange(0x2a, 0x18, ...)) rather than replacing CockpitPaletteSingleton wholesale. No index-remap/offset was found anywhere in this load path -- decoding a real .HB0 through COCKPIT.DPL with a direct, unmodified index lookup produces a correct, recognizable cockpit image (visually verified against APOCA.HB0/SAMSON.HB0), settling Milestone 8 Phase 0 Q1: the existing TextureViewerForm.PreferredPaletteFor("COCKPIT") heuristic is exactly right, not merely a plausible guess.

entries.name: Palette_InstallRange
entries.description: Palette_InstallRange(baseIndex, count, srcRgbaArray): copies count RGBA/RGB entries from srcRgbaArray into the global active display palette (*(DAT_0049b020+8) + baseIndex*4), then tracks the min/max dirty index range (DAT_0049b028/DAT_0049b02c) for a batched hardware palette update -- classic indexed-display-mode palette management. Used by the cockpit-view constructor to install the small IMPACTCP.DPL flash palette into a 24-entry sub-range (base 0x2a) of the shared 256-slot palette, distinct from CockpitPaletteSingleton's own local RGB array.

entries.name: CockpitViewInstance
entries.description: Singleton pointer to LocalPlayerMech's live cockpit/HUD view object (set once, guarded by == 0, in ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll/00431098). Directly embeds each GAU widget as a live sub-object at a fixed struct offset matching GAUFile.cs's own documented field order: a 10-slot weapon-button array at +0x1c (matches GAU's 10 weapon hardpoint slots), then single widgets at +0x1e1/+0x1e5/+0x1e9/+0x1ed/+0x1f1/+0x1f5/+0x1f9/+0x20b (chain/link/autotrack/energy-meter-family offsets), each paint-dispatched via its own vtable call. Read throughout the cockpit/HUD call graph (Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate, maybe_Sim_RenderFrame, Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets, Gau_RovingGunsightWidget, Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator, ~90 more sites) but never seen holding the HB0/HB2 background bitmap itself -- that field, and the exact function that blits the cockpit background art and composites the live 3D view into it, were not pinned to a specific offset/address this session (see docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md's open items). NOT the same object as maybe_MechInspectViewInstance (DAT_004d2544), a separate, much smaller (0x37-byte) object built by Sim_InitMissionSession right after this singleton is already in use.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_Ctor
entries.description: CORRECTS the earlier 'MechInspectView' hypothesis. This 0x37-byte object IS the player's own cockpit view manager (MECHVIEW.CPP): it holds the current view index at +0x14, the pending view command at +0x18, the CockpitView widget tree pointer at +0x1f, the owning mech at +0x29 and the herc model name at +0x2d, and it is what CockpitView_SetView/CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand drive. It is small because the heavy state lives in the CockpitView object it builds (see CockpitViewManager_LoadViews -> FUN_00431008 -> CockpitViewInstance). Also the site of CockpitPaletteSingleton's first (singleton-guarded) load of dpl\\cockpit.

entries.name: CockpitViewManager_LoadViews
entries.description: The whole cockpit bring-up, in order: (1) loads vue\\<herc> -- int32 viewCount then viewCount x 32-byte records {int x0,y0,x1,y1, cx, cy, canvasOriginX, canvasOriginY}, all coordinates shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift; every retail .VUE has viewCount=4; (2) allocates 4 slots for canopy bitmaps, 4 x 0x204 clip-region blocks and 4 span tables; (3) per view i, calls CockpitClipRegions_Load on ed<i>/hd<i> and ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans on the result, and (unless CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand) CockpitCanopy_LoadViewBitmap for db<i>/hb<i>; (4) builds the CockpitView widget object (FUN_00431008 -> ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll, which sets CockpitViewInstance) and Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets; (5) THE PER-HERC COCKPIT COLOUR SCHEME: Palette_InstallRange(0x2a, 0x18, COCKPIT.DPL.entries + (schemeIdx*0x18 + 0x20)*4), i.e. live palette slots 42..65 are overwritten with COCKPIT.DPL entries [32 + 24*schemeIdx .. +24), where schemeIdx = mechTypeRecord+0x52 = offset 80 of simvol0/dat/<MECH>.DAT (HercSimDat.Unk80_ValHudId). Retail values are a 0-8 permutation: APOCA 0, COLOSSUS 1, SAMSON 2, MAVERICK 3, OGRE 4, OUTLAW 5, RAPTOR2 6, RAZOR 7, TOMAHAWK 8, so the nine 24-entry schemes fill COCKPIT.DPL entries 32..247. This matches the independently measured retail screenshots exactly (APOCA renders canopy index i as COCKPIT.DPL[i-10] => base 32; COLOSSUS as COCKPIT.DPL[i+14] => base 56) and explains why every WORLD<n>.DPL parks exactly slots 42-65 at filler green. (6) Repeats the same install with IMPACTCP.DPL into the secondary palette object DAT_0049aef8 for the damage flash.

entries.name: CockpitViewManagerInstance
entries.description: Result of CockpitViewManager_Ctor, constructed in Sim_InitMissionSession. The player's cockpit view-state object (current view, pending view command, the 4 canopy bitmaps / clip blocks / span tables, and the CockpitView widget tree). Distinct from, and the owner of, CockpitViewInstance (DAT_0049b088).

entries.name: Resource_Load
entries.description: Resource_Load(path): wraps a folder\name string into a temporary object and calls ClassItem_LoadResource(obj, 0), returning the loaded resource handle. The single entry point every HUD sprite bank, panel and cursor load goes through after ResourcePath_BuildFolderName builds the path.

entries.name: Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges
entries.description: Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges(from, to, rampCount, levels, out): linearly interpolates palette index RANGES, not colours. Each of from/to/out is an array of (int16 start, int16 count) pairs; for each of rampCount ramps it emits `levels` interpolated ranges in 8.8 fixed point, with the final step forced exactly to the `to` endpoint. Called twice by maybe_World_LoadTheater with endpoint tables read from WORLD<n>.WLD. WORLD0 expands to 11 ramps x 16 levels, all ranges within indices 96-239 (terrain shading only; no cockpit equivalent found).

entries.name: Palette_CycleAnimatedRanges
entries.description: Per-frame animated palette cycling. Walks 5 fixed slots (DAT_004cfde8 descriptors, DAT_004cfdfc next-due times, DAT_004cfe10 rotation offsets); when a slot's due time passes it rotates that slot's palette sub-range by one entry and reinstalls it via Palette_InstallRange. Keyed off Time_GetCoarseTicks. Blinking cockpit/console lights.

OPEN LEAD for the unresolved cockpit canopy shading. Copies the live 256-entry palette into two scratch buffers, halves the RGB of two 16-entry spans, and installs them via Palette_InstallRange at base 0x20 (32) and base 0x40 (64) -- both inside the canopy art's own 42-71 index band. Candidate for the lighting-state mechanism that CockpitArt.PaletteIndexOffset currently stands in for. Callers not yet traced.

entries.name: HudHeadingTape_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the HUD heading tick tape. Lazily loads the `hudhtick` sprite bank into DAT_0049be70, selecting folder "hba" or "dba" off DAT_004d25f0 (the 640-wide vs 320-wide video mode flag).

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the multi-function display. Lazily loads three sprite banks -- `mfd` (DAT_0049cbcc), `mfd_dmg` (DAT_0049cbd4) and `radar` -- each selecting folder "hba"/"dba" off DAT_004d25f0.

entries.name: WeaponGauge_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for a weapon hardpoint gauge. Lazily loads the `pweapons` (DAT_0049c4d0) and `wpn_dmg` (DAT_0049c4d4) sprite banks, folder selected off DAT_004d25f0, and builds a 2-row animation frame table into _DAT_004d1adc.

entries.name: ThrottleGauge_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the throttle slider gauge. Lazily loads the `throttle` sprite bank into DAT_0049cfc4, folder selected by DAT_004d25bb == 3 choosing "hba" over "dba". Reads CockpitViewInstance and its own .GAU track rect. Bank frame 0 is a 2px tick, frame 1 the knob.

entries.name: maybe_SysButtonPair_Ctor
entries.description: Lazily loads the `sysbuttn` sprite bank into DAT_0049b63c (folder by DAT_004d25bb == 3), then constructs two widgets whose coordinates are built as `value << (DAT_004d25be & 0x1f)` on X and `<< (DAT_004d25c0 & 0x1f)` on Y -- the per-axis resolution shift that makes .GAU coordinates 320-wide-space and doubles them for 640-wide.

entries.name: HddMarker_Ctor
entries.description: One of the command display map's 140 marker gadgets. Lazily loads the `icons` sprite bank into DAT_0049d6b4, folder selected by VideoMode_UseHiResPanels == 3.

entries.name: maybe_CockpitFontsAndCorners_Init
entries.description: Loads the cockpit's .DFN/.HFN font set (title, cpylw, active, pushed, inactive, green6x8, red6x8) with folder chosen by DAT_004d25bb == 3 selecting "hfn" over "dfn", then the `corners` sprite bank -- hardcoded to "dba", and indeed no hba\CORNERS.HBA exists -- and finally the `alert` bank via the DAT_004d25f0 idiom.

entries.name: HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames
entries.description: HDDGauge frame loader (PHDD.CPP). Builds the resource name `pilot<n>` with _itoa, loads its .OFS animation-offset table (27 entries), then loads the matching sprite bank from folder "dba". Emits the literal errors "HDDGauge::Couldn't load anim offset" / "...bitmap array".

entries.name: VideoMode_UseHiResBanks
entries.description: Nonzero selects the 640-wide `hba` sprite banks, zero selects the 320-wide `dba` ones. Read directly by every HUD bank constructor. A parallel flag DAT_004d25bb == 3 drives the same choice for sysbuttn/throttle/icons and for .hfn over .dfn.

entries.name: VideoMode_XCoordShift
entries.description: Per-axis resolution shift for hardcoded widget coordinates: the exe writes them as `value << (VideoMode_XCoordShift & 0x1f)`. 0 in the 320-wide mode, 1 in the 640-wide one -- the mechanism behind Herculan.Engine's CockpitArt.GauToPixelScale = 2. DAT_004d25c0 is the Y counterpart.

entries.name: VideoMode_YCoordShift
entries.description: Y-axis counterpart of VideoMode_XCoordShift.

entries.name: HudColorTable
entries.description: 27 int16 palette indices, loaded from dat\COLORS.DAT (54-byte payload). HUD data files carry small logical colour ids rather than palette indices; those are resolved through this table once at load time, in place (arr[i] = table[arr[i]]). Read at 16 distinct offsets by ~60 functions; nothing in the image writes the address with an immediate because it is filled from the file. Verified: HDD ids 19/9/15/12 resolve to palette 16/10/13/14 = black/red/yellow/green, matching retail HDD screenshots.

entries.name: HudColorTable_Get
entries.description: Returns HudColorTable[DAT_0049b040[i]] -- resolves a logical colour id held in an initialised id array to a palette index.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_Ctor
entries.description: LEDBarGraph constructor: calls LedBarGraph_CtorBase then installs vtable PTR_FUN_0049bd30.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_CtorBase
entries.description: LedBarGraph_CtorBase(obj, rect, range): precomputes span = (end - start) * 0x10000 / range at field 0x14, start at 0x18, end at 0x1c, and seeds the current fill position at 0x20 from the sign of span -- a negative span fills from the far end back, which is how the H and V variants share one implementation.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_PaintToValue
entries.description: Paints the bar for a 16.16 fixed-point value: fills to start + (value * span >> 16) via LedBarGraph_FillPinstripe, then installs field 0x24 as the draw colour and covers the remainder.

entries.name: LedBarGraph_FillPinstripe
entries.description: Fills the lit span of an LED bar. Walks the x range twice -- once over even columns, once over odd -- drawing a full-height line each step, with field 0x2c as the even-column colour and 0x30 as the odd. Two near-identical shades interleaved at one pixel read as a single shaded fill rather than two colours.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Ctor
entries.description: The real shield meter, called only by Gau_ShieldDisplayWidget (00432454) with .GAU offset 0x268=616. NOT an LED bar -- it loads no sprite bank and instead builds a 0x40-byte child per shield facing via FUN_00444aec plus a text label via FUN_004387ac/FUN_00438884 (the same generic label constructors the .DFN font consumers use). That matches retail: nested green concentric boxes with a numeric readout above and below. The .GAU block at 616 is a zero header rect followed by four 16-byte rects at 632/648/664/680, all shifted by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift in FUN_00444b9c. Distinct from EnergyPoolGauge_Ctor (00444d5c), which the earlier maybe_ShieldsGauge_Ctor name wrongly claimed was this widget.

entries.name: EnergyPoolGauge_Ctor
entries.description: CORRECTS the earlier maybe_ShieldsGauge_Ctor name. This is the Master Energy Pool meter (reactor charge), not the shield meter. Called only by Gau_EnergyMeterWidget (004323e0) with .GAU offset 0x224=548, whose child rect is at 564 -- in OUTLAW.GAU that rect is (91,198)-(115,205), directly under the TRACK button, which is where retail draws the blue pinstripe bar. Builds an LED bar with value range 0x400, writing HudColorTable ids 6 and 5 into the pinstripe colour fields 0x2c/0x30 and id 19 into the remainder colour 0x24; against the corrected palette those resolve to palette indices 98/97/16 = (0,116,204), (0,40,160), (0,0,0), i.e. blue -- the old note's 'ids resolve to two greys and black' was computed against the superseded palette model. Class identity is from the binary's own class-name table, which pairs 'EnergyPoolGauge' immediately with 'LEDBarGraphV' (file offset 280429) and 'ShieldsGauge' with 'ShieldsSelectGadget' (279148): the LED bar class is EnergyPoolGauge, and ShieldsGauge is a different class entirely (see ShieldsGauge_Ctor).

entries.name: PaperDoll_Load
entries.description: pdamage.cpp .PDG loader. Reads 3 views, each an origin/size pair plus a vector of 0x1c-byte regions {int index, PixelPoint topLeft, PixelPoint bottomRight, int colorId, int spacer}; resolves each region's colorId through HudColorTable in place and shifts its coordinates by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift, with bottomRight additionally +1 in the 640-wide mode. Matches HercWorks.Core's PaperDollGraphic field-for-field, identifying its ViewRegion.Unk_val at offset 0x14 as the colour id.

entries.name: CockpitCanopy_LoadViewBitmap
entries.description: MECHVIEW.CPP:0x12e. THE previously-unlocated .HB0/.HB1/.HB2 (.DB0/.DB1/.DB2) load site. No literal 'hb0' string exists because the folder name is built at runtime: it copies the global folder literal 'dba' (or 'hba' when VideoMode_UseHiResPanels==3) into a stack buffer and overwrites index 2 with an ASCII digit via _itoa, giving db0/db1/db2 or hb0/hb1/hb2, then ResourcePath_BuildFolderName(hercName, buf) + ClassItem_LoadResource. View->file map: fileIdx = viewIdx>2 ? viewIdx-1 : viewIdx, so views 0,1,2,3 -> files 0,1,2,2 and view 4 loads nothing; after loading file 2 the same handle is also stored in slot 3, i.e. views 2 and 3 share one bitmap (view 3 is drawn horizontally mirrored, see CockpitView_SetView). Result handles land in CockpitViewManager+8[viewIdx]. The CockpitLayoutMode==1 branch increments byte 2 of the SHARED global 'dba' literal (MOV ECX,[0x4a0a28]; INC byte ptr [ECX+2]) rather than the local buffer -- verified in raw disassembly at 00429d3e; the follow-on load still uses the unmodified local buffer, so that branch loads db0 twice and corrupts the global folder name. Treat CockpitLayoutMode==1 as an unused/buggy path.

entries.name: CockpitCanopy_FreeViewBitmap
entries.description: Releases the canopy bitmap handle for one view and nulls its slot; when freeing view 2 it also nulls slot 3, which shares the same handle. Only called when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand (DAT_004d2704) is set, i.e. the low-memory mode that loads and frees canopy art per view switch instead of keeping all four resident.

entries.name: CockpitView_ApplyViewState
entries.description: Installs one view's state into the global render context (DAT_006c5ff4): copies that view's 0x204-byte clip-region block (CockpitViewManager+0xc + viewIdx*0x204, filled by CockpitClipRegions_Load) into ctx+4..ctx+0x208, points ActiveScanlineClipSpans at the view's prebuilt per-scanline span table (CockpitViewManager+0x10[viewIdx]), and copies the view's six .VUE ints into ctx[0x84..0x89]. The .VUE record's last two ints are the view's origin inside the cockpit canvas and go to DAT_004cfa24/28 (or VideoMode_X/YCoordShift-space DAT_004d25da/de in CockpitLayoutMode 2). View 4 instead installs the default full-screen clip block at DAT_004cfb1c and hides the cockpit widgets -- it is the external/no-cockpit view.

entries.name: CockpitView_SetView
entries.description: Switches the cockpit to view 0-4. Calls CockpitView_ApplyViewState, then blits the view's full-screen canopy bitmap once via Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, {0,0}, flags) with flags = 2 (horizontal mirror) for view 3 and 0 otherwise -- this is where the side view's single authored bitmap is flipped for the opposite side. Finally repaints every cockpit widget (FUN_004316c0). The canopy is NOT redrawn per frame: it is blitted once per view change and the 3D scene is then rasterized over it, clipped to ActiveScanlineClipSpans. In CockpitLayoutMode 1 view 0 additionally blits slot 1 at y+0xc5.

entries.name: CockpitView_QueueViewCommand
entries.description: Latches a pending view-change command (field +0x18) from an input action, guarded by the current view (field +0x14). Consumed by CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand.

entries.name: CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand
entries.description: Executes the pending view command. Command 4 selects view 2 and adds -0x3600 to the pilot view yaw; command 5 selects view 3 and adds +0x3600; command 6 returns to view 0 and undoes the yaw. 0x3600/0x10000 of a turn = ~76 degrees, i.e. views 2 and 3 are the two 'glance sideways' views. Command 2 selects view 4 (external).

entries.name: CockpitClipRegions_Load
entries.description: Parser for the per-view .ED0-.ED3 / .HD0-.HD3 files (folder name built by overwriting index 2 of the 'edg'/'hdg' literals with a digit). Layout after the 9-byte VOL prefix: int16 rectCount, rectCount x {int16 y0, y1, x0, x1}; then int16 spanBlockCount, and per block {int16 firstRow, int16 rowCount, rowCount x {int16 xStart, int16 xEnd}}. Rects become type-0 region objects, span blocks type-2. Coordinates are shifted by the caller's (xShift,yShift) pair, which is (0,0) for the .HD* hi-res set and VideoMode_X/YCoordShift for the .DB*-era .ED* set. Output is a 0x204-byte block (int count + up to 128 region pointers). APOCA.HD0 reads cleanly: one full-width rect for rows 0-76 then a 235-row span block from row 77 whose spans narrow inward (the canopy frame). APOCA.HD1 is empty (rectCount=0, blockCount=0), which is why view 1 shows no 3D at all.

entries.name: ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans
entries.description: Flattens a loaded region list (rects + span blocks from CockpitClipRegions_Load) into a per-scanline span table of `rowCount` rows (0xf0 << VideoMode_YCoordShift, i.e. 240 or 480). Each row is {int spanCount, ptr to spanCount x {int start, int length}}, sorted by start. Stores the result in ActiveScanlineClipSpans. This -- not any colour key -- is the cockpit's 3D-viewport cutout mechanism.

entries.name: ActiveScanlineClipSpans
entries.description: Pointer to the current view's per-scanline visible-span table (built by ClipRegions_BuildScanlineSpans). The polygon rasterizer at 00468310 indexes it per row (row*8 -> {spanCount, spanPtr}) and skips rows whose span count is zero, so the 3D scene only ever paints through the canopy's cut-out. Set to 0 for view 4 (no cockpit, unclipped full screen).

entries.name: Bitmap_Blit
entries.description: Bitmap_Blit(bitmap, {int x, int y}, flags) -- the engine-wide sprite/background blit. flags bit 1 (value 2) mirrors horizontally, bit 0 (value 1) flips vertically, 3 does both; confirmed at the reticle corner-bracket draw (0044401d..0044403a) which draws one corner sprite four times with flags 0/2/1/3, offsetting x by the bitmap's width field (+6) for flag 2 and y by its height field (+4) for flag 1. Used with flags=2 to produce the cockpit's opposite side view from the single authored side bitmap.

entries.name: Palette_LoadAndActivate
entries.description: Loads a .DPL by path and makes it THE active palette object (ActivePaletteObject / DAT_0049b020). World_LoadTheater calls it with dpl\\world<N>, so the live 256-slot palette IS the theater palette in its entirety -- it is not a merge of COCKPIT.DPL and WORLD<N>.DPL. The only cockpit-owned slots are 42..65, overwritten afterwards by the per-herc scheme install in CockpitViewManager_LoadViews.

entries.name: Palette_SetActive
entries.description: Swaps ActivePaletteObject and returns the previous one. Used to temporarily retarget Palette_InstallRange at the secondary impact palette (DAT_0049aef8) without disturbing the live one.

entries.name: Palette_FlushDirtyRange
entries.description: Pushes the accumulated dirty index range to the display and clears it; if the active palette object changed since the last flush it uploads the whole palette instead.

entries.name: Palette_BeginCrossFade
entries.description: Palette_BeginCrossFade(fromPalette, toPalette, durationTicks): precomputes per-channel 8.8 deltas into DAT_004cfe28/004d0028/004d0228 for a timed fade between two palette objects (either endpoint may be null, meaning fade to/from black). Driven per frame by Palette_StepCrossFade. This is how the impact/damage flash is applied on top of the cockpit's own colour scheme.

entries.name: Palette_StepCrossFade
entries.description: Advances the Palette_BeginCrossFade fade one frame, writing interpolated RGB straight into the live palette and extending the dirty range. Returns remaining ticks, 0 when finished.

entries.name: Palette_InterpolateColours
entries.description: Colour-space sibling of Palette_InterpolateIndexRanges: interpolates rampCount colour pairs across `levels` steps, emitting 0x01RRGGBB-style entries. Distinct from the index-range remapper used for terrain shading.

entries.name: ActivePaletteObject
entries.description: The live palette object. Field +8 is its 256 x 4-byte entry array (the array every Palette_* helper indexes). Installed by Palette_LoadAndActivate from dpl\\world<N>; DAT_0049b028/0x2c/0x30 are its dirty min/max/valid triple and DAT_0049b024 the last-uploaded object.

entries.name: VideoMode_Configure
entries.description: Sets the whole video-mode global block from a mode byte read out of the prefs file. Mode 0: VideoMode_UseHiResPanels=0, UseHiResBanks=0, viewport 320x240, canvas 320x480, coord shifts 0. Mode 1: UseHiResPanels=3, UseHiResBanks=0, viewport 640x480, canvas 640x960, shifts 1. Mode 2: as mode 1 but UseHiResBanks=1. So UseHiResPanels==3 selects .HFN/.HBA/.HB<n> art while UseHiResBanks separately selects the hi-res HUD sprite banks -- which is why the two idioms documented in cockpit-hud.md differ.

entries.name: VideoMode_UseHiResPanels
entries.description: 0 or 3. When 3 the engine loads the 640-wide art set: .HFN fonts, hba\\ sprite banks, and the hb0/hb1/hb2 canopy folders (via CockpitCanopy_LoadViewBitmap) plus the hd0-hd3 clip files. Set by VideoMode_Configure.

entries.name: maybe_CockpitLayoutMode
entries.description: Alternate cockpit layout selector, 0 by default. Value 1 makes view 0 also blit the view-1 (heads-down) bitmap at y+0xc5 and disables view 1 as a standalone view -- but its second load reuses the unmodified local folder buffer and corrupts the global 'dba' literal, so it looks like dead/buggy code. Value 2 routes blits through the windowed variant (Bitmap_BlitClipped) and moves the view origin into DAT_004d25da/de. Never observed written anywhere in the image.

entries.name: CockpitCanvasWidth
entries.description: Width of the virtual cockpit canvas the .GAU widget rects are authored in: 320 in mode 0, 640 in modes 1/2 (paired with CockpitCanvasHeight at 004d25d6 = 480 / 960). The canvas is TALLER than the 3D viewport (004d25c2/c6 = 320x240 / 640x480) because view 1's .VUE origin is (0,237): canvas rows 0-239 are the forward cockpit and rows 237-476 are the heads-down display. Views 2 and 3 sit at canvas x +320 and -320. This is why .GAU's addressable Y range runs past 240.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_FacingCtor
entries.description: Builds one 0x40-byte shield-facing child for ShieldsGauge_Ctor, one per facing, over the .GAU rects at 632 and 648. Draws no geometry: its paint slot (FUN_00444b5c) only tests visibility. The nested concentric rings the retail meter shows are painted into the herc's own canopy art in palette indices 66-71; the gauge animates them by rewriting those six palette slots (ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette).

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette
entries.description: Computes the shield meter's six ring colours and installs them at palette index 0x42 (66-71). Per facing (charge at +0xb5 and +0xb9) three rings light in turn: ring 1 from 0, ring 2 from 0x100 at twice the rate, ring 3 from 0x180 at four times, each as base * t >> 10 in Q10. Above 0x400 the same three tracks run again over base + (bright - base) * t. Colour immediates at 0049c9cb..0049c9d0: base RGB6 (25,59,23), bright (59,59,23). Install order is the stack layout, so 66-68 are the first facing outermost-first and 69-71 the second. At the nominal half charge all six resolve to RGB (48,116,44), matching the retail screenshot's meter.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_UpdateReadouts
entries.description: Fills ShieldsGauge's two numeric labels (object +0xc4 and +0xc8) from the fore/aft balance at +0xbd: itoa(balance * 200 >> 10) and its complement out of 200. An even split reads 100 and 100, which is what retail shows.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_Ctor
entries.description: One weapon row's select gadget, built by FUN_00440a68 from the .GAU hardpoint rect. Lays out two sub-rects relative to that rect, mirrored from the right edge for a right-column slot: the hardpoint state box at +6..+9 GAU x, +0..+7 y (PWEAPONS frames 4-6, 6x14 device), and the weapon-name label at +11..+35 x, +0..+5 y. Painted by WeaponSelectGadget_Paint.

entries.name: WeaponSelectGadget_Paint
entries.description: Paints one weapon row: the row plate from PWEAPONS frame 0 (selected) or 1 (not) at the .GAU rect minus one device pixel on both axes, the hardpoint state box from PWEAPONS frames 4/5/6 by state, the weapon name from the gauge's own 12-char buffer (+0xb1), and the round count. Text colour is the font: ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE / [11] GRAY for the name, [13] GREEN / [11] GRAY for the count; the label's field 0x1d is the background colour it paints first (0x2e here).

entries.name: ConsoleButton_Paint
entries.description: Paints the chain/link/auto-track console buttons: plate from PWEAPONS frames 2 + state (frame 2 unlit, solid palette index 34 = the retail blue at RGB (77,77,182); frame 3 lit, index 14 green) blitted at the widget's own rect, then the caption. The chain button's caption comes from the three-entry Roman-numeral table at 0049c71c ('I', 'II', 'III'), a literal .rdata table unrelated to the string file. LINK and TRACK are not fixed the same way: both read ConsoleButtonCaptions (004d13d0) indexed by the widget's own kind field (param_1[10]: 1=LINK, 2=TRACK), which SimStrings_LoadAll fills from STRINGS0.STR group 4. Caption font is ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE when unlit, [12] DARK when lit.

entries.name: ChainCountCaptions
entries.description: Three 4-byte inline strings 'I', 'II', 'III' indexed by chain count, read by ConsoleButton_Paint.

entries.name: ConsoleButtonCaptions
entries.description: 4-entry .bss pointer array (STRINGS0.STR group 4: 'I', 'LINK', 'TRACK', ''), filled by SimStrings_LoadAll and read by ConsoleButton_Paint, indexed by the console button's own kind field. Entry 0 ('I') is unused by that reader -- the chain button gets its numerals from the separate ChainCountCaptions table instead.

entries.name: ShieldRingColors
entries.description: Six bytes of 6-bit colour channels for the shield meter's ring ramp: base R,G,B at +0..+2 = (25,59,23) and bright R,G,B at +3..+5 = (59,59,23). Read only by ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette. Channel order matches the .DPL entry layout, byte 0 = R.

entries.name: CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand
entries.description: When non-zero, canopy view bitmaps are loaded on entering a view and freed on leaving it instead of all being loaded up front in CockpitViewManager_LoadViews. A low-memory path.

entries.name: MfdGau_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: Coordinate-shifts the MFD's .GAU block at offset 728 in place before MfdDisplay_Ctor reads it: 13 consecutive rects from int index 4 (file offset 744), then the panel rect at int index 0x38 (file offset 952). The 13 rects are zero in all nine retail .GAU files and no constructor reads them; only the panel rect is live. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_SetMode
entries.description: Switches the MFD to a screen (0-5, = F-key - 1). Lights button `mode` and unlights the previous via their +0x40 flag, stores the mode at +0xc1, then walks the 6x13 visibility table at 0049cbd8 for buttons 6-12 showing/hiding each. Gau_MfdPanelWidget calls it with 3 (SCANNER) at build time, which is what a cockpit powers up on. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Repaint
entries.description: Full MFD repaint, in order: mode buttons 0-5, the screen background, all visible buttons 0-12, the current screen's paint slot, then the title from DAT_004d13e0[mode]. Background frame is a bare switch on the mode over the `mfd` bank's frame-pointer array: modes 0/1/4 take element 1, mode 3 element 2, modes 2/5 take literal 0 and skip the blit. Frame 0 is never used as a background. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_Update
entries.description: MFD per-frame update. Dispatches the current screen's update slot via +0xcd + mode*4, refreshes the title for modes 2 and 5, and when a transmission is active draws the speaking pilot's frames at inset+(0x14,0) and fills the message label at +0x329. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButton_OnClick
entries.description: MFD button dispatch: finds the clicked button's index in the +0x18 array, then switches on it. Indices 0-5 call MfdDisplay_SetMode(i) -- this is what makes mode index = F-key - 1. Index 11 (PASS) and 12 (ACTIVE) set the radar-mode flag at CockpitViewInstance+0x203's +0x96 to 0/1 and swap which of the two lights. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButton_SetCaption
entries.description: Sets one MFD button's caption from its index at +0x28: for index < 6 it composes "F1"-"F6" on the stack from the two-byte literal at 0049cea3 ("Fx") with '1'+index written over the second byte -- the six mode captions are not stored as strings. For index >= 6 it takes DAT_004d13e0[index] from STRINGS0.STR group 5. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButton_Repaint
entries.description: Repaints one MFD button and re-fonts its caption: buttons 0-5 and 11-12 take ColorSchemePanels[12] DARK when the +0x40 lit flag is set and [10] WHITE when clear, which is why the selected F-key reads dark-on-green. Caption text is resolved the same way as MfdButton_SetCaption. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdFlashCommScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's FLASH COMM screen (mode 1). Builds six order rows: rect inset+(2,0xd)-(0x60,0x3a) GAU with the top-left nudged in and bottom-right out by 1<<XCoordShift, stepping 7<<YCoordShift per row. Font ColorSchemePanels[1] CPGREEN with [2] CPRED as the alternate at +0x21, background colour id 0x11, text margin 2<<XCoordShift. Rows list the first six of STRINGS0.STR group 0's 18 squadmate orders. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdMapScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's NAV MAP screen (mode 2). Takes the whole inset rect, allocates a 0x239-byte offscreen render target and centres it at -((x1-x0)>>1), -((y1-y0)>>1). No labels and no aux buttons. Its paint (004405e4) floods the rect with COLORS.DAT id 19 (black) before rasterizing terrain, which is why MfdDisplay_Repaint blits no chrome for this mode. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's SCANNER screen (mode 3), the largest of the six at 0x524 bytes. Builds the plot geometry (dish at inset+(0x26,1), centre at inset+(0x41,0x1c), plot radius 0x19 GAU), the 100-entry contact vector at +0x68 and the four corner readouts. Binds MFD bank frames 14 (dish) and 15 (turret wedge). Range comes from MfdScannerRanges 004d1cf4 = 50000/100000/200000 world units (300/600/1200 m at 1000 units = 6 m) indexed by the zoom field at MfdDisplay+0xc5, default 2. The `radar` bank's 10-frame sweep is NOT this screen's -- MfdDisplay_Update plays it over the same dish on a switch to mode 3. See docs/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: HudScanner_Paint
entries.description: The front window's floating scanner repeater. Belongs to the GUNSIGHT complex, not the MFD: Gunsight_Paint and Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint reach it through the one-line FUN_0043e0ec after the child loop. Takes the SCANNER screen object (CockpitView+0x1ed's +0xd9) and the widget's own point at +0x10b (.GAU offset 1196), calls MfdRadarScreen_Update to rebuild the shared contact list, and RETURNS IMMEDIATELY when that screen is the display's current one -- so it and the F4 screen are never on screen together. Draws a 0x2e-unit red circle outline (colour id 9), the turret arc as two lines at twist +/- 0x2000, MFD frame 18 at the centre, each contact as a radius-2 black disc with a radius-1 coloured core, and MFD frame 16 over the selection. Its plot scale divides by the half-size (46 device px), not by the screen's 0x19. See docs/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: Gunsight_PaintHudScanner
entries.description: One line: HudScanner_Paint(scannerScreen, gunsight+0x10b). The gunsight complex's only reference to the MFD's scanner screen.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Update
entries.description: Rebuilds the SCANNER screen's contact list from the live object list: skips the viewing machine, anything dead (+0x99/+0xa4), a group still awaiting deployment (group+0x14), an invulnerable structure type (class 1 with BASES.DAT +0x1e), a Cybrid not currently radar-visible (+0x95), and anything past the current display range on the ground plane. Survivors are rotated by Math_BuildRotation2D(-heading) and stored as (x, -y) with a colour id per class and side, so the plot is hull-relative nose-up. Also mirrors mech+0x96 into +0x34 and re-presses PASS or ACTIVE when it changed. Its hostile branch's blinking obj+0x1aa last-known-position marker is DEAD CODE: every constructor sets obj+0xa7 = 1 and nothing clears it. See docs/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: MfdRadarScreen_Paint
entries.description: Paints the SCANNER screen: floods the dish rect with raw palette index 0x11, blits MFD frame 15 rotated about its own corner at the plot centre by turretTwist - 0x6000, covers it with frame 14, draws the passive-range ring (ellipse outline, colour id 11) only when passive and 140000 < range, then frame 17 (reference line), frame 18 (player marker), each contact as a 2x2 fill, frame 16 over the selected target, and the four RNG:/TRG: readouts as right-aligned zero-padded four-character fields. See docs/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: MfdDisplay_CycleScannerRange
entries.description: The SCANNER screen's RANGE button: steps MfdDisplay+0xc5 and wraps at 3, then FUN_00446fec installs MfdScannerRanges[index] at MfdDisplay+0xbd. Stepping outwards from the default index 2 means the first press goes from 1200 m to 300 m.

entries.name: MfdMissileViewScreen_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for the MFD's MISSILE CAM screen (mode 5), matching the MFDMissileView class name in DBSIM's string table. Like the nav map it gets no background chrome from MfdDisplay_Repaint, filling the screen with its own camera image. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: Label_SetRect
entries.description: Anchors a HUD text label: stores the caller's rect at label+1..4 and computes the text anchor. Horizontal depends on the flags argument -- 2 = centre ((x1-x0)/2 + x0 + margin[0]), 4 = right (x1 - margin[0]), otherwise left (x0 + margin[0]). Vertical has no flag at all: anchorY = ((y1-y0)>>1) + y0 + (inkHeight>>1) + margin[2] + 1, where inkHeight is font+0x16 (file offset 0x1a, 11 for .HFN) and NOT the cell height at font+0xa. All of it is integer arithmetic. margin is the caller's short[4]. Paired with Label_SetText. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: Label_SetText
entries.description: Sets a HUD label's text and places it against the anchor Label_SetRect computed. Measures the run and subtracts 1<<XCoordShift (dropping the trailing advance), then places left/centre/right per the same flags. Vertical position is the stored anchor; HudFont_DrawGlyph then draws each glyph with its top row at anchor - inkHeight, so the inked band is what gets centred in the rect and the remaining cell rows hang below. Fills the label's background first when its +0x1d colour id is non-zero. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: SimStrings_LoadAll
entries.description: Opens one str\*.STR file and registers its string groups into .bss pointer arrays, in strict file order -- 41 registrations for STRINGS0.STR, so a group's index is its position in this sequence. The sixth (13 entries into DAT_004d13e0) is the MFD's caption/title table. A registration passes a second destination array only for groups whose entries carry attribute bytes, which matches the file's own self-describing per-entry attribute count. See docs/formats/str-strings.md.

entries.name: MfdCaptionTable
entries.description: 13 pointers into STRINGS0.STR group 5, filled at runtime by SimStrings_LoadAll (BSS, zero in the image). Entries 0-5 are the MFD's six screen titles (STATUS, FLASH COMM, NAV MAP, SCANNER, TARGET, MISSILE CAM) and 6-12 its aux button captions (MODE, SELECT, RANGE, TARGET, XMIT, PASS, ACTIVE). Indexed by mode for the title and by button index for captions. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButtonRects
entries.description: Four parallel int16[13] tables giving the MFD's button rects in GAU units relative to the inset screen origin: 0049cacc x0, 0049cae6 y0, 0049cb00 x1, 0049cb1a y1. Indices 0-5 are the F-key mode column at x -16..-2 with a 10-unit pitch (negative because the column sits left of the inset), 6 is a degenerate zero rect, 7-12 the per-screen aux buttons. Every rect size matches a dba\MFD.DBA frame size exactly. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdButtonVisibility
entries.description: 6 rows x 13 bytes: which buttons each MFD mode shows. Indices 0-5 are 1 in every row; the aux columns give SELECT on modes 0 and 4, XMIT on 1, RANGE/TARGET/PASS/ACTIVE on 3, and none on 2 and 5. MfdDisplay_SetMode and MfdDisplay_Repaint address it as &table[mode][6], which the decompiler folds into DAT_0049cbde + mode*13. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdStatusLabelTables
entries.description: Three parallel int16[5] tables for the MFD status screen's labels: 0049bd84 x0 (6 for all five), 0049bd8e y0 (16, 23, 32, 40, 49), 0049bd98 font selector (0,1,0,1,1) into {ColorSchemePanels[10] WHITE, [14] RED}. All in GAU units relative to the inset screen origin; each label is 6 units tall and runs right to the wireframe viewport's left edge at 45. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdStatusScreen_SetCondition
entries.description: Writes the MFD status screen's fourth and fifth labels. Label 4 (screen+0x1c) takes MfdStatusConditionStrings[state] = STRINGS0.STR group 28; state is the caller's, or FUN_00438700(damage) when the caller passes -1. Label 5 (screen+0x20) is composed from literals: "[ " (0049be2c), itoa((0x100 - damage) * 100 >> 8), then "% ]" (0049be2f) -- undamaged reads "[ 100% ]". When the subject is unreadable (screen+0x34 set) it writes "XXXXXX" and "XXX" instead. NOTE: STRINGS0.STR group 10 holds a near-identical five-string set and is dead data -- SimStrings_LoadAll is the only reference to its array. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdStatusConditionStrings
entries.description: 5 pointers into STRINGS0.STR group 28 -- OK, SHIELDS DN, INT DAMAGE, CRITICAL, DESTROYED -- filled at runtime by SimStrings_LoadAll. Indexed by condition state for the MFD status screen's fourth label in MfdStatusScreen_SetCondition. This, not the similar-looking group 10 at DAT_004d1440, is the live table. See docs/formats/mfd.md.

entries.name: MfdScannerRanges
entries.description: Three int32 scanner ranges -- 50000, 100000, 200000 world units = 300, 600, 1200 m at the game 1000 units = 6 m scale. MfdDisplay_Ctor writes all three as literals and inits the zoom field at +0xc5 to 2; 1200 m matches the RNG: readout in the retail scanner screenshot. The last entry is also read directly by the target filter FUN_00433174 as its radar-visibility range. See docs/formats/mfd-scanner.md.

entries.name: CockpitView_StepViewTransition
entries.description: Runs a queued view change's animated slide, once per frame from Sim_EndFrame just before CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand, gated on pending != -1 and the armed flag at +0x1c. For commands 0/1 (heads-down pan) it steps the display origin y by 10 canvas rows per loop iteration over vue[dest].canvasOriginY - vue[src].canvasOriginY (237, or 474 after the coord shift), then a remainder step; commands 4/5/6 step x by 0x14. The loop has no timer, retrace poll or frame boundary, so its real-time speed is CPU-bound. On completion: +0x14 += 1 (or -1), +0x18 = -1, +0x1d = 2 (two-frame cooldown). See docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md.

entries.name: Sim_EndFrame
entries.description: Per-frame tail: CockpitView_StepViewTransition, Palette_CycleAnimatedRanges, Palette_FlushDirtyRange, page flip (swaps the display context's +0x88/+0x8c page origins through DAT_004a5808/580c), then CockpitView_ProcessViewCommand. The DAT_004d25ea != 0 branch is the hardware-scroll display path.

entries.name: CockpitView_HandleViewKey
entries.description: Maps one pressed key id to a view command by current view. +0x21a is the heads-down key ([F7]/[F8]): view 0 queues command 0 (pan down), view 1 queues command 1 (pan up). +0x21e and +0x222 are the two side-glance keys, queuing 5/4 from view 0 and 6 from views 3/2.

entries.name: CockpitView_PollViewDevice
entries.description: Polls a device-state block for the four view axes -- bytes +0x1e/+0x1f/+0x20/+0x21 queue view commands 1/0/5/4 respectively -- i.e. the joystick hat's up/down/left/right, the alternative to CockpitView_HandleViewKey's keyboard path. Also handles the +0xb button edge.

entries.name: HddDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: HDDisplay constructor, .GAU offset 1212 (PHDD.CPP). Reads the block's origin, four region rects (+0xc1 screen, +0xe1 order column, +0xd1 damage column, +0xf1 title indicator), 15 widget rects and 3 comm-box marker rects; loads the 'static' and 'hdd' sprite banks and the 'hddclip' clip region; builds both page objects (+0x101 command display, +0x105 damage detail), the title label (+0x51b) and three 0x14e-byte comm gauges; ends with HddDisplay_SetPage(obj, 0).

entries.name: HddGau_ApplyCoordShift
entries.description: Pre-pass over the .GAU HDD block: adds 0x28 to the origin's y, then shifts every rect in the block by VideoMode_X/YCoordShift. The bias is what turns each retail file's authored origin (0,197) into (0,237), i.e. the same canvas origin the herc's own .VUE gives view 1 -- the row .HB1 is blitted at.

entries.name: HddButton_Ctor
entries.description: One HDDisplay sub-widget: rect at [0..3], owning display at param_1[9], index at param_1[10], label at param_1[0xb], unlit/lit frames at param_1[0xc]/[0xd], visibility state at +0x1b (2 = hidden), lit flag at +0x40.

entries.name: HddButton_Paint
entries.description: Paints one HDDisplay sub-widget, gated on state +0x1b < 2. The frame index differs by case, which is what makes some of these buttons latching and others momentary: indices 0/1 (the F7/F8 page buttons) take the frame from the object's own selection flag +0x40 and caption themselves 'F7'/'F8' from the shared 'Fx' literal at 0049d4f5 in ColorSchemePanels[12] selected / [10] not -- they have no pressed state; 2-7 (four arrows, two map magnifiers) take the frame from the shared press byte +0x1b and so light only while held; 10-12 fill the selected comm box's marker rect; 13/14 blit the plate and caption XMIT/CANCEL from STRINGS0 group 9, both frame and font indexed by that same press byte (ColorSchemePanels[4 + pressed]).

entries.name: HddDisplay_SetPage
entries.description: Switches the display between its two pages (0 = command display [F7], 1 = damage detail [F8]): unlights the old page button, hides the old page object, shows the new one, lights its button, then applies the 2x15 widget visibility table at HddPageWidgetVisibility -- a 0 sets the widget's state to 2, the value HddButton_Paint refuses to draw at.

entries.name: HddDisplay_SetTitle
entries.description: Fills the title label (+0x51b) from STRINGS0 group 11 entry 0 ('MAP') on page 0, or group 12 indexed by the damage screen's current category (' STRUCT DAMAGE' / ' INTERN DAMAGE' / ' WEAPON DAMAGE') on page 1.

entries.name: HddDisplay_SelectPilot
entries.description: Selects one of the three squad comm boxes (widgets 10-12): unlights the previous, records it at +0x52b, stores the new index at +0x517, lights its widget, sends the pilot a select message, and tells the command screen.

entries.name: HddDisplay_Repaint
entries.description: Whole-display paint: every visible widget, then the current page object's paint, then the title indicator rect (+0xf1, colour id 13 or -- while +0x51f is set, which the constructor does -- id 15), then HddDisplay_SetTitle, then the three comm gauges. A gauge slot with no squadmate in it is flooded with colour id 19 inset one device pixel instead.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_Ctor
entries.description: The [F7] command display. Builds the map viewport as the screen rect inset (4<<XCoordShift, 2<<YCoordShift) with its right edge at the order column's left minus the same, a 0x239-byte offscreen map render target centred on the zone, 140 map marker gadgets, and nine label rows down the order column at (y1-y0)/9 pitch: row 0 the incoming-message label in ColorSchemePanels[2], rows 1-8 the orders in [1] with [2] as the hotkey alternate.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_Repaint
entries.description: Floods the screen rect with colour id 19, refreshes the order rows, draws the selected order's 2px marker bar in id 15, repaints the two magnifier buttons, rebuilds the map markers and rasterizes the map.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_RefreshOrders
entries.description: Re-fonts and re-texts the eight order rows from STRINGS0 group 0 entries 10-17, passing each entry's single attribute byte as the index of its hotkey character within its own text. An available order draws in ColorSchemePanels[1] CPGREEN with the hotkey in [2] CPRED, an unavailable one wholly in [0] CPBLUE, and the selected one in [3] CPYLW.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_DrawOrderHighlight
entries.description: Blits HDD bank frame 2 + state (or 4) -- the 116x18 selected-order bar -- at an order label's own text position.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_BuildMapMarkers
entries.description: Rebuilds the map's marker gadgets: up to 9 waypoint markers from the player's own route (icons 0x4e+), then one per object in the three global object lists, then the player's own marker (icon 0x57). Gadgets past the last used one, out of the 140 allocated, are released.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_Ctor
entries.description: The [F8] damage detail. Resolves the four colour ids at HddDamageColorIds through HudColorTable in place -- nothing ever reads them -- then builds 13 rows of two labels each down the damage column: a name from the column's left edge + 0x1e<<XCoordShift, and a value column whose width is the measured width of the literal '100'. Rows are 4<<YCoordShift tall at 7<<YCoordShift pitch, all in ColorSchemePanels[1] on colour id 19. Also builds the subject caption at the screen's bottom-left and a centred no-data label, then calls HddDamageScreen_SetView(obj, 0).

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_SetView
entries.description: Selects the damage category and its row count: 0 structural = 0x13 rows, 1 internal = 0xc, 2 weapons = the subject's own fitted weapon count. The manual binds these to [S], [I] and [W], and to the display's up/down arrow buttons.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_Update
entries.description: Per-frame update and repaint. Picks the name table by category and subject type -- STRINGS0 groups 13/14 for structural (walker/flyer), 15/16 for internal, the mech's own weapon names for weapons -- floods the screen with colour id 3, sets the subject caption, blits the .PDG view for the category (0 structural, 1 internal) at the screen rect's top-left plus the view's own origin, tints its regions through PaperDoll_RecolorRectFromArt, and refills the rows. A row is a .PDG region in file order, not a table entry: the region's index selects both the name and the reading (armour entry 1+id for structural, dependent entry 20+id for internal, combined entry 32+slot for a weapon mount). Both of a row's labels are re-fonted from Damage_PickRegionTint's state through ColorSchemePanels 1, 3, 9, 2, 7. Structural regions 0 and 1 share a rect, so row 0 tints on the mean of both cockpit halves and row 1 tints nothing. See docs/formats/heads-down-display.md.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_SetSubjectCaption
entries.description: Sets the damage screen's subject caption from the display's five-entry name array at +0x548 (the player's 'YOU', three squadmate names, then 'TARGET') indexed by the subject selector at +0x55c. The player draws in ColorSchemePanels[3] on colour id 6, a squadmate in [2] on that pilot's own COLORS.DAT entry, and the target in [2] on id 15.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintIdle
entries.description: Paints one squad comm box while its pilot is not broadcasting: floods the video area with colour id 19 and fills five labels -- the pilot's name, 'STATUS:', the condition from STRINGS0 group 28, 'OBJECTIVE:', and the pilot's current order from group 40. Matches the manual's 'their video box remains darkened, displaying only their name, their status, and their current orders'. Defers to HddGauge_PaintStatic when the pilot's comms are out.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintStatic
entries.description: Draws the next of the 'static' bank's five frames into a comm box and advances the cycle -- the manual's 'the video box goes to static and you can send them no messages'.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintPilotFrame
entries.description: Draws one frame of a talking pilot into a comm box: floods it with colour id 19, blits the requested frame of the pilot<n> bank at that frame's own .OFS offset pair, and refreshes the name label.

entries.name: HddGauge_ConditionIndex
entries.description: Averages a mech's 19 structural damage bytes into a 0-100 integrity percentage and buckets it into the five STRINGS0 group 28 conditions at 90 / 74 / 51 / 1 -- OK, SHIELDS DN, INT DAMAGE, CRITICAL, DESTROYED.

entries.name: HddPageWidgetVisibility
entries.description: 2 rows x 15 bytes, indexed [page][widget] by HddDisplay_SetPage. Page 0 shows widgets 0-7 and 13-14, page 1 only 0-5. Both rows hide the three comm boxes (10-12), which HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames re-enables per occupied squad slot.

entries.name: HddSpriteBank
entries.description: The 'hdd' sprite bank handle (hba\HDD.HBA or dba\HDD.DBA), 27 frames: 0-1 the XMIT/CANCEL plate unlit/lit, 2-4 the selected-order highlight bar, 5-12 the first arrow-button set, 13-20 the second, 21-24 the two map magnifiers, 25-26 the F7/F8 page buttons. Which arrow set a herc uses is its own .GAU block value at offset 0x5c.

entries.name: HddStaticBank
entries.description: The 'static' sprite bank handle -- five 64x53 frames of video noise that HddGauge_PaintStatic cycles through a comm box whose pilot's comms are out. Ships in dba\ only.

entries.name: HddDamageColorIds
entries.description: Four COLORS.DAT logical colour ids -- 19, 9, 15, 12 -- that HddDamageScreen_Ctor resolves through HudColorTable in place to palette 16, 10, 13, 14 (black, red, yellow, green). Dead after that: 0049d9ec is materialised exactly once in the image, at 004507c9, which is the resolve loop itself, and nothing reads the resolved values. The damage rows take their colour from a ColorSchemePanels font picked by Damage_PickRegionTint's state instead. See docs/formats/heads-down-display.md, Rejected readings.

entries.name: HudFont_DrawString
entries.description: Draws a NUL-terminated run with a .DFN/.HFN font at a caller-supplied top-left, advancing the pen by each glyph's own width. A display-wide alignment override at renderContext+0x231 (1 = right, 2 = centre against the field width at +0x235) shifts the whole run first; it is 0 in the cockpit.

entries.name: HudFont_DrawGlyph
entries.description: Blits one glyph: height from font+0xa (file 0x0e cellHeight), width from HudFont_GlyphWidth, bit depth from font+0x12 (file 0x16, 8 in every retail file), pixels from the pool at font+0x22 indexed through the per-glyph offset array at font+0x26. Draws with its top row at y - font+0x16 (file 0x1a, the ink height), which is the other half of Label_SetRect's vertical rule.

entries.name: HudFont_GlyphWidth
entries.description: One glyph's advance width: the fixed width at font+0xc when that is not -1, otherwise the per-glyph width byte at font+0x2a indexed by char - firstCharCode. Every retail font stores -1 and is therefore proportional.

entries.name: HudFont_MeasureString
entries.description: Sums HudFont_GlyphWidth over a NUL-terminated run. Callers that align a run subtract 1<<XCoordShift from the result to drop the trailing advance past the last glyph.

entries.name: HudFont_CellHeight
entries.description: Returns font+0xa, the glyph cell height (file offset 0x0e; 13 for .HFN, 10 for .DFN). This is the glyph art's height, not the ink height at font+0x16 that labels centre by.

entries.name: Mouse_WndProcHook
entries.description: Registered into the MainWndProc filter chain (see WndProcHook_Register). Catches WM_MOUSEMOVE(0x200)/WM_LBUTTONDOWN(0x201)/WM_LBUTTONUP(0x202)/WM_RBUTTONDOWN(0x204)/WM_RBUTTONUP(0x205) -- none of which MainWndProc's own switch handles -- and forwards each to Mouse_DispatchEvent with a kind id (0=move,1=ldown,2=lup,3=rdown,4=rup) and a button-held bitmask built from wParam.

entries.name: Mouse_Init
entries.description: Registers Mouse_WndProcHook into the WndProc filter chain and, on first call, resets a clip/extent struct (width 0x140, height 400) via two small copy helpers at 0048062c/00480658 -- purpose not traced further, not needed to understand click handling.

entries.name: Mouse_DispatchEvent
entries.description: Rescales a raw window-client-space (x,y) from Mouse_WndProcHook into the game's internal coordinate space via a fixed-point factor (Mouse_RecomputeScale), packs the current L/R button-held bitmask into DAT_006c5fdc, and calls every enabled entry of the 10-slot mouse-listener table (DAT_006c5f5c, registered via MouseListener_Register) whose event mask has the event kind's bit set.

entries.name: Mouse_RecomputeScale
entries.description: Recomputes DAT_004a2de4/DAT_004a2de8, the 16.15 fixed-point (gameSize<<0xf)/clientSize factors Mouse_DispatchEvent uses to rescale window-client mouse coordinates into game space. Reads the window's current client rect, so it must be re-run on resize.

entries.name: MouseListener_Register
entries.description: Appends {enabled=1, eventMask, callback} to the first free slot (of 10) in the mouse-listener table at DAT_006c5f5c that Mouse_DispatchEvent fans events out to. Returns the slot index or -1 if full. Same {enabled,mask,fn}-triple-array idiom as WndProcHook_Register's table and the keyboard-binding table read by FUN_00477ae0 -- DBSIM reuses this shape for at least three unrelated subscriber lists.

entries.name: MouseListener_Unregister
entries.description: Clears slot param_2's enabled flag in the mouse-listener table at DAT_006c5f5c.

entries.name: WndProcHook_Register
entries.description: Appends a raw (hwnd,msg,wParam,lParam)-shaped filter function to the first free slot (of 10) in the table at DAT_004d3bb4 that MainWndProc tries, in order, before its own message switch -- any hook returning nonzero short-circuits MainWndProc entirely. Mouse_WndProcHook is one of four registered hooks found; the others are sound/movie-playback related.

entries.name: WndProcHook_Unregister
entries.description: Removes a hook previously added by WndProcHook_Register from the DAT_004d3bb4 table.

entries.name: CockpitMouse_Init
entries.description: Called once at cockpit setup. Registers CockpitMouse_OnEvent with MouseListener_Register under event mask 0x1e (button down/up on both buttons -- bits 1-4; bit 0, plain movement, is deliberately excluded), allocates the double-buffered per-frame event queue (two Cpp_VectorNew'd 0xe-byte-record vectors, swapped by CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue), and sets the click-vs-drag timing gate DAT_004d1e70 = 0x1e (30 coarse ticks, ~480ms at the ~62.5Hz UI timebase -- the same literal 0x1e as the event mask above but an unrelated field, easy to conflate).

entries.name: CockpitMouse_OnEvent
entries.description: The cockpit's one mouse-listener callback. Does not act on the event synchronously: pushes a {x,y,buttonMask,timestamp} record into the back-buffer queue via CockpitMouseQueue_Push (debounced to once per coarse tick) and, when a software/hardware cursor sprite is active (DAT_0049dbdf), calls Cursor_SyncPosition to keep the drawn pointer following the raw event position immediately rather than waiting for the once-per-frame queue drain.

entries.name: CockpitMouseQueue_Push
entries.description: Appends one 0xe=14-byte record {int32 x, int32 y, uint16 buttonMask, int32 timestamp} to the back-buffer vector at DAT_004d1e88, capped at 99 entries (silently drops further events past that).

entries.name: CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue
entries.description: Swaps the double-buffered event queue and drains it once per frame -- the real click/hover/drag logic. Per record: on a position change, hit-tests via Widget_HitTestChildren and either forwards to the captured widget's drag slot (if mouse-captured) or fires Widget_OnMouseHover; on a button-down edge, calls Widget_OnMouseDown; on a button-up edge, gates on the release landing within DAT_004d1e70 ticks of the press before calling Widget_OnMouseUp (or, if a drag was in progress, ends the capture and fires the captured widget's OnClick/GetValue pair directly).

entries.name: Widget_HitTest
entries.description: Point-in-widget test against a single widget, param_1. A per-widget flag at param_1+0x10 selects the shape: 0 = axis-aligned rect, inclusive bounds at param_1[0..3] (x0,y0,x1,y1); nonzero = circular/diamond region, Manhattan distance from a centre point (param_1+0x11/+0x13, int16 cx,cy) at most a radius (param_1+0x15, int16). The circular form is not exercised by any widget traced so far (MFD/HDD/console buttons and the shield facings are all rectangular); presumably serves a knob/dial-shaped control.

entries.name: Widget_HitTestChildren
entries.description: Linear-scans the flat clickable-widget list at param_1+0x256 (count at +0x254) with Widget_HitTest, returning the index of the first widget under the point whose state (+0x1b) is not 2 (hidden). Not a tree walk: every clickable widget anywhere in the cockpit is registered into one shared list by Widget_RegisterClickable, so an off-screen panel's buttons are excluded purely by their hidden state, not by not being reachable.

entries.name: Widget_OnMouseDown
entries.description: Hit-tests the press position via Widget_HitTestChildren; if a widget is hit, marks its state (+0x1b) pressed (1) and, if that widget opts in via its own +0x1d==1 flag, begins mouse capture (DAT_0049dbde=1) and forwards the position to the widget's drag-move vtable slot. Widgets built with +0x1d left 0 (every button/gauge traced so far) never enter capture and are handled entirely by press/release instead.

entries.name: Widget_OnMouseUp
entries.description: Hit-tests the release position; if it lands on the same widget that was pressed (or the right button is still held), calls the widget's own GetValue then OnClick vtable slots with that value, then clears its pressed state (+0x1b=0) and repaints it via Widget_Repaint. This is where a click actually fires -- CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue only calls this after its own press/release timing gate passes.

entries.name: Widget_TrackPressedWidget
entries.description: On a position change while a button is held, keeps the pressed widget's appearance in sync with the pointer: hit-tests, and if the hit is still the widget in DAT_0049dbdc sets its state (+0x1b) to 1, otherwise clears it to 0, repainting via Widget_Repaint on each change. This is the button that pops back up when you drag off it and depresses again when you return. Guarded entirely on DAT_0049dbdc != -1, and that global is set only by Widget_OnMouseDown and cleared to -1 by Widget_OnMouseUp, so this cannot run unless a button is down. Previously named Widget_OnMouseHover, which was wrong: DBSIM has no hover state, corroborated by CockpitMouse_Init's event mask (0x1e) excluding plain movement.

entries.name: Widget_PressedIndex
entries.description: int16. Index into the cockpit-wide clickable list of the widget a mouse button is currently held down on, or -1 for none. One global for the whole cockpit, not per-panel. Set by Widget_OnMouseDown from its own hit test, read and acted on by Widget_TrackPressedWidget, cleared to -1 at the end of Widget_OnMouseUp. Its -1 guard is what makes Widget_TrackPressedWidget a no-op unless a button is held.

entries.name: Widget_Repaint
entries.description: Calls a widget's own Paint vtable slot after a state change. The slot's numeric offset is not uniform across classes (confirmed +4 for MfdDisplay and HddButton via unambiguous ctor evidence; do not assume the same offset for every class without checking).

entries.name: Widget_RegisterClickable
entries.description: Appends one widget pointer to the caller's flat +0x256 array (count at +0x254) that Widget_HitTestChildren scans. Called once per child during every cockpit widget tree's construction (MfdDisplay_Ctor's 13 MFD buttons, ShieldsGauge_Ctor's 2 facings, etc.) with the *dereferenced* CockpitViewInstance pointer as the shared root -- every clickable widget in the whole cockpit lands in one list, not a per-panel one.

entries.name: Widget_Show
entries.description: Sets the child widget at index param_2 of the caller's +0x256 array to state 0 (normal/visible) and repaints it. Pairs with Widget_Hide.

entries.name: Widget_Hide
entries.description: Sets the child widget at index param_2 of the caller's +0x256 array to state 2 (hidden -- excluded from Widget_HitTestChildren and refused by every traced Paint slot) and repaints it. Pairs with Widget_Show.

entries.name: maybe_Widget_NotifySelfAndChildren
entries.description: Toggles a guard flag (+0x227) around calling vtable slot 0 on the caller itself, then on every widget in its +0x256 clickable-child array. What slot 0 means is class-specific (observed as OnClick/OnCommand for MfdDisplay and ShieldsGauge) so this function's own purpose -- relayout notification, a generic show/refresh cascade -- was not independently confirmed, only its mechanical shape.

entries.name: Cursor_SyncPosition
entries.description: Moves the on-screen pointer to the (x,y) in param_1. If a hardware cursor is active (DAT_004a365e), hides/shows it via two function pointers (DAT_004a5840/DAT_004a583c, a DirectDraw cursor surface's vtable calls) around updating its position (DAT_004a3638/3c); otherwise stashes the position for the software cursor overlay Screen_PresentFrame draws.

entries.name: maybe_Screen_PresentFrame
entries.description: Dual-purpose per-frame presentation: in windowed/GDI mode (_DAT_004d25e2==0), StretchBlt's the backbuffer to the window via BeginPaint/EndPaint; in fullscreen mode, raw-copies the backbuffer into VRAM and, when a software cursor bitmap is active (DAT_004d37a8), blits it at GetCursorPos() clipped to the viewport, colour-keyed on byte value 1. Named for its dominant role (frame presentation); the cursor blit is secondary but confirms the visible pointer is genuinely drawn from the same OS cursor position the click pipeline reads, not a separate abstracted position.

entries.name: maybe_Mouse_WarpCursorToPoint
entries.description: Rescales a game-space point to client coordinates (inverse of Mouse_RecomputeScale's factor) and calls SetCursorPos. Caller(s) and trigger not traced -- plausibly a 'snap cursor to this widget' affordance, not confirmed.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_OnClick
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's own vtable slot 0 (per the same *param_1=&PTR_thisFunction ctor-assignment evidence used for MfdButton_OnClick). Searches its own +0x18/+0x68 child-pointer table (populated identically to MfdDisplay's, by ShieldsGauge_Ctor) for the clicked facing widget; index 0 (front) sets state byte +0xc2=1 clearing +0xc3, index 1 (rear) the reverse. Consumed once per frame by Shield_BalanceInputRead, not painted directly.

entries.name: ShieldFacing_OnClick
entries.description: A shield-facing child widget's own click handler, reached via Widget_OnMouseUp. Gated on the left mouse button bit (param_2&1); forwards the click to its owner (pointer stored at the facing's own +0x24, set to the parent ShieldsGauge at construction) as owner->vtable[0](owner, self, buttonFlags) -- i.e. calls ShieldsGauge_OnClick -- then repaints itself and notifies its label child.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_GetStateBlock
entries.description: Trivial accessor: returns param_1+0xb5, the start of ShieldsGauge's 15-byte live state block (front charge, rear charge, balance, then the two click flags ShieldsGauge_OnClick sets). Shield_BalanceInputRead copies out of this pointer directly rather than through a richer accessor.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_SetStateBlock
entries.description: Write-back counterpart to ShieldsGauge_GetStateBlock: overwrites the 15-byte state block at param_1+0xb5 from param_2 (called by Shield_BalanceInputRead with the freshly computed front/rear percentages and a cleared click-flag pair), and sets the dirty flag at +0xb0=2 if the values actually changed. Also zeroes the front/rear fields when the gauge's +0x8d 'shields down' flag is set.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Paint
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's vtable+4 slot. Unconditionally calls ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette and ShieldsGauge_UpdateReadouts.

entries.name: ShieldsGauge_Update
entries.description: ShieldsGauge's per-frame update slot (vtable+8, called from the general HUD paint pass, not the click pipeline). Gated on visibility and a 'shields present' flag; when the dirty flag ShieldsGauge_SetStateBlock set (+0xb0==2) is pending, refreshes the ring palette and readouts and clears it. This is the bridge between Shield_BalanceInputRead's once-per-frame gameplay update and the HUD paint pass -- the click sets a flag, the gameplay tick consumes it into real sim state and a dirty bit, and this slot is what actually repaints from that bit.

entries.name: ShieldFacing_Paint
entries.description: A shield-facing child's Paint slot. Draws no geometry -- only a visibility test (FUN_00431410) -- because the concentric rings retail shows are palette-animated into the herc's own canopy art, not drawn by this widget (see ShieldsGauge_UpdateRingPalette in docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md).

entries.name: maybe_ShieldFacing_FlashTimer
entries.description: A shield-facing child's update slot: a two-stage counter at +0x1f (2->1 calls FUN_0043122c then decrements; 1->0 just decrements) -- plausibly a brief post-click flash/debounce, not independently confirmed.

entries.name: Sim_PollPlayerInput
entries.description: Reads the input device struct (axes at +0x0e steer, +0x10 throttle, +0x12 torso twist, +0x14 torso pitch) and dispatches player control: Mech_ApplyThrottleInput, Mech_TorsoTwistTick, Mech_TorsoPitchTick. Also hosts the keyboard command switch.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyThrottleInput
entries.description: Player throttle handler. Integrates the stick axis into mech+0x290 (throttle, Q10, clamped +/-0x400) at Q8(0x91,-axis) per tick, converts it to a desired speed via Q10(maxRev or maxFwd, throttle), then calls Mech_LocomotionTick. ThrottleLeverMode (0049a06e) gates the clamp: at 0 it spans the full +/-0x400, so the axis held down runs through zero into reverse.

entries.name: Mech_LocomotionTick
entries.description: The Herc control law. Sets speed (mech+0x28e), turn rate (mech+0x28c), heading (mech+0x10) and animation rate (mech+0x2a0); about 60 percent of the body is the gait state machine. Writes no position -- all translation is animation root motion. Turn rate is a tent over speed peaking at half top speed; turn-in-place sets only the animation rate.

entries.name: Mech_ApplyTerrainSlopeToSpeed
entries.description: Adjusts desired speed by dot(terrainNormal, forwardVector)/0x960, signed by direction of travel, clamped to zero on sign flip. Uphill slows, downhill speeds up.

entries.name: Mech_AiObstacleAvoidance
entries.description: Terrain and obstacle avoidance applied to steering and desired speed. AI only -- Mech_LocomotionTick skips it when the mech is PlayerMech.

entries.name: Mech_MovementTick
entries.description: Per-tick mech physics step: push transform, integrate motion, clamp Z to Terrain_HeightQuery plus typeRec[+0x16], collision test, restore and reverse speed on hit, place legs. Dispatched via mech vtable +0x18 to 00415b38 to behaviour struct +0x18; its pointer lives in an unmarked 0x24-stride table from 00499928, so Ghidra reports zero xrefs.

entries.name: Mech_IntegrateMotion
entries.description: Sets the animation playback rate from mech+0x2a0, then advances the object by dt = Math_IntegrateRateOverTick(100) via SimObject_ApplyRootMotion.

entries.name: SimObject_ApplyRootMotion
entries.description: Seeds the shape root node to identity, advances the animation by dt, reads node 0 world transform back, and applies it: pos = objRotation * delta.translation + pos, euler += eulerOf(delta.rotation). Then resets the root. The only source of Herc translation and turn-in-place rotation.

entries.name: SimObject_PushTransform
entries.description: Saves the object transform, position and the whole animated node hierarchy into globals at 004a8d54. Paired with SimObject_PopTransform.

entries.name: SimObject_PopTransform
entries.description: Restores what SimObject_PushTransform saved. Used by Mech_MovementTick to undo a blocked move.

entries.name: Mech_CollisionTest
entries.description: Returns nonzero when the just-integrated position is blocked.

entries.name: Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround
entries.description: Per-leg terrain placement over the mech animated node hierarchy.

entries.name: AnimThread_LoadFrameGroundMovement
entries.description: Called on every animation frame advance. If the sequence ground-movement flag is set, loads Transforms[transformIndices[frame * numParts]] -- part index 0, the root node -- into the thread ground translation (+0x22/24/26) and rotation (+0x28/2a/2c) and sets the ground-move flag at +0x20.

entries.name: AnimThread_ReadRootTransform
entries.description: Returns scale(groundTransform, thread[0x1c]/thread[0x1e]) composed onto the thread stored transform, where the fraction is intra-frame accumulator over frame duration. Inverse of AnimThread_WriteRootTransform.

entries.name: AnimThread_WriteRootTransform
entries.description: Stores inverse(scale(groundTransform, frac)) composed with the incoming transform. Paired with AnimThread_ReadRootTransform so that seeding identity and reading back yields the exact per-tick root-motion delta.

entries.name: AnimThread_CommitGroundMovement
entries.description: On frame exit, folds the completed frame full ground transform into the thread stored transform.

entries.name: AnimThread_UncommitGroundMovement
entries.description: Inverse of AnimThread_CommitGroundMovement, for backward playback.

entries.name: AnimThread_Advance
entries.description: Advances one animation thread by dt * thread[0x4e] >> 8, crossing frames forward or backward and driving the ground-movement load and commit hooks.

entries.name: AnimThread_SetPlaybackRate
entries.description: Writes the playback rate to thread+0x4e; restarts the sequence when the sign flips.

entries.name: ShapeInstance_StepAnimation
entries.description: Advance threads, evaluate keyframes into per-node local transforms, rebuild world transforms. FULLY RESOLVED 2026-08-22, in call order: AnimThread_StepAll (004789a0) then ShapeInst_EvalAllNodeLocals (004789f4, which runs AnimThread_EvalNodeLocals per thread) then ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms (00478b58). The keyframe interpolation is the middle step, so poses are re-blended every time this is called. CADENCE SETTLED: the sole caller is SimObject_ApplyRootMotion (0040250c), which Mech_IntegrateMotion runs once per sim tick -- poses are evaluated per TICK, not per rendered frame.
