entries.description: ShapeVolume_HeightAround with the grid-origin shift applied for the caller (origin << cellShift, i.e. world units rather than cells). Returns 0 for a shape with no collision volume.

entries.name: SimObject_GetShapeRadius
entries.description: SimObject vtable +0x10: the current LOD shape's bounding radius, shape+8 via the shape instance at obj+0x34. Every hit test's coarse reject uses it, as does the LOD selector FUN_004033e4. shape+8 is the third of the three int16 head fields ClassItemTree_ReadBaseHeader reads -- BasesDgsTransformer previously called it an id.

entries.name: Collision_ClusterBoundTest
entries.description: Tests one cluster's load-time bounding sphere against the ray: centre into muzzle space, unsigned compare of Y against radius plus the working ray length (DAT_004a9894), and FastMagnitude2D of X/Z under radius plus the ray clearance (DAT_004a9898). The cheap gate before Collision_ClusterSphereTest.

entries.name: Collision_ClusterSphereTest
entries.description: Walks a cluster's child spheres, transforming each centre into muzzle space and calling Collision_RaySphereTest with update enabled. Returns the (now shortened) working ray length + 1 if any sphere was struck, 0 otherwise.

entries.name: Collision_RaySphereTest
entries.description: One sphere against the ray in muzzle space. Rejects on an unsigned Y compare against the working ray length, then tests the off-axis distance against clearance + radius in 16-bit arithmetic ((ushort)(offAxis + reach) < (ushort)(reach * 2)) because the doubled reach can overflow a short. On a hit it clips DAT_004a9894 to the entry point, alongAxis - (reach - offAxis), floored at 0.

entries.name: Collision_ReadNode
entries.description: Reads one node of a collision model: int16 node index (-1 = the object's own frame, otherwise an index resolved through the shape instance's node-transform array) and int16 cluster count, then that many 16-byte clusters via Collision_ReadCluster. Was named Collision_LoadSubSpheres, which described the shape one level off.

entries.name: Collision_ReadCluster
entries.description: Reads a cluster's component index into the record's +6, then its sphere array via Collision_ReadSphereArray into +0/+2. The component index is what makes a destroyed section stop blocking shots. Was named Collision_LoadSubSphereFlag: the value it reads is the component index, not a flag, and the branch it guards is on the read succeeding rather than on the value.

entries.name: Collision_ReadSphereArray
entries.description: Reads a cluster's int16 sphere count into the record's +0 and, when count & 0x1fff is nonzero, that many 8-byte { int16 x, y, z, radius } spheres into +2. The mask is only a zero-test -- the allocation and the read both use the unmasked value, and no retail record sets the top bits. Was named Collision_LoadSubMeshIndices; the 8-byte records are spheres, not mesh indices.

entries.name: maybe_FlyerType_LoadResources
entries.description: Per-flyer-type resource load into a 0x70-byte type record: the shape, the .dmg component file (+0x2e), and the col/<NAME>.COL hit-sphere model via Collision_RegisterObject (+0x32, which is what the flyer's own vtable +0x20 Flyer_DirectFireHitTest passes to Mech_SelectStruckComponent).

entries.name: Flyer_DirectFireHitTest
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x20. Coarse reject on SimObject_GetShapeRadius (shape+8), then Mech_SelectStruckComponent against the type's col/<NAME>.COL model (flyerTypeRec+0x32) with the per-component alive flags at obj+0x208. Damage through vtable +0x74; spawns from ImpactFXArmor, or a fixed effect id 10 once the flyer is destroyed. No shields and no collision volume -- the simplest of the three hit tests. Ported.

entries.name: Component_AddDamage
entries.description: Adds damage to one component/dependent damage entry. An entry already holding -1 (destroyed) absorbs nothing. An entry the damage finishes stores -1 rather than the max and writes the EXCESS back through the damage pointer, which is what Component_SpillIntoDependents runs on. Returns whether the entry is now destroyed.

entries.name: Component_SpillIntoDependents
entries.description: Pours a destroyed component's overflow damage into its dependent sub-pieces, one at a time. The pick is weighted and random: each live dependent contributes its .DMG CritChance to a total, a draw under that total selects one, and if the spill destroys it the remainder goes round again. Returns true only when no live dependents remain -- which is the condition Component_ApplyDamageAndCascade requires before it will cascade.

entries.name: Component_AllDependentsDestroyed
entries.description: Whether every dependent sub-piece a component's .DMG record lists is destroyed (-1). Used only by Component_IsFullyDestroyed.

entries.name: Component_IsFullyDestroyed
entries.description: Component destroyed AND all of its dependents destroyed. The stricter of the two 'is this gone' tests; Mech_ComponentDamageWrite asks it of the two cockpit slots (0 and 1) as the mech's death gate.

entries.name: Flyer_ComponentDamageWrite
entries.description: Flyer vtable +0x74. Thin wrapper over Component_ApplyDamageAndCascade on the header at flyer+0x200: destroying component 0 loses the aircraft -- sets flyer+0x99, credits the kill through the attacker's +0x60, fires the mission action at flyer+0x1b6, and writes -100000 to flyer+0x2e so it falls.

entries.name: Flyer_Constructor
entries.description: Flyer class constructor. Installs vtable 0049a5e0, allocates the component-damage header at flyer+0x200 with literal counts of 1 and 1 (one main component, one dependent -- exactly what SKIMMER.DMG ships), and links the type record at flyer+0x1fa plus its .DMG and .COL pointers via Component_LinkMaxRefData.

entries.name: Collision_ClusterTest
entries.description: One collision cluster against the ray: Collision_ClusterBoundTest on the load-time bounding sphere first, and Collision_ClusterSphereTest over the children only if it passes.

entries.name: Collision_FindClusterForComponent
entries.description: Walks a collision model's nodes looking for the cluster that owns a given component index, via Collision_FindClusterInNode; returns the cluster and writes the owning node index out. Used by Component_DestroyAndCascade to place a destroyed component's debris, not by the hit test.

entries.name: Collision_FindClusterInNode
entries.description: Linear search over one node's 16-byte clusters for a matching component index (cluster+6). Helper for Collision_FindClusterForComponent.

entries.name: Transform_Concat
entries.description: Composes two 32-byte transforms (9 Q14 int16 matrix entries, a rank byte at +0x12, three int32 translations at +0x14/+0x18/+0x1c) into a third. Branches on both operands' rank bytes -- translation only, Z-rotation only, or full 3x3 -- as an optimisation, not a behavioural difference. Every hit test builds its object-to-muzzle frame with this.

entries.name: Transform_ApplyToShortPoint
entries.description: Transforms an int16 point by a 32-byte transform into an int32 result, Q14 with round-to-nearest (+0x2000 before the >>14). Same math as Transform_ApplyToPoint, narrower input; used for collision sphere centres.

entries.name: Transform_ApplyToPoint
entries.description: Transforms an int32 point by a 32-byte transform, Q14 with round-to-nearest and 64-bit intermediates. The int-width counterpart of Transform_ApplyToShortPoint.

entries.name: Math_RandomBelow
entries.description: A draw in [0, bound): (Math_RandomNext() & 0x7fff) % bound. The mask drops the sign bit rather than taking an absolute value, so the distribution is the low fifteen bits'. Used by Component_SpillIntoDependents' weighted pick.

entries.name: TargetSelect_SetObject
entries.description: Cockpit target selection, on the widget tree (its +0x210 is the selection): selects one named object, or clears when passed 0. Reached by the ; key (scancode 0x27), the F4 scanner's TARGET button and a gunsight click. Walks +0x210 through the live-object list from the cursor at +0x214/+0x218 until it lands on the object asked for and it passes TargetSelect_CanTarget and TargetSelect_InForwardCone, so a request for something unselectable wraps back to where it started.

entries.name: TargetSelect_Nearest
entries.description: The manual's Nearest Target, the apostrophe key (scancode 0x28) via Sim_DispatchCommand. Nearest selectable object by 3D range, considering only target classes 0 (HERC) and 2 (flyer) -- structures are excluded -- and applying no cone test at all, so it reaches something behind the machine.

entries.name: TargetSelect_Cycle
entries.description: The manual's Select Target, [Enter] (scancode 0x1c) via CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand. Files every selectable object inside the forward cone into one of four buckets by bearing error (abs(err) >> 10, clamped to 3), sorted by range within a bucket keeping four, flattens them into the 4-entry shortlist at DAT_004d0490 and takes its head; a repeat press whose head is unchanged steps to the entry after the current selection. The angular-size correction it computes is multiplied by a literal PUSH 0x0 at 004335d0 and is therefore always zero.

entries.name: TargetSelect_CanTarget
entries.description: Whether an object may be selected: alive (+0x99 and +0xa4 clear), on the other side (group+0x12), and known by either sensor route -- radar-visible (+0x95) within DAT_004d1cfc (200000, the last of the scanner's three ranges, read directly rather than the current setting), or a contact the viewer holds (viewer+0xc2+obj[0x4b]) within FUN_00426aec (30000 short / 60000 long).

entries.name: TargetSelect_InForwardCone
entries.description: Bearing to the candidate less the machine's heading PLUS its turret twist (vtable +0x3c), accepted within +/-8999 -- just under 50 degrees each side. Wider cousin of the +/-0x3000 gate the missile-lock block uses. The twist sign is the original's; Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate and the sensor sweep fold it the same way.

entries.name: Sim_DetectionTick
entries.description: The whole sensor model for one tick, from Sim_MainTick after every object update and the input poll. Three passes: tick each object's LOS-cache (+0x1e2) and contact-decay (+0x1e5) timers, running Detection_DecayContacts on expiry; run Detection_Sweep for each live human-side object, holding the locally-piloted machine (+0xa3) back to sweep LAST so squadmates' contacts reach it first; clear the per-tick action latch +0xa2.

entries.name: Detection_Sweep
entries.description: One human-side object's look around, over Cybrid objects only -- but it writes both objects' tables, so a Cybrid learns without ever sweeping. Radar painting within 200000 when either object emits and not both are painted, with 140000 the range at which a scanner paints something not emitting back. Looking runs only within 80000: a pair that already knows each other is skipped, otherwise each object's +/-0x3800 sensor arc (vtable +0x44) plus LOS makes the contact -- shared to the spotter's side by Detection_ShareContact, or kept private when the spotter is the player's machine.

entries.name: Detection_ShareContact
entries.description: Passes a new contact to every object on the spotter's own side within 100000 units, the spotter included, and sets the contact's +0x9e engagement flag inside 50000. Nothing is shared to the other side and a same-side pair is not a contact at all.

entries.name: Detection_DecayContacts
entries.description: Clears the object's own radar visibility (+0x95) then drops every enemy contact it holds that is past 100001 units or has no line of sight, mutually. The range here is measured on the GROUND PLANE only (Math_FastMagnitude2D) where every other range in the sensor model is the 3D approximation, so a flyer directly overhead stays a contact.

entries.name: Detection_LineOfSight
entries.description: Terrain ray between two objects' shape bounding-box centres (vtable +0x24 then +0x1c, or 500 with no shape record), cached per pair in the caller's row table at +0x132. The cache gate tests the OTHER object's countdown at +0x1e3 and reloads the CALLER's -- verified in raw disassembly at 00412617 and 0041263f, so it is the original's own asymmetry and not a decompiler slip. Only human-side objects sweep, so Cybrid timers stay zero and those pairs are re-walked whenever asked.

entries.name: SimObject_BearingInSensorArc
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x44: (bearing - obj+0x10 + 0x3800) < 0x7000 unsigned, so +/-78.75 degrees about the object's heading. Callers fold the aim twist into the bearing before calling.

entries.name: Mech_ToggleRadarMode
entries.description: The manual's [R] and the F4 scanner's PASS/ACTIVE buttons: flips mech+0x96 between PASSIVE and ACTIVE, gated on +0xa3 so only the locally-piloted machine toggles, then repaints the two console lights (0x2c/0x2d) and plays the mode tone. A HERC powers up PASSIVE -- nothing writes +0x96 at construction and this is its only caller. Base_Construct latches it on for structure types 5, 6, 0x1d and 0x1e, the radar masts.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_RoundsByMissileType
entries.description: Fills a 5-entry short array with rounds carried per PROJ.DAT missile subtype, by walking the mount array calling each mount's vtable +0x60 (WeaponMount_GetAmmoType) and accumulating its out-parameter (mount+0x7b) into rounds[subtype], skipping the 5 sentinel. THIS is the ammunition count; manager+0x0a is the lock state. Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate uses it to decide which lock timers run.

entries.name: Mech_LockTonePlay
entries.description: Turns mech+0x9b (lock acquired) into the cockpit lock tone: FUN_0046272c(0x15) on a 0x40-coarse-tick blink cadence while set, 0x14 when clear but the target just changed (+0x9d), 0x16 once on loss. Called from the tail of Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate for the locally-piloted machine only.

entries.name: Math_Atan2Guarded
entries.description: atan2 as a BAM angle, with the degenerate pair nudged onto an axis. ARGUMENT ORDER IS (x, y), NOT (y, x): it forwards to FUN_004929bc(p1, p2) and sets p1 -- the X -- to 1 when both are zero. Both Math_HeadingToward and Math_EulerToward call it as (dx, dy). Getting this backwards mirrors a bearing about the 45-degree line and turns an elevation into a polar angle from +Z; it cost the engine port a real bug, so state the order rather than writing 'atan2(dx, dy)'.

entries.name: Mech_GetAimNodeTransform
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x24: resolves the type record's +0x0c (.DAT file offset 10, CameraBoneId -- the node the cockpit eye rides) through the shape's part lookup (shape vtable +0x20) and returns that node's 0x20-byte transform record at shapeInstance+0x16 + index*0x20, or the zeroed DAT_006c572c when the shape has no such part. Callers take its +0x14 translation as the point to aim at and its +0x1c as a sight height. This is what makes both guidance routines and the HUD target indicator aim at a HERC's cockpit rather than the ground point its model origin sits on.

entries.name: SimObject_GetAimNodeTransform_None
entries.description: Vtable +0x24 on both the flyer and structure classes: return 0. Every caller's null branch falls back to the object's raw origin for aiming and to a literal 500 for sight height, so only a mech has an aim node. The mech's own is Mech_GetAimNodeTransform.

entries.name: GunsightChild_CtorBase
entries.description: Base of all nine roving-gunsight children: stores the caller's {x0,y0,x1,y1} rect at +4..+0x10 and sets a stub vtable each subclass overwrites. Children 4, 5 and 6 additionally receive the 38-byte target state block at +0x14.

entries.name: Gunsight_ReticlePaint
entries.description: Gunsight child 4's paint: blits one HUD-bank reticle frame centred on the .GAU reticle point (offset 1136). Frame 0 with no target, with the selection behind the near plane, or with its aim point projecting further than 5<<CoordShift from the reticle on either axis; frame 2 inside that tolerance; frame 1 when the armed missile mount also has lock (state block +0x39 = mech+0x9b).

entries.name: Gunsight_TargetIndicator_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor for gunsight child 5, the target box and its off-screen arrow: GunsightChild_CtorBase plus vtable 0049c1c4, whose slot 0 is Gunsight_TargetIndicatorPaint.

entries.name: Gunsight_TargetIndicatorPaint
entries.description: Gunsight child 5's paint: the HUD target box (pip, four mirrored corner brackets, four edge ticks -- HUD frames 3-6 unlocked, 7-10 locked) and, when the target does not project inside the .GAU's offset-1148 rect, a flat-filled arrow at that rect's border pointing at it. Box side is clamp(2*(shapeRadius>>1)*focal/distance, 25, 75) device pixels, the clamp NOT coordinate-shifted. It is the only widget that calls Cockpit_PopRenderContext before drawing and Cockpit_PushCanvasContext after, so the box alone is clipped to the canopy cutout and goes behind the cockpit frame.

entries.name: Gunsight_ClickSurface_Ctor
entries.description: Gunsight child 0: the clickable gunsight surface over the 3D view, on the .GAU's offset-1148 rect. Allocates a gadget and registers it with the cockpit's clickable list, which is the 'gunsight click' path into TargetSelect_SetObject.

entries.name: Gunsight_ClickSurface_Paint
entries.description: Child 0's paint: draws nothing, only tests the cursor point at +0x42/+0x46 against its own rect and reports the result.

entries.name: Gunsight_UnusedChild_Ctor
entries.description: Gunsight child 6. Built on Gunsight_TargetIndicator_Ctor and fed the same target state block at construction, then overwritten with vtable 0049c174 whose paint slot is a bare RET. Never drawn, and never updated per frame either -- Gunsight_SetValues pushes live state to children 4 and 5 only.

entries.name: Gunsight_UnusedChild_Paint
entries.description: Child 6's paint slot: RET. See Gunsight_UnusedChild_Ctor.

entries.name: HudWaypointIndicator_Ctor
entries.description: Gunsight children 7 and 8, both on the heading tape's rect with limits +/-0xe38. Built on HudRotationIndicator_Ctor, then given vtable 0049c154 whose paint is Hud_UpdateWaypointIndicator, plus a label child. Child 7 additionally sets its +0x45 flag.

entries.name: Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint
entries.description: The roving gunsight's vtable +8, called once a frame from maybe_Sim_RenderFrame. Copies CockpitView+0x26c..+0x27e (target, world aim point, component id) into the widget's state block at +0xb7..+0xc9, adds the target's heading (+0xc7), its shape radius from vtable +0x10 (+0xcd) and a literal 2000 (+0xd1), drives child 1 from the viewing object's heading, then runs every child's slot +4 and repaints the whole complex.

entries.name: Gunsight_GetStateBlock
entries.description: Returns the roving gunsight's 38-byte target/angle state block, widget+0xb1. Callers are Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate and the three TargetSelect_* entry points, which set byte 36 to 1 to arm the target indicator.

entries.name: CockpitView_SetTargetBlock
entries.description: Writes the frame's target block into CockpitViewInstance+0x26c..+0x27e: the selected object, its world aim point (3 ints), and the two shorts Player_ResolveTargetAimPoint produced -- a component-present flag and the component id. Gunsight_UpdateAndPaint and MfdStatusScreen_Paint both read it.

entries.name: Player_ResolveTargetAimPoint
entries.description: Resolves the point the HUD aims at on the selected target. With a targeting computer fitted (mech+0x30b) and the target inside 30000 units it asks the pod for a component aim point and component id; otherwise it takes the target's vtable +0x24 aim node transformed by the target's own rotation, falls back to the raw origin, and writes 0 to the component id.

entries.name: MfdStatusScreen_Paint
entries.description: Paint for the MFD status screen shared by F1 and F5. Latches the subject from the display's shared block (+0xb9), then branches on its target class: a HERC gets its .PDG paper doll and a twelve-dependent condition scan, a flyer gets flyers-bank frame 0, a structure gets bases/vehicles frame BASES.DAT+0x28. ID: versus TARGET: follows whether the subject is the viewing object or a squadmate; the name label's font and the integrity-versus-range choice for label 4 both follow the subject's mission-group side byte. This is the paint-time font override docs/formats/mfd.md previously recorded as untraced.

entries.name: MfdStatusScreen_Update
entries.description: The status screen's vtable +4: ticks a 30-tick blink latch at +0x34/+0x35, runs the paint, then invalidates the screen rect.

entries.name: Damage_ToConditionState
entries.description: Maps a Q8 damage fraction to a STRINGS0.STR group 28 condition index: intact = (0x100-damage)*100>>8, then >=0x5a OK, >=0x4a SHIELDS DN, >=0x33 INT DAMAGE, >=1 CRITICAL, else DESTROYED. Used for subjects with no per-component readings -- flyers and structures.

entries.name: Damage_PickRegionTint
entries.description: Picks the colour one .PDG damage region is repainted in. Writes {condition state, palette index} to the caller's two-int block. Bands are Damage_ToConditionState's -- intact >=90/74/51/1 -- and for the region mode at region+0x18 of 0, 2 or 3 the colours are HudColorTable ids 12, 15, 20, 9, 18 (green, yellow, orange, red, grey). Mode 1 instead keeps the region's own colour id (region+0x14) for the top three bands, so an undamaged region is left alone, and takes ids 6 and 17 for the last two; no retail region states a mode other than 0. Mode >= 4 falls through writing the caller's own scratch. See docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md.

entries.name: PaperDoll_RecolorRect
entries.signature: void __cdecl PaperDoll_RecolorRect(int *rect, int keyIndex, int tintIndex, int mode)
entries.description: Repaints one .PDG region in place, reading each pixel back out of the raster. Modes 0, 1 and 3 rewrite only the pixels holding keyIndex; mode 2 adds tintIndex to every pixel that is not the id-19 background. Modes 0 and 1 skip the walk entirely when the two colours agree. Mode 0 steps whole device pixels at a time when a 320-wide bank is being drawn doubled; the other three step one. The MFD status screen's route -- the HDD damage screen uses PaperDoll_RecolorRectFromArt instead. See docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md.

entries.name: PaperDoll_RecolorRectFromArt
entries.signature: void __cdecl PaperDoll_RecolorRectFromArt(int *rect, void *art, int *artOrigin, int keyIndex, int tintIndex, int mode)
entries.description: PaperDoll_RecolorRect's four modes over a source bitmap rather than the raster: mode 0 walks art's own rows (width at +6, pixels at +0xe) offset by artOrigin, so a region can be recoloured from the art without the screen underneath being repainted first. Modes 1-3 still read the raster back and do not expand pixels. The HDD damage screen's route. See docs/formats/cockpit-hud.md.

entries.name: Mech_ReadDamageReadouts
entries.description: Fills a 42-short display buffer for one machine: entry 0 is the type record's +0x6c, the rest come from Component_FillDamageReadouts.

entries.name: Component_FillDamageReadouts
entries.description: Fills the damage-readout buffer from a component-damage object: shorts 1-19 the armour components as Q8 fractions (0x100 when destroyed), 20-31 the twelve dependents on their own, 32-41 ten combined armour+dependent readings. MfdStatusScreen_Paint scans 20-31 for its CRITICAL/INT DAMAGE condition.

entries.name: Component_ReadOverallDamage
entries.description: One object's whole damage as a Q8 fraction, 0 pristine and 256 destroyed: every main component and every dependent weighed once against its own maximum, a destroyed one counting as its full maximum. Reached through the object's vtable +0x40 and printed by the MFD status screen's integrity readout.

entries.name: Mech_GetOverallDamage
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x40: Component_ReadOverallDamage on mech+0x206.

entries.name: Squad_IndexOf
entries.description: Returns an object's index in the three-entry squadmate array DAT_004d044c, or -1. MfdStatusScreen_Paint uses it to decide between ID: with a pilot name and TARGET: with a type name.

entries.name: Cockpit_CreateCanvasContext
entries.description: Allocates the cockpit widget layer's own 0x239-byte render context, sets clip mode 1 (single rect) at +0x208 and the caller's rect at +0x210..+0x21c, and stores it in DAT_004d042c. Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets passes the whole cockpit canvas and keeps the result at CockpitViewInstance+4.

entries.name: Cockpit_PushCanvasContext
entries.description: Pushes the current render context onto the stack at DAT_004d0470 and installs CockpitViewInstance+4, the full-canvas mode-1 context. Every cockpit widget paint runs inside a Cockpit_PushCanvasContext/Cockpit_PopRenderContext pair, which is why console instruments outside the canopy cutout can draw at all.

entries.name: Cockpit_PopRenderContext
entries.description: Restores the render context Cockpit_PushCanvasContext saved. Gunsight_TargetIndicatorPaint calls it deliberately mid-paint to drop back into the view's canopy-clipped context for the target box's blits.

entries.name: Raster_InstallRenderContext
entries.description: Installs a render context: DAT_006c5ff4 = ctx, and PTR_DAT_004a362c = ctx+4, its clip block. The block's mode sits at ctx+0x208 -- 0 none, 1 the single rect at ctx+0x210, 2 the region list the block holds -- and CockpitView_ApplyViewState is what puts a view's context into mode 2 with the herc's .HD/.ED canopy regions. THE ctx+4 OFFSET IS LOAD-BEARING for reading brush code: the fill brush Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch reads at clipBlock+0x228 is the field callers write as ctx+0x22c, and the line brush at clipBlock+0x224 is ctx+0x228.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch
entries.description: Applies the installed clip block to a blit: offsets the destination by the context's translation when ctx+0x20c is 1, then dispatches on the clip mode at ctx+0x208 -- unclipped, or rect-clipped to ctx+0x210 for both mode 1 and mode 2. A type-1 (transparent) bitmap is handed to Bitmap_BlitTransparent before any of that and is clipped there instead.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitTransparent
entries.description: The transparent/RLE sprite blitter. Rejects against the context's clip rect (ctx+0x210..+0x21c), then sets a per-call flag from whether the clip mode is 2 and sends every pixel run it emits either to the plain span writer (DAT_004a581c/DAT_004a5824) or to the region-clipped one (DAT_004a5820/DAT_004a5828). That flag is why a sprite drawn through a mode-2 context is cut to the canopy cutout scanline by scanline rather than to a rectangle.

entries.name: Raster_FillRect
entries.description: Fills a rect through the installed clip block: mode 0 direct, mode 1 intersected with ctx+0x210, otherwise walked against each region in the block's list (rect regions intersected, span regions clipped through FUN_00486af4). Used by the MFD status screen's label backgrounds and its component highlight.

entries.name: Math_Atan2Bam
entries.description: atan2 in binary angles, arguments (x, y): 0 is +x and +y is a quarter turn, so in screen space 0 is right and a quarter turn is down. The result is masked to 14 bits and shifted left 2.

entries.name: Math_BuildRotation2D
entries.description: Builds a 2x2 Q14 rotation matrix for a binary angle into a short[4] -- {cos, sin, -sin, cos}, both looked up in the quarter-turn table at 004a25dc.

entries.name: Math_Rotate2DPoint
entries.description: Rotates an {int x, int y} point by a Math_BuildRotation2D matrix, rounding at Q14.

entries.name: Sos_BindLibrary
entries.description: Binds the HMI Sound Operating System. GetVersion() picks sos32s03.dll under Win32s (high bit set, major <= 3) and sos9503.dll otherwise -- only sos9503.dll ships -- then walks the self-describing table at 004a6ab4: 0x24-byte records of {void **destination, char name[0x20]}, terminated by a NULL destination, GetProcAddress'ing each. 100 entry points: 44 sosDIGI*, 45 sosMIDI*, 8 sosTIMER*, sosGetErrorString, sosPrepare32Memory, sosUnPrepare32Memory. Refcounted at 004a6ab0, so repeated calls bind once.

entries.name: SosBindingTable
entries.description: HMI SOS dynamic-binding table: 0x24-byte records {void **destination, char name[0x20]}, a NULL destination terminating. 100 records. Walked by Sos_BindLibrary.

entries.name: Sos_InitBackend
entries.description: SFX backend bring-up: binds the SOS library, copies the SOUND.CFG-derived config block (rate, width, driver, buffers) into 004a0e5c..004a0e64, then opens the driver through 00473da0 -- once with the configured driver id, once with id 1.

entries.name: Music_PlayTrack
entries.description: Plays one Red Book CD track through MCI, not through SOS: MCI_OPEN device 'cdaudio', MCI_SET time format TMSF, MCI_PLAY with MCI_FROM|MCI_TO|MCI_NOTIFY from the track start to that track's own length (00473c78). The MCI_NOTIFY is what makes sfxWndProc restart it on MM_MCINOTIFY, so a track loops.

entries.name: Music_Stop
entries.description: MCI_STOP then MCI_CLOSE on the cdaudio device, and resets the device id at 004a0e44 to -1.

entries.name: Music_GetPosition
entries.description: MCI_STATUS with item MCI_STATUS_POSITION and MCI_WAIT -- the saved TMSF position Music_ResumeAt takes.

entries.name: Music_ResumeAt
entries.description: Same open/set/play as Music_PlayTrack, but MCI_FROM is a saved TMSF position rather than a track start. Used by Sound_ResumeAll.

entries.name: Music_MciDeviceId
entries.description: MCI device id of the open cdaudio device, or -1 when closed.

entries.name: Sos_MasterVolume
entries.description: Master volume, 0-100, multiplied into every voice volume by Sos_ApplyVolume. A constant 100: its only setter (004739a8) has no callers.

entries.name: Sos_LoadOrFreeSample
entries.description: (resourceName, slotIndex, load, isMidiSong). Loads or frees one resource's backend object at record+0x214. isMidiSong picks the .hmp song path (00474550 / 004745fc) over the digital sample path (00474254 / 004743fc).

entries.name: Sos_StartVoice
entries.description: (resourceRecord+4, voiceRecord+4). Starts one voice on the backend. Branches three ways on the voice flags: bit 0 = MIDI song, bit 12 = the streamed-by-name path (00474630), otherwise a SOS digital sample -- packing volume into both 16-bit halves, translating loop count 0 to -1 (infinite) and n to n-1, and copying pan and callback into the sample object.

entries.name: Sos_StopVoice
entries.description: Stops one voice on whichever of the three backend paths its flags select.

entries.name: Sos_ApplyVolume
entries.description: Converts a voice's 0-100 volume to the backend's range: volume * Sos_MasterVolume * 0x7fff / 10000 duplicated into both 16-bit halves for left and right, or volume * 0x7f / 100 for a MIDI song.

entries.name: SfxManager
entries.description: The single SFX manager instance (0x4c bytes), or 0 when sound is off. Every Sound_* entry point tests it first.

entries.name: Sfx_ReadConfig
entries.description: Reads DATA\\SOUND.CFG with GetPrivateProfileString into the manager's config block at +0x24: Driver (MME=1 / DirectSound=2) at +0x2a, Buffers (1-64, else 5) at +0x30, Rate (11 gives 0x10, else 0x20) at +0x24, Width (Mono gives 4, else 8) at +0x28. +0x26 is fixed at 1 and +0x32 at 0x200.

entries.name: Sfx_Init
entries.description: (manager, memoryCap, resourceSlots, voiceSlots). Called as (cap, 60, 90). Allocates the resource table at +0x34 (stride 0x21c) and the voice table at +0x38 (stride 0x28), fills every slot's handle with -1, then brings the backend up with the config block at +0x24.

entries.name: Sfx_Open
entries.description: (manager, name, type, userValue, loadState) -> voice handle, or -1. Handles are generation<<16|slotIndex, the generation coming from the manager's counter at +0x20; every accessor re-reads the slot's own copy and rejects a mismatch. Takes a free voice slot and defaults it (priority 5, volume 100, loop 1, pan 0x8000, pitch 0x10000), then binds a resource: an existing resource with the same name is shared and its refcount bumped, otherwise a free resource slot takes the name. type 0 = .hmp MIDI song (flag 0x1), 1 = digital sample, 2 = the streamed path (flag 0x1000).

entries.name: Sfx_Close
entries.description: Releases one voice slot and drops its resource's refcount.

entries.name: Sfx_Cache
entries.description: (manager, voiceHandle, in). Loads or unloads the voice's resource. Loading stats the file for its byte size into record+0x210, and if cached+size would exceed the manager's cap at +0x18 runs Sfx_EvictUntilFree first; on success sets record+0x20c and adds the size to the cached total at +0x1c. Unloading refuses while the resource refcount (+0x208) is 2 or more.

entries.name: Sfx_Play
entries.description: (manager, voiceHandle). Caches the resource on demand, starts it through Sos_StartVoice, sets the playing flag 0x100 and bumps the manager's playing-sample (+0x3c) or playing-song (+0x40) count.

entries.name: Sfx_Stop
entries.description: Stops one voice and clears its playing flag.

entries.name: Sfx_IsDone
entries.description: Returns nonzero when the voice is not playing; when the backend reports it finished, calls Sfx_Stop to clear the state.

entries.name: Sfx_PickEvictionVictim
entries.description: Scores every live voice and returns the lowest: (resource cached ? 100 : 0) + priority + (playing ? 1000 : 0) + (playing && looping ? 10000 : 0). An idle, uncached, low-priority voice is taken first and a looping playing one last.

entries.name: Sfx_EvictUntilFree
entries.description: Frees cached resources by repeatedly taking Sfx_PickEvictionVictim's choice until the requested number of bytes fits under the manager's cap.

entries.name: Sfx_SetVolume
entries.description: Writes voice+0x14 (0-100) and re-applies it to the backend if the voice is live.

entries.name: Sfx_SetPan
entries.description: Writes voice+0x1c; 0x8000 is centre and clears flag 0x800, anything else sets it.

entries.name: Sfx_SetPitch
entries.description: Writes voice+0x20 as 16.16; 0x10000 is 1.0 and clears flag 0x400, anything else sets it.

entries.name: Sfx_SetLooping
entries.description: Writes voice+0x18 as a repeat COUNT, not a boolean: 0 = forever, 1 = once, n = n times. Sets flag 0x80 for any value other than 1.

entries.name: Sfx_SetPriority
entries.description: Writes voice+0x0c. The sound catalog uses 5; the speech channel uses 0xff so catalog voices can never evict it.

entries.name: Sfx_SetCallback
entries.description: Writes voice+0x10, handed to the backend sample object when the voice starts.

entries.name: Sfx_GetVoiceRecord
entries.description: Validates a voice handle and returns a pointer to its record+4, or 0.

entries.name: Sfx_ServiceFinishedVoices
entries.description: Sweeps the voice table, asking the backend which playing voices have finished, clearing their 0x100 flag and decrementing the manager's playing counts.

entries.name: sfxWndProc
entries.description: MainWndProc filter registered by Sound_Init (see WndProcHook_Register). Two messages only: WM_TIMER (0x113) pumps the SOS/MME service routine, and MM_MCINOTIFY (0x3b9) with MCI_NOTIFY_SUCCESSFUL re-issues Music_PlayTrack, which is what loops the CD track.

entries.name: Sound_Init
entries.description: (enable). Registers sfxWndProc as a MainWndProc hook, allocates the five-slot speech channel pool (5 x 0x42-byte records plus a 5 x 100-byte script buffer at 004d2df4), then allocates and initialises the SFX manager with a cache cap of 2,000,000 bytes -- 1,000,000 when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set -- 60 resource slots and 90 voice slots, and loads the sound catalog.

entries.name: Sound_Shutdown
entries.description: Stops the CD, unregisters sfxWndProc, tears the SFX manager down and clears SfxManager.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_Load
entries.description: Loads str\\SOUNDS.STR -- one .STR group of 57 entries, each a filename plus a 7-byte attribute blob -- into three parallel arrays: names (004d2b0c), attribute pointers (004d2bfc) and voice handles (004d2cfc), count in 004d2dec. Per entry: resolve the path through Sound_ResolveSamplePath, Sfx_Open as a sample, priority 5, Sfx_SetLooping to attribute byte 0, Sfx_SetVolume to Math_Q16Multiply(byte 1, 65000), Sfx_Cache if byte 2 is set, then default byte 4 to 5 and byte 5 to 100 where they are 0xff and set byte 8 to 100. The code reads a TEN-byte blob: bytes 7-9 are runtime scratch (resume flag, category volume, throttle counter) that the file does not supply.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_Names
entries.description: 57 pointers to the catalog's .wav filenames, into the loaded SOUNDS.STR buffer.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_Attributes
entries.description: 57 pointers to the catalog's attribute blobs, into the loaded SOUNDS.STR buffer. Byte 0 loop count (0 = forever), 1 volume 0-100, 2 preload, 3 throttle divisor, 4 rolloff start / 1024 world units (0xff gives 5), 5 cutoff / 1024 world units (0xff gives 100), 6 variation count, 7 resume flag, 8 category volume percent, 9 throttle counter. Bytes 7-9 are runtime-only and overlap the next entry's header in the file buffer, which is inert because every pointer is collected before the first write.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_Voices
entries.description: 57 SFX voice handles, one per catalog id. Index 10 (004d2d24) is where the effects half starts.

entries.name: SoundCatalog_Count
entries.description: Number of catalog entries actually opened.

entries.name: Sound_ResolveSamplePath
entries.description: Prefixes a catalog filename with 'HMI\\', or 'HMX\\' when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set. SIMSOUND.VOL carries both banks, hmx being the same content at half the sample rate; EXPLO5.WAV is in hmi only.

entries.name: Sound_IsCategoryEnabled
entries.description: Splits the catalog at id 10: below 10 answers to the music enable flag (0049f90c), 10 and up to the effects flag (0049f910). This is why every data-driven table plays SoundId + 10.

entries.name: Sound_Play
entries.description: (catalogId). Non-positional. Rolls the variation count (attribute byte 6) to displace the id, sets volume to Math_Q16Multiply(byte 1, 65000) * byte 8 / 100 -- or 0 when the category is muted -- and plays.

entries.name: Sound_PlayAt
entries.description: (catalogId, worldPoint). Positional. Rolls the variation count, then Sound_Place computes volume and pan; plays only if the result is audible. One entry point covers every data-driven sound in the sim (PROJ.DAT, ROCKETS.DAT, EXPLOS.DAT, the alerts).

entries.name: Sound_Place
entries.description: (catalogId, worldPoint) -> audible. Resets the model transform and pushes the point through the current camera transform, so the listener is the camera. With d = Math_FastMagnitude3D(view): beyond attribute byte 5 * 1024 the volume is 0 and nothing plays; at or past byte 4 * 1024 it is (max - d) * vol / max -- the divisor is max, not max - min, so a sound at exactly min is already attenuated. Final volume is scaled by attribute byte 8 / 100. Pan is (-2a) & 0xffff for a = Math_Atan2Bam(viewX, viewY) below 0x8000, and 2a & 0xffff above.

entries.name: Sound_UpdatePosition
entries.description: Re-runs Sound_Place for a sound already playing, without starting it.

entries.name: Sound_ThrottleCheck
entries.description: (catalogId) -> may play. interval = (2 - detailSetting 004d1fc7) * attribute byte 3; interval 0 always plays, otherwise attribute byte 9 counts up (wrapping at 0x0f) and only every interval-th call passes. Keeps a sound fired by many objects at once from playing once per object.

entries.name: Sound_Stop
entries.description: Stops one catalog id's voice.

entries.name: Sound_IsPlaying
entries.description: Returns whether one catalog id's voice is still playing.

entries.name: Sound_Preload
entries.description: Caches one catalog id's sample without playing it.

entries.name: Sound_MuteMusic
entries.description: Zeroes the volume of catalog ids 0-9 and clears the music enable flag; when a CD track is set, saves the position and stops the CD instead.

entries.name: Sound_MuteEffects
entries.description: Zeroes the volume of catalog ids 10 and up and clears the effects enable flag.

entries.name: Sound_UnmuteMusic
entries.description: Restores ids 0-9 to Math_Q16Multiply(byte 1, 65000) * byte 8 / 100, or resumes the CD from the saved position, and sets the music enable flag.

entries.name: Sound_UnmuteEffects
entries.description: Restores ids 10 and up to their own volumes and sets the effects enable flag.

entries.name: Sound_SetCategoryVolume
entries.description: Writes attribute byte 8, the per-sound category scale every volume computation multiplies through, and re-applies the resulting volume.

entries.name: Sound_SetBaseVolume
entries.description: Overwrites attribute byte 1 (the authored 0-100 volume) and re-applies it.

entries.name: Sound_ShiftMusicSet
entries.description: (delta, charIndex). Offsets one character of each of the ten music filenames by delta and re-opens them -- how a different music set would have been selected. All ten name battle1.wav, which ships in no archive.

entries.name: Sound_SuspendAll
entries.description: Records which catalog voices are playing into attribute byte 7, saves the CD position into 0049f91c, stops the CD and services the backend. Paired with Sound_ResumeAll.

entries.name: Sound_ResumeAll
entries.description: Replays exactly the catalog voices whose attribute byte 7 was set by Sound_SuspendAll, and resumes the CD from the saved TMSF position.

entries.name: Sound_MusicEnabled
entries.description: Enable flag for catalog ids 0-9.

entries.name: Sound_EffectsEnabled
entries.description: Enable flag for catalog ids 10 and up.

entries.name: Music_CdTrack
entries.description: CD track number for the mission, written by Sim_InitMissionSession. 0 means use the (dead) digital music ids instead.

entries.name: Music_CdEnabled
entries.description: CD music enable byte, written by Sim_InitMissionSession.

entries.name: Music_SavedPosition
entries.description: TMSF position saved by Sound_SuspendAll for Music_ResumeAt.

entries.name: Sound_SpeechEnabled
entries.description: Enable flag for the five-slot speech channel; without it Voice_Acquire opens nothing.

entries.name: VoiceSlots
entries.description: Five 0x42-byte speech channel records. +0x00 SFX voice handle, +0x04 next script event time, +0x08 current portrait frame (-1 = finished), +0x0a script cursor, +0x0e wav name, +0x2f this slot's 100-byte .SNC buffer, +0x33 name pointer for the by-name lookup, +0x37 last-use tick for LRU, +0x3b in-use, +0x3c owning catalog id, +0x3e SFX voice handle.

entries.name: Voice_Acquire
entries.description: (wavName, sncPath) -> slot. Looks the name up across the five speech slots; a miss evicts the least recently used (Voice_EvictLru), copies the name in, opens an SFX voice at priority 0xff so catalog voices can never evict it, caches it, and loads the .SNC script. Gated on Sound_SpeechEnabled.

entries.name: Voice_EvictLru
entries.description: Picks the speech slot with the oldest last-use tick (+0x37), closes whatever voice it held and returns it.

entries.name: Voice_PlayNamed
entries.description: (wavName, volume). Acquires a speech slot for the name with no .SNC script, sets its volume and starts it.

entries.name: Snc_Load
entries.description: (slot, sncPath, voiceHandle). Reads the .SNC file into the slot's 100-byte buffer: an int32 length followed by that many bytes of {int8 frame, int8 deltaTicks} pairs, then appends the 0xff terminator itself -- the terminator is NOT in the file. With no path the buffer is just 0xff and the voice plays with the portrait held.

entries.name: Snc_Start
entries.description: Points the slot's cursor at the start of its script; an immediately-0xff script sets the frame to 1 and plays without animation, otherwise stamps the start time and runs Snc_Advance. Then plays the voice.

entries.name: Snc_Advance
entries.description: Reads {frame, delta} pairs, accumulating delta into the slot's next-event time until it passes now, publishes the frame at slot+0x08, and re-inserts the slot into the global event queue. Reaching 0xff sets the frame to -1, which is what tells HddGauge_PaintPilotFrame the message is over.

entries.name: Snc_ServiceQueue
entries.description: Drains the global .SNC event queue (004d2efa, 8-byte {time, slot} entries, count 0049f97c) of everything now due, calling each slot's Snc_Advance.

entries.name: Snc_GetFrame
entries.description: Returns the slot's current portrait frame (slot+0x08); -1 once the script has ended.

entries.name: SncEventQueue
entries.description: Global .SNC timer queue: 8-byte {uint32 time, void *slot} entries, count at 0049f97c, drained by Snc_ServiceQueue.

entries.name: CommBox_BeginMessage
entries.description: Builds the two filenames for one comm message and acquires a speech slot. suffix = '_' + 2-digit message id + 3-digit variant; the wav is 'P' + voiceBank + suffix in simvoice/simvoicf/simvoicg, the script 'P' + ('A' + squadSlot) + suffix in snc/. voiceBank is (slot >> 2) + 1 with 3 remapped to 4, so twelve squad slots share three recorded voices P1_/P2_/P4_ -- the same grouping as str\\PILOT0/1/2/4.STR.

entries.name: Voice_ArchiveName
entries.description: Returns the voice archive name, patching the last character of the literal 'simvoice' with the language byte at 004d25ba: SIMVOICE / SIMVOICF / SIMVOICG.

entries.name: Cockpit_PowerUpSound
entries.description: The cockpit's power-up audio. Plays Sound_Play(0x13) -- start3, the start-up sequence -- once per session, gated on cockpit+0x245 and stamping cockpit+0x241 with Time_GetCoarseTicks. Then, ONLY when the piloted machine's type record (mech+0x1f2) has a nonzero +0x50 -- file offset 78, InputFlagFlyer, the RAZOR alone -- starts the looping engine hum Sound_Play(0x2d) and immediately drops it with Sound_SetPitch(0x2d, 42000), about 0.64 of its recorded rate. Despite the sample being called herceng1, a walking HERC never plays it; its running noise is its footsteps.

entries.name: Sound_SetPitch
entries.description: Sets one catalog id's playback rate through Sfx_SetPitch, as the original's 16.16 ratio (0x10000 = 1.0). Cockpit_PowerUpSound is the only caller found, dropping the engine hum to 42000.

entries.name: LockTone_PhaseSounded
entries.description: Mech_LockTonePlay's blink latch: set once the lock tone has sounded for the current phase of the 0x40-coarse-tick cadence, cleared when that bit goes low, so the tone plays once per phase rather than every tick.

entries.name: LockTone_WasLocked
entries.description: Mech_LockTonePlay's edge latch: set while a lock is held, so that losing it plays trgunloc (0x16) exactly once. The branch that consumes it returns before the target-changed test, which is why switching target while locked plays the loss tone and not the acquisition blip.

entries.name: Sound_DetailSetting
entries.description: An options-screen 0-2 value the sound throttle scales against: Sound_ThrottleCheck computes its interval as (2 - this) * the catalog row's throttle divisor, so 2 zeroes the interval and lets every call through while 0 doubles the authored divisor. Also read by an options-screen label (FUN_004571f4 case 8) and by FUN_00403914 and FUN_00408bd8.

entries.name: Sos_SetMasterVolume
entries.description: Writes Sos_MasterVolume from the passed voice record's +0x10. Dead: it has no callers, so the master volume stays at its initialised 100 for the whole run.

entries.name: Sos_BindRefCount
entries.description: Sos_BindLibrary's refcount. Nonzero means the SOS entry points are already bound, so repeated calls skip the LoadLibrary and the GetProcAddress walk.

entries.name: ViewObjectPtr
entries.description: Pointer to the active view object; its +4 is the camera position triple. Simulation code reads it directly for two audio range gates -- Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround tests a machine against it before playing a footfall, and Rocket_TickUpdate tests each round against it for the missile-inbound warning -- so the camera position is an input to the simulation, not only to the renderer.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_KeyDispatch
entries.description: Vtable slot 4 of the [F7] command display: switches on a DOS scancode, not a widget index. D/A/F/T/G/O/C/E arm the eight orders, ,< and .> step through them, Tab cycles the eligible unit for ATTACK ENEMY or DEFEND POSITION, Enter drops the map cursor, keypad 5 recentres the map, and X and Backspace press the XMIT and CANCEL widgets. The transmit branch reuses the radar-mode tone pair as an accepted/rejected blip: Sound_Play(0x1a) when the transmit resolves to a recipient and Sound_Play(0x1b) when it does not.

entries.name: MessagePort_QueueInit
entries.description: Builds the message port's queue: a vector of ten 0x31-byte records. The port is instantiated twice per cockpit view -- the computer's scrolling ticker at view+0x20b and the pilot/squad channel at view+0x207.

entries.name: MessagePort_Enqueue
entries.description: Fills one queued record from a SYSTEM.STR entry's eight attribute bytes: id at +0x00, filename digit at +0x16, priority at +0x17, and the four timings at +0x1c/+0x20/+0x24/+0x28, each multiplied by 0x3c coarse ticks. minTime/maxTime stay durations until the message is shown; minWait/maxWait get the post tick added at once. The insert stops at the first queued entry of strictly higher priority, so low sorts first.

entries.name: MessagePort_AddBeginCallback
entries.description: Registers one of up to two begin callbacks at port+0x4b9, fired when a message comes due. Only the pilot/squad port registers any -- the comm box's CommBox_OnMessageBegin/CommBox_OnMessageEnd pair. The computer's port has none.

entries.name: MessagePort_Tick
entries.description: The message port's whole lifecycle, on four latches: +0x4c9 due, +0x4ca ready (set by the paint, which is what puts one frame between due and shown), +0x4cb cancelled, +0x49e a line is up. Drops queued messages past index 0 whose maxWait has passed, takes the queue front as current, then shows / holds / takes down. A line comes down when cancelled, when maxTime has passed, when minTime has passed and the queue holds more than one message, or when LocalPlayerMech+0x99 says the player's machine is dead. That middle clause is the whole of the port's preemption.

entries.name: SystemMessages_Index
entries.description: Indexes SYSTEM.STR into a 63-slot table at base + attr[0] * 9, each slot a {char *text; byte count; byte *attributes} triple, counting how many strings landed in each. Two entries sharing an id would become variants of one message and the post would roll between them; all 63 retail ids are distinct, so every count is one.

entries.name: MessagePort_Withdraw
entries.description: Withdraws a posted message, matching on the message id AND the record's +0x02 subject pointer, so the same message about two machines is two entries. Sets the cancel latch on the current message only if it is not yet due -- a line already on screen runs out its display time -- and otherwise removes the match from the queue. Mech_ToggleRadarMode withdraws both radar lines before posting the one the mode became.

entries.name: MessagePort_Pause
entries.description: Marks the port paused, recording the coarse tick it stopped at. Paired with MessagePort_Resume.

entries.name: MessagePort_Resume
entries.description: Shifts every deadline in the queue, the current message's two display deadlines and the scroll's publish time forward by however long the pause lasted, so a paused line keeps the rest of its display time.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_Speak
entries.description: The pilot/squad channel's voice dispatch. Builds its P*_* filename out of the message id and the queued record's +0x16 digit the same way CommBox_BeginMessage does.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_WrapText
entries.description: Word-wraps a pilot/squad message to that channel's box width. It paints several wrapped lines where the computer's ticker scrolls one.

entries.name: PilotMessagePort_Paint
entries.description: Paints the pilot/squad channel's several wrapped lines. Its box is the .GAU field at content offset 1668 -- full screen width, ten units tall -- read by Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets rather than by Gau_Load.

entries.name: MessagePort_Ctor
entries.description: Constructs a message port from the box rect Gau_BuildCockpitWidgets read out of the .GAU and coordinate-shifted into device pixels.

entries.name: MessagePort_SetText
entries.description: Latches the line the ticker will draw: strncpy of 0x50 characters, so a longer message is truncated there.

entries.name: MessagePort_PickVariant
entries.description: Rolls between the variants SystemMessages_Index counted for an id -- the same roll SOUNDS.STR attribute byte 6 drives. No retail id has more than one, so it always picks that one.

entries.name: MessagePort_Show
entries.description: Puts the current message up. Swallows a repeat of the same id inside 300 coarse ticks (about 4.8 s), and a swallowed repeat refreshes that window rather than leaving it. Otherwise latches the line, restores the box rect, publishes the scroll origin, repaints, plays an alert tone picked by a switch on the id (0x00/0x13 -> 0x19 strcfail; 0x0c/0x0f/0x10/0x14/0x15 -> 0x18 wrnwoop2; everything else 0x1a gnract -- the switch names a dozen further ids that all reach the default arm's tone), then speaks the line. Message 0x36 TRANSFERRING DATA is armed to blink here.

entries.name: MessageTicker_Paint
entries.description: Paints the computer's ticker: the box flooded with COLORS.DAT id 19 (black), a one-pixel frame in id 9 (red) through the fill brush's style 4, and the line in ColorSchemePanels[2] CPRED. Narrows the live clip rect by 3 << VideoMode_XCoordShift on each side before the glyphs go down, so the text slides under the frame rather than past it. Anchors the glyph row at ((height - cellHeight) >> 1) + inkHeight + 1, which HudFont_DrawGlyph subtracts inkHeight back off -- the cell centred in the box, not Label_SetRect's ink-centred rule. Message 0x36 is centred instead of scrolled.

entries.name: MessageTicker_ScrollText
entries.description: Recomputes the scrolling line's x every frame as port+0x4af - (0x23 << VideoMode_XCoordShift) * elapsed / 0x3c: it starts at the box's right edge and travels left at 35 authored units a second, 70 device pixels in the 640-wide mode. There is no wrap -- a line that outlives its own width simply leaves.

entries.name: MessagePort_Erase
entries.description: Takes the line down and erases its box, filling the same rect with the same COLORS.DAT id 19 the paint floods it with and nothing else -- which is what identifies that colour as the background rather than as part of the frame.

entries.name: CommBox_OnMessageBegin
entries.description: The pilot/squad port's begin callback, installed through MessagePort_AddBeginCallback. Starts that speaker's .wav and .SNC portrait and plays the whitenz static under it.

entries.name: CommBox_OnMessageEnd
entries.description: The matching end hook for CommBox_OnMessageBegin.

entries.name: Cockpit_PowerUpTick
entries.description: The cockpit power-up sequence. Once 200 < coarse ticks have passed since it began, walks the ten heads-down gauges (FUN_0041b514, then FUN_00438700 < 0x5a) and posts message 0x22 POWERUP INITIATED. INTERNAL DAMAGE DETECTED. if any is under, else 0x21 ... ALL SYSTEMS NOMINAL. At 16 ms a coarse tick that lands 3.2 s in, inside start3's five seconds rather than after them.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_ToggleAutoTrack
entries.description: The console buttons manager's auto-track toggle, reached from ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock and from Sim_DispatchCommand's command 0x14 (and forced off by command 0xe). Flips the manager's +0xb3, pushes the new state into the tracking object at +0x20 and repaints it, then withdraws both 0x26 AUTO TRACKING ENGAGED and 0x27 AUTO TRACKING DISABLED from the computer's message port and posts the one the mode just became -- the same shape as Mech_ToggleRadarMode. Refuses outright when the tracking object's +0x1b is 2.

entries.name: MessageChannelModes
entries.description: Four-byte array of message channel enable bytes the preferences screen writes, offered as OFF / TEXT ONLY / VOICE ONLY / TEXT-VOICE. Entries 2 and 3 are PilotMessageMode and ComputerMessageMode.

entries.name: PilotMessageMode
entries.description: MessageChannelModes[2]: the PILOT MESSAGE preference, gating the pilot/squad port's two halves.

entries.name: ComputerMessageMode
entries.description: MessageChannelModes[3]: the COMPUTER MESSAGE preference. The display runs when the byte is not 1 and the voice when it is not 0 -- three behaviours, not four, so which of the screen's four labels carries which value is not settled by the code. With the display off the port still runs the whole lifecycle and only skips the drawing (port+0x4d2).

One-line accessor returning DAT_004cfa20. MessagePort_Show reads its +0x14 as a mode enum and refuses to display a message in mode 4, suppressing the line exactly as the TEXT-OFF preference does while the lifecycle runs on. The enum's values and the object's class are not decoded. Distinct from CockpitViewManagerInstance despite the matching offset Sim_DispatchCommand tests there.

The object FUN_00429820 returns. Two of its fields gate the computer message display: +0x14, the mode enum MessagePort_Show refuses mode 4 on, and +0x1c, a byte MessageTicker_Paint tests first and returns on. The object's class is not decoded.

entries.name: WeaponMount_CtorBase
entries.description: Base weapon-mount constructor, run by every mount class before its own. Loads the hardpoint's weapon model when the .GL mounting code (+6) is under 4 via WeaponMount_ShapeForMountingCode, installs it with ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames at mount+0x10, translates its point lists to the mount point with Shape_TranslatePointLists, resolves the two .GL aim nodes at +2/+4 (both -1 on every retail chassis), zeroes the flag blocks at +0x33/+0x3b/+0x43, and writes the refire scale 0x400 to +0x63.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ShapeForMountingCode
entries.description: Instantiates one weapon model: reads template[0x22 + mountingCode*2] as an index into the mechwpns chunk table, opens that raw chunk as a memory stream, loads the shape from it, and binds the wpntex atlas at shape+0x26. One fresh copy per mount, because the caller then translates its points and stamps a transform id into it.

entries.name: WeaponModels_LoadShapeChunks
entries.description: Opens dts/mechwpns and reads every top-level chunk (all type 0x140008) raw into malloc'd buffers: DAT_004a9988[i] is the buffer, DAT_004a9a78[i] its length, DAT_004a9b68 the count. Retail ships 56 weapon shapes. They are kept as bytes rather than parsed once because each mount needs its own copy.

entries.name: WeaponModels_FreeShapeChunks
entries.description: Frees the DAT_004a9988 buffers WeaponModels_LoadShapeChunks allocated and nulls each slot.

entries.name: ShapeInstance_CtorCellFrames
entries.description: Two-field shape-instance holder: stores the shape at +0, then allocates +4 as a PRIVATE copy of the shape's per-sequence cell-frame array (shape+0x1c, shape+0x24 entries), or null when the shape carries no sequence. Element 0 of that copy is the cell a TSCellAnimPart draws, which is what lets two mounts carrying the same weapon flash independently.

entries.name: Shape_TranslatePointLists
entries.description: Adds a point offset into a shape's own geometry, recursing on the part-list types and, at a group, marking the points its polys actually reference (poly+6, plus poly+8 entries from the index list at poly+0x0a) and adding the offset to those only. Used to move a freshly-loaded weapon model to its hardpoint's mount point.

entries.name: WeaponMount_HardpointBoneId
entries.description: Returns the mount's .GL record +0, the hardpoint's bone id. The same id WeaponMount_PrepareShot resolves the firing frame from, so the drawn weapon and its shot ride one node.

entries.name: Shape_StampTransformId
entries.description: Writes one transform id into every part of a shape, recursing through the part lists: at a TSGroup/TSBSPGroup (0x140014, 0x14000b) into part+4, and at a TSBSPPart (0x140015) across the whole per-node transform array at +0x1c. Mech_ConfigureLoadout uses it to hang a weapon model on the hardpoint's bone.

entries.name: WeaponMount_Destroy
entries.description: The mount side of weapon-mount destruction, and idempotent -- its whole body sits under a test of the destroyed byte. Clears the weapon model at mount+0x10 and sets mount+0x49, then, for a visibly-mounted hardpoint, spawns the mechwpn2 shape at template+0x26 as debris on a Math_EulerToward bearing. The third argument picks the debris lifetime pair: 0 gives (2, 0x14), anything else (0xff, 0xffff). Ported except the debris.

entries.name: TSBSPPart_RenderNode
entries.description: Walks a TSBSPPart's BSP tree from one node, back-to-front. Nodes are 14 bytes at part+0x18 (int16 normal triple, int32 coeff, front int16, back int16) with a parallel per-node transform id at part+0x1c (-1 = untransformed). A front/back value below zero draws nothing; with bit 0x4000 set it names child (value & 0x3fff) and renders it through vtable +0x1c; otherwise it is another node index. A child no node reaches is never drawn -- the Parts array is a pool the tree indexes, not a draw list.

entries.name: TSDetailPart_Render
entries.description: Detail-level selection. size = (radius << DAT_006c60ac) / max(FastMagnitude3D(viewOffset) - radius, 1); t = Q10Multiply(DAT_004a1034, size); i starts at the STRUCTURE DETAIL bias DAT_004a1038 and advances while details[i] < t; renders parts[min(i - bias, count-1)]. Thresholds are ascending and index-aligned with Parts, so part 0 is the coarsest and the last is the finest; bias 0 is MAXIMUM.

entries.name: FireEffect_LoadResources
entries.description: Loader for the BURNING-OBJECT effect, not the muzzle flash. Reads dts/fire.dts (fire2.dts when CockpitArt_LoadOnDemand is set) into the shape table DAT_006b4fac, allocates the effect pool DAT_006b4fb4 (10 entries) and its free list DAT_006b4fb8, loads the two banks fire0/fire1 (fire0s/fire1s on demand) into DAT_006b4fb0, then reads dat/FIRE.DAT -- a 4-byte header plus one byte per shape -- and points each shape's +0x26 at the bank that byte names. Retail: 4 shapes, banks [0,0,1,1]. Carries the fire.cpp assert string.

entries.name: FireEffect_Ctor
entries.description: Builds one burning-object effect on shape index param_5: copies the owner pointer to +0x4a, the attach point to +0x50, sets the lifetime/priority at +0x59 (5, or 30 when DAT_004a9ed2 != 4) and +0x57 = 0x40. The first live instance starts sound 0x33 and the last stops it (FireEffect_Dtor), counted by DAT_006b4fbc. At detail level 4 only shapes 1 and 3 are built; the others go straight back on the free list.

entries.name: maybe_FireEffect_AcquireSlot
entries.description: Takes a free entry from the effect pool DAT_006b4fb4, or when none is free walks the live ones and returns the one with the lowest +0x59 -- the field FireEffect_Ctor writes its lifetime/priority into. Read as evict-the-least-important; +0x59's exact meaning is not independently confirmed.

entries.name: FireEffect_Dtor
entries.description: Destroys one burning-object effect and decrements DAT_006b4fbc, stopping sound 0x33 when it reaches zero.

entries.name: FireEffect_ReleaseForOwner
entries.description: Walks the effect pool and returns every entry whose owner pointer at +0x4a matches the argument to the free list -- an object's fires going out when it is destroyed.

entries.name: FireEffect_RegisterSubsystem
entries.description: Registers FireEffect_LoadResources as a phase-2 subsystem loader and LAB_0046b084 as phase 5, and nulls the effect pool pointer.

Forwards to SimObject_ApplyRootMotion(obj, obj+0x34, arg) when obj+0x39 is set, and does nothing otherwise. Mech_ConfigureLoadout calls it as (mech, 0) ahead of its per-hardpoint loop. It has NOTHING to do with hardpoint visibility, which it was previously suspected of: the placeholder parts are replaced at draw time by Mech_SpliceHardpointShapes.
entries.name: SimObject_ApplyRootMotionIfEnabled
Mech_Draw
entries.description: Mech vtable +0x00, reached from the ObjList draw-table walk. Runs Mech_SpliceHardpointShapes over every LOD root of the type's shape -- replacing each hardpoint placeholder part with the fitted weapon's shape or a blank record -- and then calls Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel. Gated on DAT_004a9c06.

entries.name: Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel
entries.description: Picks which root of a multi-root shape to draw, per frame, from projected size (radius << DAT_006c60ac / (viewDistance - radius)) against the threshold table at obj+0x41, starting at index min(count-1, DAT_0049736c) and advancing while the size is below the threshold. Installs the transform, calls the shape instance's vtable +0x1c, then restores root 0. A close object therefore draws the root at the bias index.

entries.name: SimObject_InstallModelTransform
entries.description: Builds the object's Q14 euler rotation matrix at obj+0x12 when the dirty flag at obj+0x32 is clear, then installs it as the current model transform. Called twice by Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel, around the LOD pick.

entries.name: Mech_SpliceHardpointShapes
entries.description: Walks a root's hardpoint slot list against the machine's mount array and overwrites each slot: the mount's weapon shape when one is fitted, else the next 0x18-byte blank from typeRec+0xec. The replacement inherits the placeholder's TSBasePart.Transform (+4) and IdNumber (+6). This is why a machine's own .DTS placeholder geometry is never drawn, fitted or not.

entries.name: MechType_BindHardpointSlots
entries.description: Builds one root's hardpoint slot list: for each hardpoint bone id, resolves the shape's vtable +0x24 to the ADDRESS of the part slot holding the part whose TSBasePart.IdNumber is that id, storing null for the -1 the invisible mounting emits. Writes a {void **slots; short count} pair, which MechType_InitOne keeps per LOD root at typeRec+0xe6 with the count at +0xea.
entries.signature: void __cdecl MechType_BindHardpointSlots(void *slotList, void *shapeRoot, short hardpointCount, short *boneIds)

entries.name: GunLayout_CollectHardpointBones
entries.description: Walks a .GL hardpoint list (26-byte records) and writes one short per hardpoint: the record's BoneId when its mounting code at +6 is under 4, else -1. Returns the hardpoint count. The -1 is what keeps the invisible mounting out of the hardpoint splice, which matters because that bone carries real body geometry.

entries.name: WeaponMounts_MountForHardpointSlot
entries.description: Linear search of the mount manager's array for the mount whose .GL record's +0x17 equals the argument, or null. Damage components 19-28 are the mounts, so the caller passes component - 19. The match is on the .GL slot, not on a position in the array.

entries.name: WeaponMount_ConditionChangedBase
entries.description: Base weapon-mount vtable +0x68, the condition notification Mech_ComponentDamageWrite pushes through every mount with its component's reading before and after the write. A reading of 0x100 destroys the mount, with no roll.
entries.signature: void __cdecl WeaponMount_ConditionChangedBase(void *mount, void *mech, int before, int after)

entries.name: WeaponMount_ConditionChanged
entries.description: Vtable +0x68 for the two mount classes that carry a weapon. Runs the base slot, then, while the mount is not empty (+0x7b) and the reading is past 0x80: a Missile mount rolls rand & 0x3ff < 300 for each 25 points crossed and the first success destroys it; a Bullet mount instead sets its refire scale mount+0x63 = 0x400 - steps * 0x66, which makes a damaged gun fire FASTER since WeaponMount_PrepareShot multiplies by it; a Beam mount gets neither.
entries.signature: void __cdecl WeaponMount_ConditionChanged(void *mount, void *mech, int before, int after)

entries.name: maybe_g_ShapeDetailBias
entries.description: The starting index of Shape_DrawAtDetailLevel's LOD-root walk, clamped to the root count. A close object draws exactly this root, so a nonzero value makes root 0 unreachable at any distance. Almost certainly the STRUCTURE DETAIL setting, by analogy with TSDetailPart_Render's identical bias, but its writer was not traced.

entries.name: maybe_Salvage_QueueDestroyedWeapon
entries.description: Appends one int32 to the global list at DAT_004a9ef0, bumping the count at DAT_004a9eee. Its one traced caller is Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage's weapon-mount destruction roll, on the Cybrid branch only, packing the destroyed weapon's catalog id (template+0x56) with its remaining condition. Post-mission salvage is the obvious purpose and is not proven -- the consumer was not traced.

entries.name: LightManager_InitSubsystem
entries.description: Builds the effect light manager singleton DAT_004a968c (0x404 bytes, FUN_00406e44), then overrides the constructor's falloff constants with LightManager_SetFalloffConstants(mgr, 10, 2000) -- the pair that actually reaches every frame, giving A=0 and B=62 after the setter's >>5. Also builds the effect-light handle pool DAT_004a9682.

entries.name: LightManager_Construct
entries.description: Effect light manager constructor: Cpp_VectorNew of 20 slots at +0x6c, stride 0x23, each flagged free with a null light pointer; embeds a light object at +0x328 and zeroes the two free-list counts at +0x35c and +0x3b0. Its own LightManager_SetFalloffConstants(mgr, 2000, 3000) call is dead -- LightManager_InitSubsystem overwrites it immediately.

entries.name: LightManager_SetFalloffConstants
entries.description: Stores the manager's two falloff constants SHIFTED RIGHT BY 5: mgr+0x10 = A = param>>5, mgr+0x14 = B = param>>5. The live call is (10, 2000), so A=0 and B=62 -- not 10 and 2000.

entries.name: LightManager_ClaimSlot
entries.description: Claims the first free effect-light slot for a world point: marks it busy, copies the position, seeds intensity 0xff, copies A/B from the manager, appends the slot to the live array at mgr+0x1c and recomputes the cull radius. Returns the slot index. NO FULL-TABLE GUARD -- with all 20 busy it writes the slot record through the caller's own worldPoint pointer and returns 0x14; see KNOWN_ISSUES.md.

entries.name: LightManager_ReleaseSlot
entries.description: Frees a slot: sets the free flag, swap-removes its pointer from the live array, and recycles its attached light object through LightManager_RecycleLight.

entries.name: LightManager_SetSlotPosition
entries.description: Writes a slot's world position (slot+1/+5/+9). Reached only through EffectLight_SetPosition; nothing in retail moves an effect light.

entries.name: LightManager_SetSlotIntensity
entries.description: Writes a slot's intensity to BOTH +0x0d (int16) and +0x1b (int32) and recomputes the cull radius. The only writer of +0x1b, which is the field every consumer actually reads.

entries.name: LightManager_RecomputeCullRadius
entries.description: slot+0x17 = (slot.intensity * B * 0x20) / 10 + A * 0x20. With A=0 and B=62 that is intensity * 198.4, so a full-intensity light is culled past ~50,592 world units.

entries.name: LightManager_SelectLightsForObject
entries.description: Called once per depth-sorted render entry from ObjList_DrawEntryRender, with the entry's position and its SimObject_GetShapeRadius. Per live slot: cull past slot+0x17; else Math_Atan2Guarded(dist>>5, radius>>5) < 8000 picks a DIRECTIONAL approximation (distance-attenuated intensity, direction rebuilt at length 0x800) and otherwise a POINT light (unattenuated, falloff constants handed to the shade path as light+0x34=0 and light+0x38=1984). Far is directional, near is point -- the helper takes (x, y), so the angle is the object's angular size. See docs/formats/effect-lights.md.

entries.name: LightManager_RecycleLight
entries.description: Unregisters a synthesised light and pushes it back onto the manager's directional (+0x35c) or point (+0x3b0) free list by its type field +0x16.

entries.name: EffectLight_Construct
entries.description: Attaches an effect light: claims a manager slot at the world point, stores the index at handle+0x0c, and sets the slot intensity to the EXPLOS.DAT row's FrameIntensity[0]. Called only by Explosion_Construct, gated on the row's LightMode being nonzero.

entries.name: EffectLight_Destruct
entries.description: Releases the handle's manager slot and optionally frees the handle.

entries.name: EffectLight_SetIntensity
entries.description: Sets the handle's slot intensity. Explosion_TickUpdate calls it with FrameIntensity[frame] & 0xff on each flipbook step.

entries.name: EffectLight_SetPosition
entries.description: Sets the handle's slot position. No retail caller moves an effect light.

entries.name: LightManager_SetCameraPosition
entries.description: Copies the view object's position into mgr+0x00..+0x08 once a frame from maybe_Sim_RenderFrame. Read by nothing on the live path -- its only consumer, FUN_00407284, has zero callers.

entries.name: LightManager_SelectLightsUnconditional
entries.description: Dead: zero callers. A cull-by-fixed-distance variant of LightManager_SelectLightsForObject that always builds a point light, with no directional approximation.

entries.name: Light_Unregister
entries.description: Swap-removes a light pointer from the active light list DAT_006c6130 and decrements DAT_006c612c. The inverse of Light_Register.

entries.name: Light_TransformToModelSpace
entries.description: Transforms a light's world position (+0x04) and direction (+0x10) by the given transform into the model-space copies at +0x22 and +0x2e. Those copies, NOT the world fields, are what Light_ComputeShadeForFace and Light_ComputeShadeForNormal read. Driven per composed node by maybe_Raster_SetModelTransform, gated on DAT_006cbc88.

entries.name: Light_EnableModelSpaceTransform
entries.description: Sets DAT_006cbc88, the gate on the per-node light-to-model-space transform. Called unconditionally by Light_ResetSystem, so it is always on inside a mission.

entries.name: Light_ResetSystem
entries.description: Per-mission light system reset called from Sim_InitMissionSession: clears the ten active light slots, enables the model-space transform, and reinstalls the identity model transform.

entries.name: Light_GetType
entries.description: Returns light+0x16: 0 ambient (never created anywhere in the binary), 1 directional, 2 point.

entries.name: Light_GetIntensity
entries.description: Returns light+0x1a, the light's intensity, set through vtable slot +4.

entries.name: Light_GetModelPosition
entries.description: Returns light+0x22 -- the MODEL-space position Light_TransformToModelSpace writes, not the world-space +0x04.

entries.name: Light_GetModelDirection
entries.description: Returns light+0x2e -- the MODEL-space direction, not the world-space +0x10.

entries.name: Light_GetRangeNumerator
entries.description: Returns light+0x38, the NUMERATOR of the point-light falloff (B * 0x20 = 1984). Easily swapped with Light_GetFalloffOffset (0048d97e), which returns +0x34; the two are adjacent, both int32, and reversing them turns a 1/d falloff into a constant.

entries.name: Light_GetFalloffOffset
entries.description: Returns light+0x34, the DENOMINATOR offset of the point-light falloff (A << 5 = 0). See Light_GetRangeNumerator for why the pair is worth stating explicitly.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_DrawMap
entries.description: Everything inside the command display's map viewport, in order: flood, re-centre on the player plus the pan offset, clamp, terrain raster, the 1200 m grid, the mission border rect, then every marker with the selected pilot's link line and the chosen unit's box.

entries.name: HddMap_DrawTerrain
entries.description: Blits the prebuilt map raster between two projected corners with a rotation, through the currently installed map view projection.

entries.name: HddMap_BuildTerrainRaster
entries.description: Builds the command display map raster once per mission: each height-grid cell becomes palette index min(height,0x7f)/8 + 16, Gouraud-shaded two triangles per cell into an 8-bit bitmap sized to fit the mission box inside 640x400.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_AddObjectMarker
entries.description: One object's map marker: icon from its target class and its group's side byte, size from HddMarker_SetSize, and for the two structure classes the colour and reference size its range falloff draws a box with.

entries.name: HddMarker_Paint
entries.description: Paints one map marker: eight-octant heading frame plus its nudge for a HERC or flyer, a range-scaled box for a structure far from the map centre, and the scanner circle for a radar structure.

entries.name: HddMarker_SetSize
entries.description: Sets a marker gadget's square extent and the half-extent its icon is drawn back by, so the icon lands centred on the object.

entries.name: HddMap_ClampAndInstallView
entries.description: Clamps the map centre so the viewport stays inside the mission box grown by 60000 on every edge, then writes the centre and the scale into the map view projection.

entries.name: HddMap_ToViewport
entries.description: Adds the map viewport origin and half-extent to a projected point.

entries.name: HddMap_FromViewport
entries.description: The inverse of HddMap_ToViewport.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_HitTestMarker
entries.description: Turns a map viewport point into world units and returns the first live object within the marker click radius of it.

entries.name: HddMap_ZoomOut
entries.description: One magnifier step out, up to the scale that fits the whole mission box.

entries.name: HddMap_ZoomIn
entries.description: One magnifier step in, down to a floor of 60000 (8.8 fixed world units per pixel).

entries.name: HddMap_RecomputePanStep
entries.description: Recomputes the arrow pan step from the current zoom: 5000 world units at the closest view rising to 50000 at the widest.

entries.name: HddMap_PanLeft
entries.description: Scrolls the map one pan step toward the mission box's minimum x, or by whatever room is left.

entries.name: HddMap_PanRight
entries.description: The same toward maximum x.

entries.name: HddMap_PanUp
entries.description: The same toward maximum y.

entries.name: HddMap_PanDown
entries.description: The same toward minimum y.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_SelectOrder
entries.description: Arms one of the eight orders, or clears the selection with -1. The four that want a target picked on the map also raise the designate flag and write the matching group 32 prompt into the message row.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_SelectPilot
entries.description: Moves the comm-box selection, dropping whatever order was armed for the previous pilot and setting or clearing all eight order-availability bytes.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_CancelTransmission
entries.description: CANCEL: drops the armed order, the map pick and the pilot selection together.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_SetMessageRow
entries.description: Writes one of STRINGS0 group 32 four prompts - SELECT PILOT, SELECT COMMAND, DESIGNATE LOCATION, DESIGNATE TARGET - into the row above the order list.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_EnableOrders
entries.description: Sets all eight order-availability bytes, which is the whole of what makes the order list live.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_DisableOrders
entries.description: Clears all eight, greying the list back to CPBLUE.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_NextOrder
entries.description: Steps the armed order forward one place, wrapping; returns at once with none armed.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_PreviousOrder
entries.description: The same backwards.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_PickTarget
entries.description: Resolves a map click for an armed order into either an eligible unit or a gridpoint, and marks the transmission ready.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_PickPilot
entries.description: Resolves a map click with no order armed into a squad slot, which is the manual's "select the pilot's marker on the map".

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_Update
entries.description: Vtable slot 1: services a queued map click, advances the half-second blink, re-fonts the order rows whose selection changed, and redraws the map when anything moved it.
